Disaster Risk Management (DRM) Consultant, 21.5 Months, Kathmandu, Office Based with Travel (Open for National Candidates Only) Req#596182
Job no: 596182
Contract type: Consultant
Duty Station: Kathmandu
Level: Consultancy
Location: Nepal
Categories: Emergency
Contract Duration: 21.5 months
Working arrangement: Office Based

UNICEF works in over 190 countries and territories to save children’s lives, defend their rights, and help them fulfill their potential, from early childhood through adolescence.

At UNICEF, we are committed, passionate, and proud of what we do for as long as we are needed. Promoting the rights of every child is not just a job – it is a calling.

UNICEF is a place where careers are built. We offer our staff diverse opportunities for professional and personal development that will help them reinforce a sense of purpose while serving children and communities across the world. We welcome everyone who wants to belong and grow in a diverse and passionate culture, coupled with an attractive compensation and benefits package.

Visit our website to learn more about what we do at UNICEF.

For every child, the right to Safety.

How can you make a difference?

Nepal faces recurrent risks from multiple hazards, including earthquakes, floods, droughts, fires, and landslides.

In partnership with the Government of Nepal, UNICEF supports emergency preparedness, response, and resilience-building efforts to reduce disaster risks and protect vulnerable populations.

UNICEF also works closely with federal, provincial, and local governments to strengthen risk-informed planning and improve the effectiveness of disaster risk reduction (DRR) and emergency preparedness and response (EPR) systems.

Effective coordination, information management, monitoring, reporting, and stakeholder engagement are essential to ensuring quality programme implementation and accountability across all levels of government.

To support the implementation of ongoing DRR and EPR initiatives, including the Strengthening Urban Preparedness, Earthquake Preparedness and Response (SUPER) Project and Anticipatory Action (AA) interventions, UNICEF Nepal Country Office seeks to engage a Disaster Risk Management Consultant.

The consultant will provide technical and coordination support to strengthen the planning, implementation, monitoring, reporting, and knowledge management of UNICEF-supported DRR and EPR programmes.

The role will contribute to improved programme quality, evidence-based decision-making, accountability, and institutional capacity for disaster preparedness and response at federal, provincial, and local levels.

The consultant will also facilitate collaboration with government counterparts, consortium partners, private sectors, civil society organizations, UN agencies, and other stakeholders to promote integrated, multi-sectoral approaches and support the timely achievement of programme objectives and donor commitments.

Overall Deliverables:

The consultant will provide technical leadership and coordination support for the implementation, monitoring, reporting, information management, stakeholder engagement, and knowledge management of UNICEF-supported DRR, EPR, SUPER, and Anticipatory Action initiatives, ensuring timely delivery of high-quality outputs, strengthened partnerships, enhanced accountability, and evidence-based programme implementation across federal, provincial, and local levels.

Scope of Work:

The Disaster Risk Management Consultant will provide technical, coordination, and information management support to strengthen the planning, implementation, monitoring, and reporting of UNICEF-supported Emergency Preparedness and Response (EPR) and Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) programmes, including the SUPER Project, Anticipatory Action (AA) initiatives, and emergency response interventions.

Key responsibilities will include:

  • Strengthen coordination and collaboration with government counterparts at federal, provincial, and local levels, including NDRRMA, MoHA, MoLMCAFAGA, LDTA, and other relevant stakeholders, to support effective implementation of EPR and DRR initiatives.
  • Provide technical and coordination support for the implementation, monitoring, and reporting of EPR, DRR, SUPER, Anticipatory Action, and emergency response programmes to ensure timely achievement of programme results.
  • Facilitate engagement and coordination with consortium partners, UN agencies, private sectors, INGOs, civil society organizations, and other stakeholders to promote integrated and multi-sectoral approaches to disaster risk management.
  • Coordinate closely with UNICEF sections and field offices to strengthen programme coherence, knowledge sharing, and implementation support across project locations.
  •  Lead information management, monitoring, and progress tracking processes, ensuring timely collection, analysis, and reporting of programme results, risks, and implementation challenges.
  •  Support the documentation, packaging, and dissemination of good practices, innovations, lessons learned, and evidence generated through programme implementation.
  •  Analyse and maintain pre-crisis and preparedness-related sectoral information across WASH, Education, Health, Nutrition, Child Protection, and Social Policy to support risk-informed planning and decision-making.
  • Organize and facilitate coordination, review, and consultation meetings with government partners, field offices, and project stakeholders to strengthen collaboration and accountability.
  • Consolidate programme updates, monitoring findings, and results from field offices in Madhesh, Lumbini, Karnali, and Sudurpaschim Provinces to support evidence-based reporting and decision-making.
  • Support capacity strengthening of provincial and local governments, CSOs, and other partners on Emergency Preparedness and Response, Disaster Risk Reduction, Anticipatory Action, and related risk-informed programming approaches.
  • Frequent travel to fields, where UNICEF programme exists (Madhesh, Lumbini, Karnali and Sudurpaschim provinces) and beyond those in case of emergencies, which requires support in coordination and monitoring.

If you would like to know more about this consultancy, please review the complete Terms of Reference here: Download File Terms of Reference TMC0006911.pdf

To qualify as an advocate for every child you will have…

Minimum requirements:

Education:

Master’s degree in Disaster Risk Management (DRM) and related field

Work Experience:

10 years of experience in the field of disaster risk management with focus on urban preparedness and response programme including coordination with different stakeholders covering federal, provincial and local governments.

Sound knowledge on communication, analytical and writing skills.

Working with UN in a consortium mechanism would be added value.

Language Requirements:

English and Nepali

Fluency of local languages from any of four provinces is an asset.

Knowledge/Expertise/Skills:

Federal, provincial and Local government planning cycle, and private sector engagement, risk transfer, anticipatory action, cluster approach and coordination mechanism with multi stakeholders on multi-hazards, especially on earthquake and fire.

Working with vulnerable communities would be added value.

Proficiency in MS Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook) and database management including ICT.

Ability to work independently, take initiative, and deliver timely, high-quality results.

Strong communication, advocacy, and social mobilization skills.

Desirables:

Field level experience, sub-national level planning including working with province and municipalities is must.

Prior coordination experience with multistakeholder platforms at provincial or local government level.

For every Child, you demonstrate…

UNICEF’s Core Values of Care, Respect, Integrity, Trust and Accountability and Sustainability (CRITAS) underpin everything we do and how we do it. Get acquainted with Our Values Charter: UNICEF Values

UNICEF promotes and advocates for the protection of the rights of every child, everywhere, in everything it does and is mandated to support the realization of the rights of every child, including those most disadvantaged, and our global workforce must reflect the diversity of those children. The UNICEF family is committed to include everyone, irrespective of their race/ethnicity, disability, gender identity, sexual orientation, religion, nationality, socio-economic background, minority, or any other status.

Technical Manager, M&E (Nepal)
Location: Kathmandu

The Organization:

Lutheran World Relief, which is part of Corus International, has been present in Nepal since 2013. Corus International is the parent of a family of world-class organizations working to deliver the holistic, lasting solutions needed to end extreme poverty once and for all. We are a global leader in international development, with 150 years of combined experience across our brands. Our nonprofit and for-profit subsidiaries include IMA World Health and its fundraising brand Corus World Health, Lutheran World Relief, CGA Technologies, Ground Up Investing, and Farmers Market Brands. In Nepal, Corus operates under Lutheran World Relief. Our more than 400 employees around the globe are experts in their fields and dedicated to helping the world’s most vulnerable people break the cycle of poverty and lead healthy lives.
At Corus we believe that good only grows stronger and we reflect that belief in our workplace culture. We value every employee’s specialized area of expertise and nurture professional growth. We promote an engaging and supportive work environment, where employees feel enabled and driven to innovate, learn and collaborate. And because our subsidiaries often function as partners, our employees have the opportunity to work across our enterprise family.

Job Brief:

Position Summary: The Technical Manager, Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) will lead the design, implementation, and oversight of the MEL framework for the Takeda Pharmaceutical Company Limited-funded Strengthening warning systems, infrastructure, and health responses for climate-sensitive diseases and disasters “Suswastha (Good Health”) project. This role ensures compliance with Takeda’s Monetary Donation Agreement obligations, including reporting, audit, transparency, and accountability requirements. The M&E Manager will coordinate with technical teams, partners, and affiliates to ensure systematic data collection, analysis, and reporting that demonstrate program impact and accountability. S/he will also ensure that beneficiary stories, program indicators, and evaluation findings are documented and shared in line with Takeda’s standards and Corus International’s learning agenda.

Responsibilities:

Technical Delivery Services, Quality and Impact (60%)

  • Design and manage MEL systems aligned with Takeda’s reporting and audit obligations.
  • Ensure timely submission of mid-year, annual, and final reports, with aggregated and anonymized data.
  • Oversee beneficiary story collection, ensuring compliance with data protection and informed consent requirements.
  • Track progress of program targets and deliverables, identifying issues/challenges that need to be addressed, and ensuring that technical reporting requirements are met in line with
  • Project Management Manual as well as complementary tools, policies, and procedures
  • Support Donation Usage Reviews and audits by preparing documentation and ensuring compliance with Takeda’s Digital CSR Donation Management System.
  • Manage, model and coach colleagues, including sub-recipient staff, in best practices in technical delivery and activities.
  • Participate in forums that enhance sector knowledge to incorporate into technical activities on the project.
  • Work in partnership with project team and sub-recipients, LWR Nepal team, headquarters/regional TBU staff.
  • Provide input into budgeting and forecasting exercises related to technical activities spending within the fiscal year.

Coordination and Collaboration (25%)

  • Based on knowledge of the PBU and project portfolio, provide inputs into interdepartmental efforts such as quarterly portfolio reviews, program implementation and learning exchanges (PILE) and program reviews.
  • Manage documentation of Corus’ technical capacities based on project achievements in coordination with project team and partnership with TBU team.
  • Contribute to the wider work of the TBU through active participation in the achievement of the project deliverables, team meetings, working groups and the development and sharing of technical knowledge and resources.
  • Work closely with program staff, Organization Affiliate (LWR), and Subcontractors to ensure MEL compliance across all activities.
  • Facilitate regular review meetings with partner organizations and stakeholders to discuss program progress and reporting outputs.
  • Coordinate with technical leads to integrate MEL findings into programmatic decision-making.
  • Represent the project in national and international forums, showcasing MEL innovations and program evidence.

Data Management, Documentation, and Reporting (15%)

  • Contribute to the quality data reported into the project reporting system, in collaboration with the MEL team.
  • Prepare high quality, timely technical content, including monthly and/or semi-annual performance reports, and other project documents under the guidance of the Project Director, with support from PBU, headquarters, and TBU, as applicable.
  • Apply knowledge of donor rules and regulations to monitor for technical and MEL compliance for various actions during project start up, implementation, and close out.
  • Ensure data integrity and completeness by maintaining project documentation in electronic databases, as applicable.
  • Develop and maintain databases for program monitoring, ensuring data integrity and security.
  • Prepare high-quality technical reports, dashboards, and donor-required documentation.
  • Ensure compliance with anti-corruption, transparency, and human rights obligations in MEL reporting.
  • Document lessons learned and best practices for dissemination across Corus and Takeda networks.

Supervisory:

This position has no direct reports.

Education & Experience:

  • Bachelor’s with at least 5 years’ experience in Monitoring and Evaluation or equivalent combination of education and experience; Master’s desired.
  • Strong knowledge of MEL frameworks, performance monitoring plans, and donor compliance systems.
  • Familiarity with digital MEL platforms, statistical software, and mobile data collection tools.
  • Experience working with colleagues in a multicultural, multi-linguistic environment.
  • Demonstrated experience managing terms and conditions as well as other international donors.
  • Proven track record of developing and maintaining strong working relationships with host country counterparts and NGO/FBO/CBO actors.
  • Experience working with international partners and or local (NGO/FBO/CBOs, universities and other technical institutions).
  • Demonstrated experience with international donor reporting, audits, and compliance (experience with pharmaceutical or corporate donors preferred).

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:

  • Strong analytical and reporting skills with attention to detail.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills to work with diverse teams and stakeholders.
  • Ability to manage data audits, compliance reviews, and donor reporting requirements.
  • Excellent communication and influencing skills to communicate effectively and credibly, both verbally and in writing in English.
  • Proficiency in Office 365 applications including Word, Excel, SharePoint, and PowerPoint. Experience with Salesforce a plus.
  • Ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a team.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead the coordination of/collaborate on program implementation across multiple teams (between departments, between HQ and country offices, etc.).
  • Commitment to Corus core values, safeguarding, and ethical standards.

Physical and Mental Requirements:

  • The physical requirements that may be needed to execute responsibilities may include bending, standing, and walking, etc.
  • The mental requirements that are essential to satisfactorily executing the responsibilities outlined in this job description include, but not limited to: learning new tasks, comprehending, and retaining information, completing tasks independently, effectively communicating verbally and in writing, demonstrating proficiency in using computer software to perform assigned tasks.

Other Duties:

This job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive list of activities, duties or responsibilities for the position. Duties, responsibilities and activities may change at any time with or without notice. All positions are required to perform any additional tasks assigned by the supervisor. Global positions that are bound by contracts will not be changed without notice and approval.

Working Conditions, Travel and Environment:

  • LWR has an in-person work policy, with all employees reporting to the office Monday through Friday. The employee must be available to work outside normal office hours or on the weekends as required.
  • This position must be able to travel as required for standard domestic and international business purposes. While performing the duties of this job in different locations, the employee may be exposed to precarious settings under high-security risks and/or very basic living conditions and outside weather conditions, as well as to infectious diseases.
  • If applicable, must have authorization to work in the country of assignment.

As a member of the Corus Family, each employee is expected to:

  • Foster a work environment where everyone feels valued and included.
  • Support employees’ evaluation and promotion processes based on skills and performance.
  • Promote a safe, secure, and respectful environment for all members of Corus family, stakeholders in general, and particularly for the communities we serve.
  • Follow Corus Code of Conduct helping to prevent any type of abuse including workplace harassment, sexual abuse and exploitation, and trafficking in persons.
  • Adhere to the Organizational Core Values

Corus International prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type and affords equal employment opportunities to employees and applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, age, national origin, disability status, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by U.S. or International law.

Position Title: Project Manager (Transactional)
Duty Station(s): Nuwakot, Rasuwa
Seniority Level: Mid Level
ICS Level: ICS 10
Contract Type:ICA – LICA – Specialist – Regular
Contract Level: LICA 10
Posting End Date: 05-Nov-2026

Duration

Open-ended subject to organizational requirements, availability of funds and/or satisfactory performance

Job Highlight

Lead impactful projects delivering essential transactional services, ensuring excellence in HR, procurement, and grants management within a dynamic global framework.

About the Region

The Asia Pacific Regional Office, based in Bangkok, Thailand, provides strategic leadership and oversight for UNOPS operations across 17 countries, ensuring high performance, operational excellence, and alignment with organizational goals. Operations currently span Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Cambodia, China, India, Indonesia, Lao PDR, Myanmar, Nepal, Papua New Guinea, Pakistan, the Philippines, Sri Lanka, Thailand, Vietnam, and the Pacific Islands. Across these countries, we work closely with key stakeholders to strengthen partnerships and maximize impact through five main operating units: Afghanistan (AFCO), Myanmar (MMCO), South Asia Multi-Country Office (SAMCO), East Asia and Pacific Multi-Country Office (EAPMCO), and the Asia Regional Health Cluster (ARHC). Through these entities, we provide agile, client-focused service delivery across diverse sectors – including infrastructure, health, procurement, and project management – supporting the implementation of sustainable development solutions across the region.

About the Country/Multi-Country Office

The South Asia Multi-Country Office (SAMCO) supports UNOPS operations across six countries: Bangladesh, India, the Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan, and Sri Lanka. SAMCO delivers a broad range of services and technical expertise in climate change, water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH), infrastructure, procurement, human resource management, and fund management. Each country office is staffed with local technical experts and maintains strong partnerships with national governments, ensuring context-specific solutions and effective project implementation.

About the Project Office

Duty Station: The duty station will be confirmed based on the location of the project and the operational requirements of UNOPS Nepal Office.

Offer and Contract Process: The issuance of an offer and contract will be subject to the signing of the relevant project agreement and the availability of funds.

Role Purpose

The Project Manager (Transactional) is responsible for the effective delivery and daily oversight of projects which provide transactional services, such as HR services, procurement, grants or services, to UNOPS partners. The Project Manager serves as the focal point for coordination with donors, partners and beneficiaries, ensuring alignment with contractual commitments and UNOPS performance standards. Acting on behalf of the Project Board, the Project Manager ensures that project outputs are delivered within agreed tolerances of time, cost, scope, quality, risk, and benefits.

Functions / Key Results Expected

Project Delivery and Performance

  • Develop, complete and update the project implementation plan.
  • Implement the approved plan (including establishment of milestones) within tolerances set by the Project Board.
  • Embed sustainability dimensions, including social and gender considerations, and environmental and economic aspects, into the project life span.
  • Manage the production of required outputs, taking responsibility for overall progress and use of resources while initiating corrective action where necessary.
  • Ensure that quality of work packages and deliverables comply with the quality requirements defined in the implementation plan.
  • Liaise with external suppliers or account managers to ensure quality and timely delivery of outputs.
  • Manage acceptance and delivery of work packages.
  • Monitor project progress, control project variances (if any), and manage changes.
  • Identify, anticipate and advise senior management and the project board on mitigating measures against project risks to ensure that benefits to partners and other stakeholders are maximized.
  • Identify and report potential opportunities for UNOPS to the supervisor.

Procedures

  • Comply with the organization’s policies and standards, and ensure project information is kept updated in project management systems.
  • Be aware of applicable local laws and regulations, and ensure adherence. This includes international regulations and standards, where applicable, as well as technical standards.
  • Prepare and adapt all relevant plans for approval by the project board, and manage baselines
  • Manage the reporting obligations defined in the implementation plan and legal agreements.
  • Maintain project documentation in an orderly manner for accessibility and audit support when needed.
  • Understand and apply the UNOPS financial rules and regulations. Be accountable for the use of delegation of authority (where applicable) and ensure compliance with relevant policies and standards of ethics.
  • Provide a formal handover of the project to the closure manager when applicable.
  • Support project audit activities, including planning, preparation and coordination during audits and follow-up on audit observations/ recommendations.

Monitoring and Reporting

  • Include a results framework and M&E plan in the project implementation plan with clearly defined indicators and agreed targets, ensure regular monitoring and tracking of project results.
  • Prepare and issue regular project and financial reports in accordance with partner and UNOPS requirements for reporting.
  • Regularly review project status and evaluate performance criteria (scope, cost, schedule, and quality)
  • Maintain diaries and progress reports as required by UNOPS standard operating procedures.
  • Provide routine oversight and analysis of delivery data within the dashboard system.
  • Ensure all project team members track and regularly update milestones and targets for the duration of the project life span.

Stakeholder Engagement

  • Develop stakeholder engagement strategies and plans. Actively engage stakeholders, take feedback, and adjust as necessary.
  • Establish solid working relationships with the project board (executive, senior users and senior suppliers); clients; and key stakeholders.
  • Enable formulation of project communication plans and monitor effectiveness of project communications.
  • Coordinate stakeholder engagement and communication, ensuring effective timing and interdependency management of communications. Ensure stakeholders are aware of project activities, progress, and exceptions, and are in a position to accept handover outputs.

Quality Assurance

  • Work with internal stakeholders to ensure projects comply with audit requirements.
  • Work with procurement/ purchasing personnel to ensure effective interface with suppliers’ quality systems.
  • Coordinate quality reviews of project documents and deliverables.
  • Provide quality control for management outputs (e.g. project documents, reports, etc)..

Knowledge Management and Innovation

  • Create a learning environment for the project team, encourage knowledge sharing and training to contribute to longer-term capacity building.
  • Actively interact with other project managers and the wider project management (PM) community, share case studies, lessons learned and best practices.
  • Stay abreast with latest updates and good practices of the profession, participate in training and learning activities for self to advance proficiency and competency.
  • Ensure lessons learned are shared in a timely and appropriate manner.
  • Provide feedback to corporate practice groups on policy and systems, when needed.
  • Provide feedback to functional groups on policies and related guidance to support the continuous improvement of UNOPS policy framework.

Personnel Management

  • Organise and structure the project team, ensure clearly defined roles and responsibilities. Provide regular guidance and direction, as needed, and support the team in effectively performing their tasks.
  • Lead and motivate the project management team, and manage performance.
  • Ensure performance reviews are conducted fairly, accurately, and on time.
  • Select, recruit, and train project teams as required, taking gender parity and diversity objectives into account.
  • Ensure safety and security for all project personnel in compliance with the UN Department of Safety and Security (UNDSS) standards.

Skills

Project Coordination, Project Implementation, Project Planning, Quality Assurance, Reporting, Risk Management, Stakeholder Management

Competencies

Education Requirements

Required

  • Bachelor’s degree (or equivalent) in any discipline with 7 years of relevant experience OR
  • Master’s degree (or equivalent) in any discipline with 5 years of relevant experience is required.

Desired

  • A globally recognized professional certificate (e.g. PRINCE2, PMI, etc) or membership in Project Management is desired.

Experience Requirements

Required

  • Relevant experience is work in project management specific to HR processes or services, financial management, grants management, procurement or related areas.
  • Experience in project coordination and operations management is required
  • Knowledge of relevant quality standards, and assurance methodologies is required

Desired

  • Experience of working in multicultural environments or UN system organizations in a developing country is desired.
  • Experience in development or humanitarian contexts is desired.

Language Requirements

Additional Information

  • UNOPS does not accept unsolicited resumes.
  • UNOPS will at no stage of the recruitment process request candidates to make payments of any kind.
  • Applications to vacancies must be received before midnight Copenhagen time (CET) on the closing date of the announcement. Applications received after the closing date will not be considered.
  • Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted and invited to proceed to the next stage of the selection process, which may include various assessments.
  • UNOPS embraces diversity and is committed to equal employment opportunity. Our workforce consists of a wide range of nationalities, cultures, languages, races, gender identities, sexual orientations, and abilities. We strive to sustain and strengthen this diversity, fostering an inclusive working environment where all personnel are treated with respect and have equal access to opportunities.
  • UNOPS evaluates all applications based on the skills, qualifications and experience outlined in the vacancy announcement. We are committed to a fair and transparent selection process and welcome diverse perspectives, including those of women, indigenous and racialized communities, individuals of diverse gender identities and sexual orientations, and persons with disabilities.
  • We are committed to enabling all candidates to perform at their best during the assessment process. If you are shortlisted and require support or reasonable accommodation to complete any assessment, please inform our human resources team upon receiving your invitation.
  • UNOPS has zero tolerance for sexual exploitation and abuse (SEA), sexual harassment, and other forms of abusive conduct, including discrimination, abuse of authority, and harassment. To uphold these standards, background checks are conducted for all final candidates to help ensure that individuals with a history of such conduct are not hired. Job Highlight

Lead impactful infrastructure projects, transforming communities and driving sustainable development.

About the Region

The Asia Pacific Regional Office, based in Bangkok, Thailand, provides strategic leadership and oversight for UNOPS operations across 17 countries, ensuring high performance, operational excellence, and alignment with organizational goals. Operations currently span Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Cambodia, China, India, Indonesia, Lao PDR, Myanmar, Nepal, Papua New Guinea, Pakistan, the Philippines, Sri Lanka, Thailand, Vietnam, and the Pacific Islands. Across these countries, we work closely with key stakeholders to strengthen partnerships and maximize impact through five main operating units: Afghanistan (AFCO), Myanmar (MMCO), South Asia Multi-Country Office (SAMCO), East Asia and Pacific Multi-Country Office (EAPMCO), and the Asia Regional Health Cluster (ARHC). Through these entities, we provide agile, client-focused service delivery across diverse sectors – including infrastructure, health, procurement, and project management – supporting the implementation of sustainable development solutions across the region.

About the Country/Multi-Country Office

The South Asia Multi-Country Office (SAMCO) supports UNOPS operations across six countries: Bangladesh, India, the Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan, and Sri Lanka. SAMCO delivers a broad range of services and technical expertise in climate change, water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH), infrastructure, procurement, human resource management, and fund management. Each country office is staffed with local technical experts and maintains strong partnerships with national governments, ensuring context-specific solutions and effective project implementation.

About the Project Office

Duty Station: The duty station will be confirmed based on the location of the project and the operational requirements of UNOPS Nepal Office.

Offer and Contract Process: The issuance of an offer and contract will be subject to the signing of the relevant project agreement and the availability of funds.

Role Purpose

The Project Manager (Infrastructure) is responsible for the effective delivery and day-to-day management of infrastructure projects, which may involve the construction of physical assets, technical outputs, or both. These projects span a range of sectors, including (but not limited to) education, health, transportation, irrigation, and port infrastructure. The Project Manager serves as the focal point for coordination with donors, partners and beneficiaries, ensuring alignment with contractual commitments and UNOPS performance standards. Acting on behalf of the Project Board, the Project Manager ensures that project outputs are delivered within agreed tolerances of time, cost, scope, quality, risk, and benefits.

Functions / Key Results Expected

Project Delivery and Performance

  • Develop, complete and update the project implementation plan.
  • Implement the approved plan (including establishment of milestones) within tolerances set by the Project Board, including the development of infrastructure designs and coordinating design reviews.
  • Embed sustainability dimensions, including social and gender considerations, and environmental and economic aspects, into the project life span.
  • Manage the production of required outputs, taking responsibility for overall progress and use of resources while initiating corrective action where necessary.
  • Ensure that quality of work packages and deliverables comply with the quality requirements defined in the implementation plan.
  • Liaise with external suppliers or account managers to ensure quality and timely delivery of outputs.Manage acceptance and delivery of work packages.
  • Monitor project progress, control project variances (if any), and manage changes.
  • Identify, anticipate and advise senior management and the project board on mitigating measures against project risks to ensure that benefits to partners and other stakeholders are maximized.
  • Identify and report potential opportunities for UNOPS to the supervisor.

Procedures

  • Comply with the organization’s policies and standards, and ensure project information is kept updated in project management systems.
  • Be aware of applicable local laws and regulations, and ensure adherence. This includes international regulations and standards, where applicable, as well as technical standards.
  • Prepare and adapt all relevant plans for approval by the project board, and manage baselines
  • Manage the reporting obligations defined in the implementation plan and legal agreements.
  • Maintain project documentation in an orderly manner for accessibility and audit support when needed.
  • Understand and apply the UNOPS financial rules and regulations. Be accountable for the use of delegation of authority (where applicable) and ensure compliance with relevant policies and standards of ethics.
  • Provide a formal handover of the project to the closure manager when applicable.
  • Support project audit activities, including planning, preparation and coordination during audits and follow-up on audit observations/ recommendations.

Monitoring and Reporting

  • Include a results framework and M&E plan in the project implementation plan with clearly defined indicators and agreed targets, ensure regular monitoring and tracking of project results.
  • Prepare and issue regular project and financial reports in accordance with partner and UNOPS requirements for reporting.
  • Regularly review project status and evaluate performance criteria (scope, cost, schedule, and quality)
  • Maintain diaries and progress reports as required by UNOPS standard operating procedures.
  • Provide routine oversight and analysis of delivery data within the dashboard system.
  • Ensure all project team members track and regularly update milestones and targets for the duration of the project life span.

Stakeholder Engagement

  • Develop stakeholder engagement strategies and plans. Actively engage stakeholders, take feedback, and adjust as necessary.
  • Establish solid working relationships with the project board (executive, senior users and senior suppliers); clients; and key stakeholders.
  • Enable formulation of project communication plans and monitor effectiveness of project communications.
  • Coordinate stakeholder engagement and communication, ensuring effective timing and interdependency management of communications. Ensure stakeholders are aware of project activities, progress, and exceptions, and are in a position to accept handover outputs.

Quality Assurance

  • Work with internal stakeholders to ensure projects comply with audit requirements.
  • Work with procurement/ purchasing personnel to ensure effective interface with suppliers’ quality systems.
  • Coordinate quality reviews of project documents and deliverables.
  • Provide quality control for management outputs (e.g. project documents, reports, etc))

Knowledge Management and Innovation

  • Create a learning environment for the project team, encourage knowledge sharing and training to contribute to longer-term capacity building.
  • Actively interact with other project managers and the wider project management (PM) community, share case studies, lessons learned and best practices.
  • Stay abreast with latest updates and good practices of the profession, participate in training and learning activities for self to advance proficiency and competency.
  • Ensure lessons learned are shared in a timely and appropriate manner.
  • Provide feedback to corporate practice groups on policy and systems, when needed.
  • Provide feedback to functional groups on policies and related guidance to support the continuous improvement of UNOPS policy framework.

Personnel Management

  • Organise and structure the project team, ensure clearly defined roles and responsibilities. Provide regular guidance and direction, as needed, and support the team in effectively performing their tasks.
  • Lead and motivate the project management team, and manage performance.
  • Ensure performance reviews are conducted fairly, accurately, and on time.
  • Select, recruit, and train project teams as required, taking gender parity and diversity objectives into account.
  • Ensure safety and security for all project personnel in compliance with the UN Department of Safety and Security (UNDSS) standards.

Contractors, Engineering Design, Project Control, Project Planning, Stakeholder Management, Project Resource Management, Project Team Management

ABOUT WFP

The World Food Programme (WFP) is the leading humanitarian organization saving lives and changing lives, delivering food assistance in emergencies and working with communities to improve food security, nutrition, resilience and sustainable development.

ORGANIZATIONAL CONTEXT:

The position is based in the Supply Chain Delivery function of the WFP Nepal Country Office and reports to the Deputy Country Director or designate.

WFP Nepal is responding to current emergency and early-recovery requirements while maintaining a longer-term focus on country capacity strengthening. The position therefore operates across the emergency preparedness, response, recovery and systems-strengthening continuum. It combines operational supply chain delivery with technical assistance to national and sub-national institutions, including support for Humanitarian Staging Areas, market systems and cash-based transfer activities.

The job holder is expected to anchor a substantive, multidisciplinary portfolio; provide high-quality technical and managerial advice; and maintain the operational readiness required to scale up rapidly when an emergency occurs.

JOB PURPOSE:

To manage and provide specialist leadership for integrated supply chain activities that meet immediate emergency response and recovery requirements while strengthening sustainable national systems for future preparedness and response.

The job holder will plan and oversee supply chain delivery across procurement, logistics, transport, warehousing, inventory management and service provision; manage emergency preparedness and response activities and Humanitarian Staging Areas; support market-based and cash-based interventions; and lead institutional and country capacity strengthening initiatives with government, humanitarian, development and private-sector partners.

TERMS AND CONDITION

Position Title: Head of Supply Chain
Contract Type: Regular Consultant
Level: II
Contract Duration: 11 months (Extendable)

KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES (not all-inclusive, within delegated authority)

1. Strategy and integrated delivery: Lead the planning, implementation and monitoring of integrated supply chain delivery activities supporting emergency response, early recovery, resilience and Country Strategic Plan priorities, ensuring coherence across logistics, procurement, programme and partnership workstreams.

2. Context analysis and solution design: Analyse the operational context, supply chain risks, market conditions and evolving needs; design agile, cost-effective and sustainable end-to-end supply chain solutions; and recommend timely adjustments to management.

3. Emergency response and recovery: Provide technical and operational leadership during emergencies and post-emergency recovery, including rapid assessments, response planning, scale-up and transition arrangements, while ensuring continuity of critical supply chain services.

4. Emergency preparedness: Lead supply chain preparedness activities, including contingency planning, scenario analysis, readiness assessments, operational concepts, standard operating procedures, framework arrangements, pre-positioning strategies, simulations and lessons learned.

5. Supply chain operations management: Plan and oversee procurement, contracting, transport, warehousing, inventory, distribution and service-delivery activities, ensuring quality, timeliness, cost-efficiency, risk mitigation, internal controls and compliance with WFP policies and standards.

6. Humanitarian Staging Areas: Provide strategic and operational oversight of Humanitarian Staging Areas and related preparedness assets, ensuring effective governance, safe and compliant operations, accurate inventory management, readiness for activation and sustainable institutional arrangements.

7. Country capacity strengthening: Design and implement country capacity strengthening initiatives in supply chain and emergency preparedness and response, based on jointly identified institutional needs, national priorities and sustainable transition pathways.

8. Institutional technical assistance: Advise government institutions and other national actors on supply chain strategies, policies, systems, organisational arrangements, business processes, operational plans, standards and performance frameworks at federal, provincial and local levels.

9. CBT and market development: Provide supply chain and market expertise to cash-based transfer and market-development activities, including market and retailer assessments, supply chain network mapping, bottleneck analysis, local procurement options, value-chain linkages and measures to improve market access, functionality and resilience.

10. Partnerships and coordination: Build and maintain productive partnerships with government entities, UN agencies, NGOs, development partners, academia, financial and retail actors, suppliers, transporters and other private-sector service providers to achieve common preparedness, response and systems-strengthening objectives.

11. Service provision: Develop and manage responsive supply chain services for government and humanitarian and development partners, ensuring clear service arrangements, transparent costing, reliable delivery, performance monitoring and protection of WFP’s interests.

12. Performance, risk and innovation: Establish performance indicators, monitor implementation and expenditure, identify operational and institutional risks, recommend corrective action, and drive continuous improvement through data, technology, innovation and evidence-based learning.

13. Resource mobilisation: Contribute technical content to concept notes, project documents, budgets, funding proposals, donor briefings and reporting, and support engagement with partners to mobilise resources for emergency response, recovery, preparedness and capacity strengthening.

14. Team leadership: Lead, coach and develop staff and project teams; promote integrated planning, accountability, inclusion, knowledge sharing and high performance; and strengthen the technical capacity of WFP colleagues and partners.

15. Representation: Represent WFP in relevant supply chain, logistics, emergency preparedness and response, market systems and institutional coordination forums, as delegated, and communicate complex operational and strategic issues clearly to senior stakeholders.

16. Other: Perform other duties as required.

Education:

Advanced University degree in Supply Chain Management, Logistics, Engineering, Economics, Business Administration, Emergency Management, International Development or another relevant field, or a First University degree with additional years of related professional experience and/or training.

Experience:

Minimum of 6 years of progressively responsible professional experience in supply chain management, logistics, procurement, emergency preparedness and response, humanitarian operations, country capacity strengthening, market systems or related fields. Experience managing substantive projects, teams or operational portfolios in complex environments is required.

Knowledge & Skills:

Strong knowledge of integrated supply chain planning and operations; emergency preparedness, response and recovery; procurement and logistics processes; warehousing and inventory management; market assessment and CBT support; institutional capacity strengthening; project management; performance and risk management; partnership development; and clear communication with senior internal and external stakeholders.

For every child, the right to Education

Position: National Director – WV Nepal
Location: Lalitpur, Nepal
End Date: November 13, 2026

With 75 years of experience, our focus is on helping the most vulnerable children overcome poverty and experience fullness of life. We help children of all backgrounds, even in the most dangerous places, inspired by our Christian faith.

Come join our 31,000+ staff working in nearly 100 countries and share the joy of transforming vulnerable children’s life stories!

Employee Contract Type: International Assignment (WVI – Paid via GCLA) Fixed Term (Fixed Term)

Job Description:

The National Director (ND) of World Vision International (WVI) Nepal has overall responsibility for the strategic leadership and operational effectiveness of World Vision’s programmes in Nepal. Our 2026-2030 Country Strategy aims to deliver results for the well-being of one million children especially the most vulnerable. It focuses on integrated livelihoods & nutrition, inclusive & quality education, child protection & participation, humanitarian response, disaster resilience, strengthening partnerships, gender equality, disability and social inclusion, in an environment that is increasingly vulnerable to climate change.

You will be expected to lead the office in pursuing these strategic goals, being an effective leader locally, a responsible member of the WVI Partnership, ensuring WVI Nepal’s consistent focus on WVI’s Our Promise strategy to maximise impact – well-being of the most vulnerable children, families and communities, while adapting WVI standards to the changing context in Nepal.

You will be deeply comfortable with collaborating with other WVI offices and divisions internally to achieve shared child well-being objectives, and externally with the Government of Nepal, local NGO partners, civil society organisations (CSOs), development partners, local community leaders and the private sector.

The ND models a high standard of personal Christian leadership, ministry, and integrity, leading by examples through lifestyle and work relationships, and providing spiritual guidance to staff on the organization’s Vision, Mission and Core Values.

Your Key Responsibilities will include:

Delivering on Child Well-being Aspirations / Results, Outcomes and Targets, including but not limited to:

  • Delivering improved outcomes for children in line with the WVI Nepal Country Strategy 2026-2030 and the SHIELD integrated program framework
    Providing strategic oversight and leadership to ensure impactful program implementation through local partner Non-Government Organizations (PNGOs), including strengthening of partnerships through implementation of the Partners of Choice Action Plan.
  • Preparing for and implementing rapid and effective responses to major emergencies affecting children, including having an up to date preparedness plan and Business Continuity Plan (BCP), and building relationships with key humanitarian and development actors.
  • Creating enabling environment to champion innovative programming, process and systems.

Leading effective external engagement and strategic partnerships for child well-being, locally and internationally, including but not limited to:

  • Defining strategic partnership objectives with Government of Nepal at all levels, district level partner NGOs, CSOs, Development Partners, Local Community Leaders including inter-faith leaders, and Private Sector (including Media) to achieve shared child well-being objectives.
  • Building partnerships and relationships with key decision makers, including strategic national partners to leverage advocacy for shared child well-being objectives.
  • Coaching Senior Leadership Team (SLT) and external-facing Senior Managers to pro-actively and constructively engage with external partners in influencing programs and policy development and implementation on child rights issues through multiple development, advocacy and humanitarian forums (i.e. Technical Working Groups of Association of INGOs in Nepal/ AIN, Provincial Partner Coordination Meeting, Humanitarian
  • Cluster, Joining Forces alliance and Development Partners Coordination).
  • Acting as a Twin Citizen ensuring that National Office participate in global processes and decisions and allocates resources and talent where most needed, share and apply relevant good practices.
  • Build reputation of WVI Nepal with Government as a leading child focused organization, mitigating risks associated with our Christian identity.

Achieving Operational and Stewardship Excellence and Optimal Yield to Ministry, including but not limited to:

  • Ensuring functioning project management information system and other support systems so that all programs are managed on time, on budget and on targets, in achieving the desired impact on child well-being.
  • Ensuring program quality through rigorous program management cycle (design, implementation, monitoring, evaluation, learning) and effective execution of community accountability system and PNGOs capacity strengthening.
  • Ensuring effective stewardship and accountability of WVI Nepal resources, finances and people, consistent with performance standards established by WVI.
  • Implementing fit-for-purpose and adaptive organization and cost structure and systems/process supportive for effective field implementation and organizational efficiency
  • Promoting and modelling high level of transparency, integrity and zero tolerance to fraud
  • Ensuring pro-active enterprise risks identification, mitigation and review in collaboration with Risk Prime and Risk Committee.
  • Ensuring organizational compliance to relevant Government directives and laws and WVI Bylaws.
  • Ensuring dialogue with Global and Regional Office for potential future implementation of shared support services in the region tailored to Nepal’s context of program implementation via partners.

Increasing and Diversify Funding Portfolio, including but not limited to:

  • Ensuring that business development plans, cross-function collaboration system, decision making process, and the necessary staffing are in place to maintain, diversify and grow the funding base for the country programs, supports the donor engagement plan as needed, liaising pro-actively and extensively with funding offices, as well as the bilateral and multilateral donor communities.
  • Facilitating effective consortium and partnership formation with key partners
  • Ensuring high level quality checks and compliance with relevant WVI, government, and donors.
  • Building funding diversity through active exploration of new funding modalities, including climate based funding.

Enabling thriving and inclusive organisational culture and building high performing teams

  • Serving as a role model and lead as example on servant leadership, aspired organization cultures and WVI core values
  • Building a culture of workplace diversity and inclusion, including appropriate gender and ethnicity diversity across all levels of staff, and appropriate implementation of WVI core values in respect to our Christian identity in the multi faith context of Nepal
  • Ensuring effective performance management implementation & fit-for-purpose capacity building programs for all staff are in place and delivered

title.rendered: Project Coordinator, MEAL Officer, Admin and Finance Officer, Field Supervisor, UDAAN Facilitator

content.rendered:
Prerana, a national-level NGO established in 1998, is committed to promoting and protecting the rights of women, people with disabilities, economically disadvantaged groups, adolescent girls, and other marginalized communities. The organisation currently operates across Madhesh and Bagmati Provinces of Nepal in collaboration with national and international NGOs, as well as local, provincial, and federal governments and other key stakeholders.

Prerana, in partnership with CARE Nepal, is implementing the “UDAAN: Amplifying Girls’ Aspirations” Project in Sarlahi District, Madhesh Province. The project aims to improve access to quality education for out-of-school adolescent girls by addressing the social, economic, and other barriers that prevent them from enrolling in, continuing, and completing their education. Through accelerated learning opportunities, community engagement, and adolescent empowerment initiatives, the project seeks to create a supportive and inclusive learning environment that enables girls to continue their education, strengthen their confidence, pursue their aspirations, and realise their full potential.

To ensure the effective implementation of the project, Prerana invites applications from qualified, experienced, self-motivated, and result-oriented Nepali citizens for the following positions based in Sarlahi District. The selected candidates will play a key role in supporting efforts to increase access to education for out-of-school adolescent girls and contribute to the overall success of the UDAAN: Amplifying Girls’ Education project.

title.rendered: Project Coordinator, Finance Officer, Technical Supervisor (Civil Overseer), Social Mobilizers

content.rendered:
Community and Rural Development Society Nepal (CARDSN), Nuwakot is a non-governmental organization established in 2054 BS with the purpose to support and empower the most vulnerable, poor, and underprivileged population through sustainable interventions for children, youth, and women.
CARDSN with the support of Lutheran World Relief implement “Nepal Flood Emergency Response and Reconstruction Support Project” in Gosaikunda Rural Municipality-Rasuwa and Belkotgadi Municipality-Nuwakot. The project leverages expertise in water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH), shelter and Livelihood.
In this connection, CARDSN invites applications from eligible and qualified candidates for the following positions under the “Nepal Flood Emergency Response and Reconstruction Support Project” who meet the specified criteria.

Positions:

1. Project Coordinator – 1
2. Finance Officer -1
3. Technical Supervisor (Civil Overseer)-1
4. Social Mobilizers -2

1. Project Coordinator (80% field based)

  • Number required: 1
  • Duty station: Rauwa and Nuwakot
  • Reports to: Executive Director
  • Contract Period: 1 Nov 2026 to 30 Sep 2027

Duties/Responsibilities

  • Prepare and update annual, quarterly, monthly and weekly work plans with project staff and stakeholders.
  • Lead implementation of livelihood recovery, reconstruction and WASH activities against approved targets and timelines.
  • Monitor project progress against the logframe, indicators, budget and implementation schedule, identify issues and take corrective action.
  • Provide guidance to the Overseer and other project staff, conduct team meetings, field visits and performance reviews.
  • Prepare budget forecasts and monitor expenditure with the finance and administration team; ensure transparent use of resources.
  • Coordinate with municipalities, rural municipalities, ward offices, government line agencies, community groups and development partners.
  • Monitor outputs and outcomes; ensure transparent beneficiary selection, records, accessible feedback mechanisms and use of community feedback.
  • Prepare timely narrative, progress and donor reports, with evidence, lessons learned and supporting documentation.
  • Ensure compliance with safeguarding, prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse, anti-fraud, procurement and organizational policies.

Minimum qualifications and experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in Development Studies, Social Sciences, Civil Engineering, Agriculture, Public Health, Rural Development or a related field; a master’s degree is an advantage.
  • At least 3–5 years of relevant project implementation or coordination experience in the NGO/INGO sector.
  • Experience in livelihoods, disaster recovery, reconstruction, WASH or integrated community development.
  • Experience in team supervision, work planning, budget monitoring, stakeholder coordination and reporting.
  • Good written and spoken Nepali and English; knowledge of the local language is an advantage.
  • Good computer skills, including MS Word and Excel and willingness to travel frequently to project communities.
  • Must hold a valid two-wheeler driving license.

Key competencies Leadership, accountability, planning, problem-solving, communication, teamwork, conflict management, inclusion and commitment to safeguarding.

2. Finance Officer (20% field based)

  • Number of Positions: 1
  • Duty Station: Nuwakot
  • Reports To: Project Coordinator /Executive Director
  • Contract Duration: 1 Nov 2026 to 30 Sep 2027

Duties/ Responsibilities

  • Maintain accurate and up-to-date books of accounts, ledgers, cashbooks, bank records, vouchers, and supporting documents in accordance with CARDSN procedures and applicable accounting standards.
  • Check payment requests, invoices, bills, purchase orders, contracts, attendance records, and other supporting documents for completeness, accuracy and proper authorization before processing.
  • Record project transactions in the accounting system and ensure expenses are charged to the correct project, budget line and accounting code.
  • Ensure that all financial transactions are supported by appropriate documentation and approved by authorized personnel.
  • Maintain proper records of cash advances, staff advances, vendor payments, and settlements in accordance with organizational policy.
  • Monitor project budget utilization and prepare budget-versus-actual reports.
  • Ensure that project expenditure is consistent with the approved budget, donor agreement and organizational financial procedures.
  • Maintain an updated record of budget utilization and expenditure against each approved budget heading.
  • Ensure timely bank deposits and payment processing in accordance with approved financial procedures.
  • Maintain proper records of tax invoices, withholding certificates, payroll documents, and other statutory financial documents.
  • Support internal and external audits, donor financial reviews and compliance checks.
  • Must hold a valid two-wheeler driving license.

Minimum Qualifications and Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, Management, or a related field. A relevant professional accounting qualification is an advantage.
  • At least 2–3 years of relevant experience in accounting or financial management, preferably with an NGO/INGO or donor-funded project.
  • Knowledge of bookkeeping, bank reconciliation, budget monitoring, payment documentation, financial reporting and audit preparation.
  • Good working knowledge of MS Excel and accounting software.
  • Experience in NGO financial management and donor financial reporting is an advantage.
  • Understanding of applicable Nepal tax and statutory compliance requirements relevant to the position.
  • Good communication and coordination skills.
  • Must hold a valid two-wheeler driving license.

Key Competencies Integrity and professional ethics, Accuracy and attention to detail, Confidentiality and accountability, Financial analysis and problem-solving, Time management and organization, Communication and teamwork, Compliance with organizational policies.

3. Technical Supervisor- Civil Overseer (80% field Based)

  • Number required: 1
  • Duty station: Nuwakot and Rasuwa
  • Reports to: Project Coordinator
  • Contract: 1 Nov 2026 to 30 Sep 2027

Duties/Responsibilities

  • Conduct field surveys and assess the technical feasibility of proposed infrastructure.
  • Assist with technical drawings, cost estimates, bills of quantities (BoQs), material specifications and construction schedules..
  • Monitor progress, workmanship, material quality and technical specifications; identify defects and recommend corrective measures.
  • Maintain site diaries, measurement books, progress photographs and construction records.
  • Support implementation of water supply systems, sanitation facilities, drainage, handwashing facilities and other approved WASH infrastructure.
  • Coordinate water quality testing with authorized laboratories or competent service providers when required.
  • Ensure accessibility, gender, child-safety, environmental and disaster-resilient considerations are incorporated where applicable.
  • Verify quantities and quality of materials; maintain records of material use and report discrepancies, delays and cost risks.
  • Coordinate with the local government technical sections, user committees and community representatives.
  • Monitor site safety, use of personal protective equipment and measures to reduce environmental and community risks.

Minimum qualifications and experience

  • Diploma in Civil Engineering or an equivalent recognized qualification relevant to the role.
  • At least 2–3 years of relevant experience in construction supervision, rural infrastructure, reconstruction or WASH projects.
  • Practical skills in site surveying, preparing estimates and BoQs, reading technical drawings and supervising construction.
  • Knowledge of construction quality control, occupational safety and disaster-resilient infrastructure.
  • Familiarity with AutoCAD and MS Excel is an advantage; ability to prepare technical reports and travel to field sites is required.
  • Must hold a valid two-wheeler driving license.

Key competencies Technical accuracy, attention to detail, quality assurance, field supervision, problem-solving, recordkeeping and occupational safety awareness.

4. Social Mobilizer (80% field Visit)

  • Number of Positions: 2 (50% women)
  • Duty Station: Rasuwa And Nuwakot
  • Reports To: Project Coordinator
  • Contract Duration: 1 Nov 2026 to 30 Sep 2027

Duties/Responsibilities

  • Conduct household visits, community consultations, group discussions, and participatory assessments to identify community needs, priorities and barriers to participation.
  • Explain project objectives, eligibility criteria, assistance packages, selection processes, timelines and feedback and complaints channels in clear and accessible language.
  • Support transparent beneficiary identification and verification according to approved project criteria.
  • Mobilize community members for livelihood training, skills development, income-generating activities, reconstruction support, WASH awareness and other approved project activities.
  • Facilitate community meetings, orientations, training sessions, awareness campaigns and other field activities.
  • Collect information on beneficiary participation and livelihood activities and report findings to the Project Coordinator.
  • Support community awareness of safe construction practices and the importance of maintaining completed infrastructure.
  • Conduct community awareness activities on safe drinking water, sanitation, personal hygiene, handwashing and environmental cleanliness.
  • Promote menstrual hygiene awareness where appropriate to the project and community context.
  • Collect and submit accurate field data, attendance sheets, beneficiary records, household visit records and activity reports.

Minimum Qualifications and Experience

  • At least Grade 12 / +2 or equivalent. A diploma or bachelor’s degree in Social Sciences, Development Studies, Agriculture, Public Health, or a related field is an advantage.
  • At least 1–2 years of relevant experience in community mobilization, social development, livelihoods, WASH, reconstruction or similar field-based work.
  • Previous experience working with rural communities or local development projects is an advantage.
  • Good communication and facilitation skills in Nepali and the local language used in the project communities.
  • Ability to maintain records, prepare simple reports and use a smartphone or basic digital data-collection tools.
  • Ability and willingness to work regularly in communities and travel within assigned wards.
  • Good interpersonal skills and the ability to work effectively with diverse community groups.
  • Commitment to inclusion, accountability and safeguarding.
  • A valid two-wheeler driving licence and access to a two-wheeler for regular field visits are mandatory.
  • Candidates must be residents of the Rasuwa or Nuwakot districts

Key Competencies Community engagement and mobilization, Respectful communication and facilitation, Inclusion and gender sensitivity, Accurate recordkeeping and reporting, Teamwork and coordination, Problem-solving and accountability, Commitment to safeguarding and community participation.

Please visit the Job Description (LINK) for minimum educational, professional qualification and competencies required.

Preference will be given to local candidates, women and individual from marginalized communities.

Working for Access and Creation Nepal (WAC Nepal) is nonprofit, non-government and nonpolitical humanitarian development organization has been going to implement the project named “Empowered communities and CSOs for inclusive nutrition governance in the hilly and mountain regions of Western Nepal” (Better Nutrition Project) to strengthen a sustainable and inclusive nutrition governance for an effective and efficient implementation of the Multi-Sector Nutrition Plan (MSNP III, 2023 – 2030) with the consortium of Local Initiatives for Biodiversity, Research and Development (LI-BIRD) and Welthungerhilfe (WHH) in Chaurpati Rural Municipality, Sanfebagar Municipality, Mellekh Rural Municipality, Bannigadi Jayagadh Rural Municipality and Mangelsen Municipality of Achham District. WAC Nepal is seeking qualified, dynamic and motivated Nepali citizens on the following positions for smooth implementation of the project.

Position: District Coordinator

1 Person (Based on Sanfebagar)

Minimum Qualification and Experience: Master’s degree in public health, Nursing or other relevant fields, with 3 years of relevant work experience in Nutrition Sector.

Major Responsibility:

  • Provide technical support in planning, implementation, monitoring, and quality assurance of nutrition project activities in coordination with the Program Manager.
  • Lead the district-level nutrition component, including capacity building of local governments, child growth monitoring, NERP camps, LANN+ activities, and nutrition education for FCHVs and targeted communities.
  • Provide technical guidance and support to the project team for effective implementation of nutrition interventions.
  • Ensure coordination and integration of nutrition, agriculture, and WASH interventions in project areas.
  •  Develop context-specific strategies to reach underserved, vulnerable, and marginalized communities to prevent and reduce malnutrition.
  •  Support government health facilities in nutritional assessment of children under five and the identification, referral, and management of children with acute malnutrition.
  •  Provide technical assistance to local governments in implementing MSNP III and nutrition-friendly local governance activities.
  •  Strengthen the capacity of local government officials, health workers, FCHVs, and community groups on nutrition-related issues.

Required Languages: English and Nepali

The duty station is Rasuwa, Nepal.

Background

The Humanitarian Affairs Officer, UNOCHA, position is established to support the humanitarian response to the floods affecting Rasuwa and surrounding disaster-affected areas of Nepal. The position is intended to reinforce UN field-level coordination during the immediate response period, working closely with government authorities, UN agencies, NGOs, humanitarian partners, and affected communities.  Under the direct supervision of the RCO/OCHA Bidur Hub lead and the overall supervision of the Resident Coordinator’s Office Nepal and the Head of OCHA’s Regional Office for Asia and the Pacific (ROAP), the incumbent will work in close collaboration with the UN Resident Coordinator, Government and relief/recovery partners to support the formulation of strategies of engagement in support of the mandate of OCHA at both managerial and operational levels.

The Humanitarian Affairs Officer will provide on-site humanitarian coordination in flood-affected areas, with a particular focus in Rasuwa and Nuwakot. The incumbent will help ensure that operational agencies and local authorities have a common understanding of priority needs, response activities, constraints and gaps, and that field-level issues requiring attention are communicated promptly to relevant coordination and decision-making structures. The role is operational and field-facing and requires regular travel to affected communities and response locations. The incumbent will also be responsible for providing advice and support to the Resident/Humanitarian Coordinator and operational partners to consider the priorities of the most vulnerable communities in humanitarian and early recovery planning.

Duties and Responsibilities

1.) Ensures effective humanitarian coordination at field level in support of national authorities

  • Provide a visible and sustained OCHA /RCO coordination presence in Rasuwa and other designated flood-affected areas.
  • Facilitate and support field coordination meetings with local authorities, UN agencies, NGOs, Red Cross/Red Crescent actors and other operational partners.
  • Promote complementarity among responders, identify duplication and gaps, and support practical follow-up on agreed coordination actions.
  • Maintain regular liaison with affected communities and relevant local structures so priority concerns can inform coordination discussions.
  • Support field partners to steer a collective approach to Accountability to Affected People (AAP). This means joint community consultations, harmonized messaging in local languages, and shared feedback and complaint mechanisms, whose findings inform response planning and are followed up with communities. Work with the PSEA Network and agency focal points so that these channels are safe and accessible for reporting sexual exploitation and abuse, and that survivor-centred referral pathways are in place and known to communities and responders.

2.) Monitoring, assessment and analysis of humanitarian needs

  • Monitor humanitarian conditions, priority needs, access constraints, emerging risks and response coverage through regular field visits and engagement with partners.
  • Support or participate in inter-agency rapid assessments and field missions as required.
  • Consolidate field observations and partner inputs into concise situation updates, analysis and recommendations for OCHA and humanitarian leadership.
  • Flag critical gaps, underserved locations and operational bottlenecks requiring coordinated action.

3.) Support to operational response and emergency preparedness

  • Promote timely coordination around immediate life-saving priorities and evolving operational requirements following the floods.
  • Support contingency and preparedness discussions where continuing rainfall, landslides, access disruption or other hazards may affect communities or response operations.
  • Encourage partners to integrate relevant humanitarian policies and principles, protection considerations, accountability to affected people and inclusion in field-level response planning.

4.) Information sharing, reporting and coordination support

  • Maintain regular information exchange between responders in affected areas and coordination structures at national and regional levels.
  • Support partners to engage women, persons with disabilities, older persons and marginalized groups in response decisions, using safe and inclusive channels that also serve as entry points for PSEA reporting and referral.
  • Track how community feedback is acted upon across partners, and flag recurring concerns, including SEA risks, to coordination forums and the PSEA Network so the response can adjust.
  • Prepare meeting records, action points, field updates, briefing notes and inputs to humanitarian reporting products.
  • Support mapping of operational presence, needs and response gaps in collaboration with information management colleagues and partners.
  • Track agreed actions and follow up with responsible partners to support timely implementation

5)  Partnership, advocacy and enabling humanitarian access

  • Build constructive working relationships with local and district authorities, humanitarian organizations, civil society and community representatives.
  • Identify operational or coordination issues that may impede assistance and elevate them through appropriate channels.
  • Provide field evidence and analysis to support advocacy on priority humanitarian needs, equitable assistance and effective response coverage.

Work implies frequent interaction with the following:
Staff at all levels within RCO/OCHA Bidur Hub, UN RCO Nepal and Regional Offfice for Asia and the Pacific . Representatives of Nepal National Disaster Management Organizations, other UN agencies and other organizations that work on disaster risk managemet and related issues.
Results Expected: 
Provides sound analytical inputs and advice that contributes to improving institutional capacity and articulates  humanitarian response to the Nepal 2026 Flash Flood with a special focus in Rasuwa. Provides timely delivery of assigned tasks, maintains partnerships and interacts effectively with colleagues internally and externally.

Core Competencies

    LEVEL 3: Set and align challenging, achievable objectives for multiple projects, have lasting impact

Introduction

People in Need (PIN) is a non-governmental, non-profit, international organisation founded in the Czech Republic in 1992. PIN arrived in Nepal as part of a humanitarian response to the April 25, 2015 earthquake. Since its inception in Nepal, PIN has had a strong role advocating and addressing the needs of marginalised populations. This includes people who live in geographically remote areas of Nepal, people who are from historically marginalised ethnic groups, and those marginalised because of their age and/or gender identity (women and girls). PIN has also supported Nepal’s post-earthquake reconstruction efforts, ensuring that the most vulnerable people are not left behind with resilience (focused on shelter and resettlement) and inclusive education programming. PIN-Nepal is strongly committed to safeguarding children and vulnerable adults, including persons with disabilities, in line with its safeguarding framework and child protection policy. The Information Management Officer will support the Project Manager/Humanitarian Manager in ensuring the timely, quality and accountable delivery of data management to flood-affected communities in Rasuwa.

The position will provide technical support to the DAO–Rasuwa, as well as coordination and programme support throughout the response and recovery process. Key responsibilities will include conducting needs assessments, supporting activity planning from recovery through reconstruction, engaging with relevant stakeholders, monitoring programme activities, documenting progress and lessons learned, preparing reports, and coordinating closely with humanitarian stakeholders and relevant government authorities.

The post holder will ensure that activities are implemented in accordance with organisational policies, donor requirements, humanitarian principles, and relevant technical and quality standards.

Scope of Work

The Information Management Technical Officer, under the supervision of the Programme Manager, will be seconded to the DAO – Rasuwa to provide technical support for the development and management of information systems related to geohazard assessment, recovery, and reconstruction. This role involves coordinating with DAO, NDRRMA, Province authorities, local authorities, and system development agencies to update and share municipal response to recovery data with the shelter and other relevant clusters. The Officer will also lead the creation of information products such as reports, maps, infographics, and national-level outputs like situation reports and bulletins, ensuring their effective dissemination. Additionally, the role includes maintaining and updating relevant content on websites, facilitating strong communication and information-sharing mechanisms among stakeholders, and delivering capacity-building support to Local, government agencies and partners for effective data access and analysis.
