UPSHIFT is UNICEF’s flagship programme for transferable skills and social entrepreneurship. Drawing on best practices from non-formal education, experiential learning, and business education, it creates a comprehensive learning journey comprised of workshops, mentorship, and entrepreneurial challenges. The programme is deeply rooted in Human Centered Design (HCD) principles and empowers young people to identify and analyze problems within their communities and develop products or services to address them.
Since its launch in 2014, UPSHIFT has expanded to 59 countries, graduating 7 million young people who have completed over 200 million hours of learning. To achieve sustainable scale, the programme focuses on integrating into formal education systems and utilizing digital platforms for blended learning delivery. The primary blended delivery model, UPSHIFT Powered by Unisolve, was built from the grounds up to support UPSHIFT delivery in schools and has successfully graduated over 2 million secondary school students to date. To accelerate the scaling of this digital model, the UPSHIFT Global team has ported the Unisolve-based learning journey to Google Classroom providing a faster, cost-effective platform and has started to integrate Al into the adaptation, deployment and running of the programme inclusing the development of teacher focused tools access and utilize the learning journey at a much lower cost.

  • Knowledge Management & Communications – Organise key documents, meeting notes, learnings and project information, and support the preparation of presentations, briefing notes, dashboards and other materials for internal and external stakeholders.
  • Support to the UPSHIFT transition – Include consolidating the digital portfolio, country activities, existing assets, implementation documentation and outstanding commitments into a structured handover package for the Education team.
  • Process Improvement & Automation – Identify repetitive and time-consuming activities and explore opportunities to streamline, automate or improve workflows using digital and Al tools, while supporting priority projects and emerging strategic initiatives.

Introduction

People in Need (PIN) is a non-governmental, non-profit, international organisation founded in the Czech Republic in 1992. Since its inception in Nepal, PIN has had a strong role in designing and facilitating systemic solutions, advocating for and addressing the needs of vulnerable populations affected by disasters, including people who live in geographically remote areas of the country, historically marginalised ethnic groups, and those marginalised because of their age and/or gender identity. Scope of Work

The Reporting and Knowledge Management Coordinator will support high-quality reporting and knowledge management across the Bhotekoshi Flood Response and the RAIN Programme, working closely with programme managers, field teams and technical staff to consolidate information and produce clear, evidence-based reports and knowledge products.

The person will work under the guidance of, and provide direct support to, the programme managers and teams whose work they report on, while liaising with a wide range of colleagues across reporting, MEAL, communications and field-level functions.

The post holder will be based in Kathmandu and will split their time between the Bhotekoshi Flood Response and the RAIN Programme, as required.

All PIN staff agree to:

  • Comply with all relevant PIN policies, Country Program Policies, and guidelines related to their position.
  • Show a strong commitment to the inclusion of all groups within Nepal and dedication to PIN Nepal’s Inclusion Guidelines.
  • Perform and accurately complete administrative tasks related to their position.
  • Strive for quality in all aspects of their work and ensure the highest quality performance of the Country Program.
  • Maintain a positive attitude and promote a professional & productive working environment across all staff, departments, and among all of PIN’s partners.
  • Adhere to PIN Code of Conduct and key policies including Anti-Corruption Policy, Child Protection Policy and Safeguarding Policy.

About the Programmes

People in Need (PIN) Nepal implements a portfolio of programmes and emergency responses, including the ongoing Bhotekoshi Flood Response and the RAIN Programme, a longer-term programme addressing climate resilience and disaster risk reduction. Consistent, high-quality reporting and knowledge management across this portfolio are essential to demonstrate impact, meet donor requirements, and inform future programming.

Key Summary of Functions

The Reporting and Knowledge Management Coordinator will support the preparation of reports and the consolidation of programme knowledge across the Bhotekoshi Flood Response and the RAIN Programme, working with data and inputs from field teams to produce clear, well-structured and presentable reporting and knowledge outputs for a range of internal and external audiences.

Reporting Support

  • Support the preparation of quarterly reports, donor reports, year-end reports and other periodic reporting requirements across the Bhotekoshi Flood Response and the RAIN Programme.
  • Support the Humanitarian Manager with development of the Situation Report and 5W matrix. and other relevant reporting.
  • Draft, compile and format narrative and summary reports in line with donor and organisational requirements and timelines.
  • Work with programme and response teams to gather accurate, evidence-based content for reports.
  • Support consistency, quality and clarity of reporting outputs across different teams, sites and programmes.
  • Track reporting schedules and deadlines and support relevant teams to meet them.

Knowledge Management and Documentation

  • Consolidate good practices and case studies from across the Bhotekoshi Flood Response and the RAIN Programme.
  • Develop briefs and summaries that capture key results, challenges and recommendations from field implementation.
  • Support systematic documentation of programme and response experiences for internal reflection and external sharing.
  • In coordination with the Communication and Advocacy team, ensure regular publication of knowledge briefs to showcase the programme visibility via different media channels as relevant.

Data Analysis and Knowledge Product Development

  • Work with raw programme and response data, both quantitative and qualitative, to extract key findings for reports and knowledge products.
  • Analyse and synthesise information from multiple sources into clear, accurate and well-structured written content.
  • Develop comprehensive, well-presented reports and summaries suitable for a range of audiences, including donors, senior management and communications/media.
  • Support the development of visually engaging and accessible reporting and knowledge materials, in coordination with communications colleagues where relevant.

Field and Team Liaison

  • Liaise regularly with field teams, enumerators, project and programme staff, and colleagues working in reporting, MEAL and communications roles across the Bhotekoshi Flood Response and the RAIN Programme.
  • Coordinate with programme managers and technical staff to gather inputs, data and updates required for reports and knowledge products.
  • Support coordination between the Bhotekoshi Flood Response and the RAIN Programme to encourage consistent reporting practices across programmes.

Support to Programme Managers

  • Provide day-to-day reporting and documentation support to the programme managers and teams whose work they report on.
  • Assist programme managers in preparing donor updates, internal briefings and other reporting requirements as needed.
  • Help programme managers follow up on task completions and retrieve data and inputs from programme and field teams, in a timely manner.
  • Support the Consortium Manager and programme managers with ad hoc reporting and documentation tasks as required.
  • Provide any other administrative and documentation support to the programme managers and the Consortium Manager, as required.

Compliance

  • Ensure reporting and knowledge outputs reflect PIN’s safeguarding, PSEA, Child Safeguarding and Code of Conduct commitments where relevant.
  • Handle programme and beneficiary data responsibly and in line with organisational data protection standards.
  • Report any concerns regarding data accuracy, misuse, or compliance issues through appropriate channels.

Requirements

Education

  • Bachelor’s degree in development studies, social sciences, communications, or a related field. A Master’s degree is an advantage.

Relevant Experience

  • Minimum 4 years of relevant experience in reporting, monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning (MEAL), or programme documentation, ideally within the development or humanitarian sector.
  • Experience preparing donor reports, quarterly reports, or similar periodic reporting products.
  • Experience working with field-based teams and consolidating inputs from multiple sources.
  • Experience developing case studies or similar knowledge products is an advantage.

Desired Knowledge, Skills and Competencies

  • Excellent written and verbal articulation skills in English; Nepali language skills an advantage.
  • Strong analytical skills, with the ability to work with raw quantitative and qualitative data and translate it into clear findings.
  • Excellent report-writing, editing and document formatting skills, with strong attention to detail.
  • Ability to produce comprehensive, well-organised and visually presentable reports and knowledge materials for varied audiences, including donors and media.
  • Good knowledge of MS Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint); familiarity with data visualisation or design tools is an advantage.
  • Strong coordination and interpersonal skills, with the ability to liaise effectively with field teams, enumerators and colleagues across different functions and programmes.
  • Ability to manage multiple deadlines and work efficiently across more than one programme at a time.
  • Familiarity with donor reporting formats and requirements (e.g., FCDO or similar) is an advantage.

Blind Youth Association Nepal (BYAN) is a national, youth-led, rights-based organization dedicated to promoting the rights, leadership, and meaningful participation of children and young persons with disabilities in Nepal. BYAN works to advance inclusive development by strengthening the capacity and leadership of children and young persons with disabilities, while advocating for inclusive policies and systems at local, provincial, and national levels. The organization’s key thematic areas include inclusive education, youth leadership and civic engagement, disability rights advocacy, sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR), climate change and disability inclusion, accessibility and assistive technology, and research and evidence-based advocacy. Through partnerships with government agencies, civil society organizations, and development partners, BYAN works to ensure that persons with disabilities are actively included in development processes and decision-making platforms.

BYAN is implementing a three-year project titled “YATRA” – Youth-Led Actions for Transformation through Rights-Based Advocacy and Disability Movement in partnership with CBM Global Disability Inclusion. The project is being implemented in the Bagmati Province and Madhesh Province, with a particular focus on Bara District, Rautahat District, Sarlahi District, Dhanusha District, Mahottari District, Chitwan District, and Kathmandu. The project primarily focuses on strengthening the organizational and leadership capacity of grassroots Organizations of Persons with Disabilities (OPDs), particularly youth-led and youth-focused OPDs, to sustain and lead the disability movement at the local level. YATRA adopts a comprehensive approach that includes capacity strengthening, youth leadership development, data and evidence generation, policy advocacy, and movement building to advance disability rights and inclusive governance. The project emphasizes enhancing youth participation within the disability movement while also promoting disability inclusion within the broader youth movement, enabling young persons with disabilities to actively contribute to advocacy processes and influence policies, plans, and programs that affect their lives.

Details/requirements:

Organization: Blind Youth Association Nepal (BYAN)
Position: Capacity Strengthening and Knowledge Management Officer
Number of Position: 1
Location: Simara, Bara, Madhesh Province
Salary: Negotiable
Duration: Three Years

Position Overview

The Blind Youth Association Nepal (BYAN) is seeking a dynamic and motivated Capacity Strengthening and Knowledge Management Officer to support initiatives aimed at strengthening the organizational capacity of Organizations of Persons with Disabilities (OPDs) and enhancing learning and knowledge management within the project. The position will coordinate capacity development initiatives, facilitate trainings and learning events, and document best practices and lessons learned to strengthen institutional learning.
The Officer will also support Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability, and Learning (MEAL) functions by contributing to data collection, monitoring project progress, and promoting evidence-based decision-making and advocacy. The role will serve as a key link between field-level implementation and project management, working closely with Inclusion Facilitators and the Project Coordinator to ensure effective coordination, information flow, and quality implementation of project activities.

Key Responsibilities:

Organizational Development and Capacity Strengthening

  • Support the organizational strengthening of local Organizations of Persons with Disabilities (OPDs), particularly youth-led and grassroots OPDs, to enhance their governance, leadership, and program management capacities.
  • Facilitate organizational development (OD), advocacy, leadership, and related capacity-building trainings for OPDs and project partners.
  •  Provide mentoring and technical guidance to Inclusion Facilitators and OPD leaders to strengthen their skills in documentation, planning, advocacy, and inclusive practices.
  • Support under-represented and marginalized OPDs, including those led by women and youth with disabilities, to conduct self-advocacy and rights-awareness trainings within their communities.
  •  Promote cross-learning, peer exchange, and collaboration among OPDs to strengthen the disability movement at the local level.
  •  Engage with relevant stakeholders, including local governments, civil society organizations, and networks, to promote disability inclusion and strengthen partnerships for advocacy and capacity development.
  •  Coordinate closely with project teams and Inclusion Facilitators to enhance field-level skills and ensure quality implementation of project activities.

MEAL and Knowledge Management

  •  Support the implementation of the project’s Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability, and Learning (MEAL) framework to track activities, outputs, and outcomes.
  •  Develop and maintain systems for data collection, documentation, and analysis to monitor project progress and support evidence-based learning.
  • Document best practices, lessons learned, case studies, and success stories to capture project experiences and strengthen knowledge sharing.
  •  Compile narrative reports, progress updates, and other learning products to support internal and donor reporting.
  • Conduct periodic monitoring visits and coordinate with field teams to ensure the quality and effectiveness of project activities.
  • Maintain and update project databases, monitoring tools, and knowledge management systems.
  •  Contribute to strengthening learning, accountability, and evidence-based advocacy within the project.

Qualifications and Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in Social Sciences, Development Studies, Gender Studies, Disability Studies, or a related field (Master’s degree preferred).
  • Minimum three years of relevant experience in MEAL, knowledge management, organizational development, or project implementation in the development or NGO sector.
  •  Demonstrated experience in facilitating trainings, workshops, and mentoring programs for organizations and communities.
  • Experience in stakeholder engagement, partnership building, and advocacy initiatives, including local governments, networks, or civil society organizations.
  •  Strong understanding of disability rights, inclusion, and youth engagement.
  • Experience in data collection, monitoring, evaluation, and knowledge management systems, including report writing and documentation of lessons learned and good practices.
  • Experience in developing learning products such as case studies, success stories, or briefs is desirable.
  • Ability to coordinate with field teams, manage multiple tasks, and work in a dynamic environment.
  • Excellent facilitation and communication skills in English and Nepali. (Communication skill in local language will be an additional advantage)
  • Strong analytical, documentation, and report-writing skills.
  • Ability to mentor and support field staff and partners.
  •  Proficiency in Microsoft Office, Excel, and data management tools.
  •  Strong interpersonal skills and capacity to work collaboratively with diverse stakeholders.
  •  Commitment to rights-based and inclusive approaches, particularly for persons with disabilities and under-represented groups.

How to Apply

Interested candidates are requested to submit their CV and cover letter along with expected salary to hr@byanepal.org by 27 Oct 2026.

Please mention the subject line:

“Application for the Post of Capacity Strengthening and Knowledge Management Officer.”

BYAN is an equal opportunity employer and promotes inclusion across gender, caste, ethnicity, Dalit, and disability. Persons with disabilities and LGBTIQ+ individuals are strongly encouraged to apply. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted for further processes. The organization reserves the right to reject any or all applications without assigning any reason.

Position: Exam Coordinator

Application Expiry Date: 2026-11-17

The Exam Coordinator plans, conducts, and manages all examinations of the college, both internal and those run by Tribhuvan University. The role ensures every exam is fair, secure, on schedule, and fully compliant with TU rules, the Office of the Controller of Examinations (OCE), and the relevant Dean’s Office.

The Exam Coordinator is the single point of contact between the college, students, faculty, and TU for all examination matters, from registration and admit cards to results, records, and grievances. As QAA Assistant, the role also supports the college’s Internal Quality Assurance Committee (IQAC) in meeting the Quality Assurance and Accreditation (QAA) standards of the University Grants Commission (UGC), Nepal. This covers data collection, documentation, the Self Study Report (SSR), stakeholder feedback, and readiness for the Peer Review Visit (PRV).

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

A. Internal Examinations

  •  Prepare the annual internal exam calendar (unit tests, midterm/terminal, pre-board, re- exams and practical exams) in line with the academic calendar and TU schedule.
  • Collect question papers from faculty on time and check them against the TU syllabus, marks distribution, and blueprint.
  •  Maintain strict confidentiality in setting, moderation, printing, storage, and distribution of question papers.
  •  Prepare seat plans, invigilation duty rosters and room allocation for every exam.
  •  Brief invigilators on rules and conduct, and monitor exam halls to prevent malpractice.
  •  Coordinate timely evaluation of answer sheets and collect marks from faculty within set deadlines.
  •  Compile, verify, and publish internal results, and share performance reports with the Campus Chief and Program Coordinators. Organise retests and makeup exams for eligible students as per college policy.

B. Tribhuvan University Examinations

  •  Track all TU notices on exam forms, fees, schedules, routines and results, and circulate them to students and staff promptly.
  •  Manage student exam form filling, eligibility checks (attendance, internal marks, fee clearance), and submission to TU within deadlines.
  • Prepare and submit internal assessment and practical marks to TU in the required format and portal.
  • Collect and distribute admit cards, and resolve any errors in name, symbol number, or subjects with TU.
  • Coordinate with TU when the college serves as an exam centre: centre setup, seating,
    question paper custody, answer sheet packing and dispatch.
  •  Coordinate with external examiners for practical, viva, and project or thesis defense exams.
  • Handle retotalling, rechecking, partial and chance exam applications on behalf of students.
  •  Collect and distribute transcripts, mark sheets, provisional certificates and other TU documents.

C. Results, Records and Data

  •  Maintain accurate, secure records of all internal and TU exam results, both digital and physical.
  • Prepare result analysis by program, semester and subject to support academic improvement.
  • Keep records of exam fees, forms submitted, admit cards issued, and documents received from TU.
  •  Archive question papers, answer sheets and mark ledgers as per retention policy.

D. Coordination and Communication

  •  Act as the main link between the college, TU, faculty, students and parents on exam matters.
  • Hold exam briefing meetings with faculty and staff before every exam cycle.
  •  Communicate exam schedules, rules and results clearly through notice boards, website, email and student groups.
  •  Address student queries and grievances related to exams and resolve them fairly and quickly.

E. Compliance, Integrity and Improvement

  •  Enforce exam rules and codes of conduct, and report malpractice cases to the Exam Committee and TU as required.
  • Serve as Member Secretary of the college Examination Committee and keep its minutes.
  • Ensure readiness of exam halls, furniture, lighting, CCTV, stationery, and labs for practicals.
  •  Prepare exam-related reports for internal audits, QAA and accreditation processes.
  •  Propose improvements to exam processes, including digital tools for results and records.
  •  Perform any other exam-related duties assigned by the immediate supervisor.

F. Quality Assurance and Accreditation (QAA Assistant)

  •  Assist the IQAC Coordinator in planning and running all QAA activities as per UGC Nepal QAA guidelines.
  • Collect, verify, and organize data and evidence for the Self Study Report (SSR) under each UGC criterion.
  • Maintain an organized evidence file system, both digital and physical, for every QAA criterion.
  •  Prepare the Annual Quality Assurance Report and other periodic reports for the IQAC and UGC.
  • Run feedback surveys from students, faculty, alumni, parents, and employers, and compile the analysis.
  •  Support tracer studies of graduates and maintain alumni employment and further study data.
  •  Keep records of academic results, pass rates, faculty profiles, research, training, seminars, and community activities.
  • Update institutional data in UGC EMIS and other reporting systems on time.
  •  Track action plans from QAA recommendations and report progress to the IQAC.
  •  Link exam results and analysis with QAA reporting to show academic quality and improvement.

KEY REQUIREMENTS

  • Qualification: Minimum bachelor’s degree in any discipline from a recognized university (Education, Management, or a related field preferred).
  •  Experience: Minimum 2 years of experience in exam management or academic administration at a college affiliated with Tribhuvan University. Freshers can also apply.
  •  Strong organizational and planning skills, with the ability to handle several exam cycles at once.
  • High integrity and discretion in handling confidential papers and data.
  •  Good computer skills: MS Excel, MS Word, email, and online university portals; familiarity with college management or result systems is a plus.
  • Clear written and spoken communication in Nepali and English.
  •  Attention to detail and accuracy with marks, records, and deadlines.
  •  Ability to work calmly under pressure and resolve student issues fairly.
  • Team leadership to guide invigilators and exam support staff.
  • Good report writing, data analysis, and documentation skills.

WHY JOIN US?

  •  Salary considered among the best in the education industry.
  • Covered in Social Security Fund (SSF).
  • Festival Allowances for all staff.
  • Paid holidays, covering sick leave and institute-calendar holidays, including Winter Holidays.
  • For new mothers, paid maternity leave, day care facility with nominal rates, lactation break.
  •  Paternity Leave for New Fathers.
  •  Staff discount on child education and eligible relatives’ education.
  • Office Uniform.
  •  Refreshments at United Coffee Club at subsidized rates and discounts on United Aiselu Farm (UAF) products.
  •  Lunch facility for staff at the campus canteen.
  • Easy loan access through United Education Cooperatives.
  •  Staff development program with coaching, mentoring and training opportunities.
  •  Length of service reward for long-term, dedicated staff.
  •  Company events including picnics, sports meets and festive celebrations.
  • Employee referral scheme.

We are committed to building an inclusive, growth-oriented, and dynamic workplace where contributions are valued, and potential is nurtured. If you are ready to be part of a purpose-driven team, we’d love to hear from you.

Position: Trainee-Administrative and Logistics

Description

WORKSITE LOCATION: Kathmandu with field visits as and when required.

LENGTH OF TRAINEESHIP: Six Months

ABOUT PROSPER GLOBAL

Prosper Global is a leading global organization powered by the belief that a better world is possible. In disaster, in hardship, in more than 40 countries around the world, we partner to put bold solutions into action — helping people triumph over adversity and build stronger communities from within. Now, and for the future. Prosper Global has been operating in Nepal since 2005, implementing programs in food security, agriculture, market development, financial services, girl’s education, climate change adaptation and disaster risk reduction. We take a systems-based approach in our programming, with the aim of improving the lives and potential of vulnerable individuals and communities across Nepal.

GENERAL POSITION SUMMARY

The Trainee – Administrative and Logistics support position is a structured learning opportunity designed to build professional skills in day-to-day program operations, logistics management, and financial coordination. This role offers dual benefit: the trainee gains hands-on experience in administrative and operational backbone of humanitarian and development programs, while the organization benefits from the trainee’s proactive support in ensuring the smooth implementation of activities and operational management. While mentorship is provided, the trainee is expected to take initiative, manage their learning journey effectively, and maintain full accountability for the documentation, procurement workflows, and event coordination tasks they oversee.

LEARNING AREAS AND KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

1. Procurement, Logistics and Financial Compliance

  • Procurement Systems (ProSource): Develop practical skills in using ProSource to create, process, track, and manage Purchase Requisitions (PRs), Purchase Orders (POs), and related procurement transactions.
  • Procurement Planning and Processes: Understand procurement procedures, including preparation of RFQs, collection and evaluation of quotations, price negotiation, supplier selection, procurement recommendations, and purchase order processing.
  • Vendor and Supplier Management: Develop skills in supplier communication, quotation follow-up, sample review, price negotiation, delivery coordination, and supplier performance monitoring.
  • Logistics and Inventory Management: Coordinate the transportation, receipt, storage, distribution, and tracking of goods and equipment while maintaining accurate inventory records.
  • Asset and Fleet Management: Understand procedures for asset tracking, equipment handover, vehicle maintenance, fuel monitoring, transportation arrangements, and proper maintenance of supporting records.
  • Goods and Services Receipt Verification: Verify delivered goods and completed services against approved specifications, quantities, purchase orders, and delivery schedules before confirming receipt.
  • Financial Processing and Payment Management: Understand the payment process, including expense settlements, vendor payment requests, invoice verification, receipt confirmation, and review of supporting documentation.
  • Procurement and Financial Compliance: Understand and apply Prosper Global’s procurement, logistics, and finance policies, procedures, approval workflows, and internal controls to ensure transparency, accountability, and compliance.
  • Documentation and Audit Readiness: Develop skills in maintaining complete and accurate procurement files, quotations, evaluation records, purchase orders, invoices, receipts, asset records, and other supporting documents for audit purposes.
  • Procurement and Payment Pipeline Tracking: Monitor procurement requests, pending approvals, purchase orders, deliveries, goods receipts, and vendor payments to ensure timely processing and follow-up.
  • Coordination and Communication: Strengthen coordination with program, procurement, finance, administration, logistics, and suppliers to ensure timely delivery of goods and services and smooth implementation of activities.
  • Reporting and Record Management: Maintain procurement trackers, inventory registers, asset records, logistics reports, and payment status updates accurately and systematically.
  • Risk Management and Problem-Solving: Identify potential procurement, logistics, and financial compliance issues, resolve discrepancies, and seek appropriate guidance to minimize operational and financial risks.
  • Continuous Improvement: Apply feedback, strengthen technical knowledge, and improve accuracy, efficiency, and accountability in procurement, logistics, and financial compliance activities.

2. Interdepartmental Coordination and Communication

  • Stakeholder Liaison: Learning how to effectively communicate and bridge the gap between field teams and headquarters to provide routine updates.
  • Cross-Functional Synergy: Understanding the interdependent relationship between Program, Operations, and Finance teams and learning how to facilitate the smooth flow of information between them.
  • Professional Networking: Building the interpersonal skills necessary to coordinate with diverse teams and external vendors.

ACCOUNTABILITY

Reports Directly to: Administrative and Logistics Officer

Works Directly with: Operations and Finance Team members

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS AND SKILLS

  • Strong willingness to learn, and professional growth.
  • Fresh graduates who have completed a bachelor’s degree or master’s degree in management, development Studies, or any other relevant fields within last two years.
  • Good written and spoken English and Nepali to handle professional documentation and meeting minutes.
  • Good communication skills and interpersonal skills.
  • Basic computer skills (MS Word, MS Excel, MS PowerPoint).
  • Previous experience in a formal office setting, internship, or volunteer work within an NGO is advantageous.
  • Experience with or a quick ability to learn digital procurement or financial management systems is advantageous.
  • Basic understanding of livelihood, food security, climate change, DRR, resilience, and humanitarian actions are an advantage.
  • Attention to detail and organizational skills.
  • Preference will be given to female, persons with disabilities and applicants from the marginalized communities.

SUCCESS FACTORS

Success in this role is defined by a proactive learning mindset and the initiative to turn on-the-job opportunities into professional growth within a dynamic development and humanitarian context. A successful trainee will transition from assisted tasks to the independent management of assignments, bringing creative ideas to knowledge management and communication while remaining strictly accountable for the quality of their results. By demonstrating resilience, cultural sensitivity, and a commitment to planned professional development, you will help spark innovative ways to share information and contribute to the overall success of high-quality, collaborative programming.

The most successful Prosper Global team members have a strong commitment to teamwork and accountability, thrive in evolving and changing environments and make effective written and verbal communication a priority in all situations. Prosper Global Team members represent the agency both during and outside of work hours when deployed in a field posting or on a visit/short-term assignment to a field posting. Team members are expected to conduct themselves in a professional manner and respect local laws, customs and MC’s policies, procedures, and values at all times and in all in-country venues.

ONGOING LEARNING

In support of our belief that learning organizations are more effective, efficient and relevant to the communities we serve, we empower all team members to dedicate 5% of their time to learning activities that further their personal and/or professional growth and development.

TEAM ENGAGEMENT AND EFFECTIVENESS

Achieving our mission starts with how we build our team and collaborate. By bringing together individuals with a variety of experiences, backgrounds, and perspectives, we strengthen our ability to solve complex challenges and drive innovation. We foster a culture of trust and respect, where every team member is valued for their contributions, empowered to reach their full potential, and motivated to do their best work.

We recognize that building a strong and effective team is an ongoing process, and we remain committed to learning, improving, and growing together.

EQUAL EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITY

Prosper Global is an equal opportunity employer committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all employees and qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, sex, sexual orientation, religion or belief, national origin, age, disability, marital status, veteran status, or any other characteristics protected under applicable law.

SAFEGUARDING AND ETHICS

Prosper Global is committed to ensuring that all individuals we come into contact with through our work, whether team members, community members, program participants or others, are treated with respect and dignity. We are committed to the core principles regarding prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse laid out by the UN Secretary General and IASC and have signed on to the The Misconduct Disclosure Scheme We will not tolerate child abuse, sexual exploitation, abuse, or harassment by or of our team members. As part of our commitment to a safe and inclusive work environment, team members are expected to conduct themselves in a professional manner, respect local laws and customs, and to adhere to Prosper Global Code of Conduct Policies and values at all times. Team members must complete mandatory Code of Conduct eLearning courses upon hire and annually.

As an applicant, if you witness or experience any form of sexual misconduct during the recruitment process, please report this to Prosper Global Integrity Hotline (integrityhotline@prosperglobal.org).

The MEL Trainee position is a structured learning opportunity for a recent graduate or early-career professional who wants to build practical skills in monitoring, evaluation, accountability, and learning within development and humanitarian programming. Working under the guidance of the MEL team and in coordination with program colleagues, the trainee will support data collection, data management, data quality checks, analysis, reporting, and learning activities. The position offers hands-on exposure to digital data collection tools and evidence-based program management. The trainee is expected to demonstrate curiosity, attention to detail, initiative, confidentiality, and accountability for assigned tasks and outputs.

LEARNING AREAS AND KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Good written and spoken Nepali and English, with the ability to communicate clearly and work collaboratively.
  • Strong attention to detail, organization, problem-solving, and ability to follow instructions and meet deadlines.
  • Willingness and ability to participate in field visits and work respectfully with diverse communities and partners.

SUCCESS FACTORS

Success in this role will be demonstrated through a proactive learning mindset, attention to detail, respect for data quality and confidentiality, and the ability to turn feedback into improved work. The trainee should progressively take responsibility for assigned tasks, communicate clearly with colleagues, meet agreed deadlines, and contribute to a collaborative learning environment. The role requires professionalism, cultural sensitivity, integrity, and respect for the communities and participants with whom Prosper Global Nepal works.

Integrated Community Development Campaign (ICDC) Nepal is a non-profit making, non -governmental, non – religious and service oriented national level organization. ICDC has been working in the various thematic issues of socio-economic development including livelihood, education, advocacy, environment, sanitation, DRR, human/child rights protection, gender, youth, employment and migration as well as mental health/psychosocial support and HR development. Integrated Community Development Campaign (ICDC) Nepal is implementing an Emergency Flood Response project in Nuwakot, and Dhading districts to deliver timely, needs-based humanitarian assistance and immediate service recovery.

ICDC invites applications from highly competent, experienced and committed professionals for the following positions based in project districts.

Position: Logistic Officer
No. of Vacancy: Few
Project: Child Protection-focused Early Recovery Response, Nuwakot and Dhading
Duty station: Dhading with frequent travel to Nuwakot
Reports to: Project Coordinator, ICDC Nepal (with technical/financial coordination with ICDC Finance Manager and Donor as required)
Works closely with: Project Coordinator, Finance Officer, Engineer, MEAL Officer, Field Officers, Case Workers and ICDC Administration/Logistics team
Duration: 6 months from contract signature (Extension subject to funding and performance).
Salary/benefits: As per ICDC Nepal rules

Position Purpose

The Logistic Officer is responsible for the day-to-day procurement, logistics, supply, asset and operational support required for timely and effective project implementation in Nuwakot and Dhading. The post ensures that goods and services are procured transparently, delivered safely and on time, and properly documented in accordance with ICDC Nepal, and donor requirements.

Key Responsibilities

  •  Procurement planning: Develop and regularly update the project procurement plan in coordination with the Project Coordinator, Engineer, Finance Officer and Field Officers.
  •  Procurement: Facilitate procurement of WASH supplies, hygiene materials, office and field equipment, construction materials and other project requirements in accordance with approved procedures.
  • Supplier management: Obtain quotations, maintain supplier records, support supplier selection and ensure goods and services meet approved specifications, quality and price requirements.
  • Logistics and transportation: Organize transportation, delivery and distribution of project supplies and equipment to field locations, including remote and flood-affected areas.
  •  WASH and infrastructure supplies: Coordinate procurement and delivery of WASH materials and construction supplies in line with technical specifications provided by the Engineer.
  • Stock management: Maintain accurate stock records, conduct regular physical stock checks and ensure proper storage, handling and issuance of project supplies.
  • Asset management: Maintain project asset and equipment registers, ensure proper allocation and safe use of project assets, and report loss, damage or required repairs.
  • Field logistics: Support field teams with transportation, accommodation, communication equipment and other logistical arrangements required for project activities and monitoring visits.
  • Documentation and compliance: Maintain complete procurement and logistics files, including requisitions, quotations, evaluations, purchase orders, delivery notes, invoices and stock records.
  • Coordination with Finance: Work closely with the Finance Officer to ensure procurement documentation is complete and payments to suppliers are processed promptly.
  •  Risk and safety: Assess logistical and access challenges related to floods, landslides and road conditions and propose practical solutions to maintain safe and uninterrupted project operations.
  • Reporting: Provide regular procurement, stock, asset and logistics updates to the Project Coordinator and flag delays or operational risks requiring corrective action.

Key Deliverables

  • Updated procurement plan and procurement activities completed on schedule.
  • Goods and services procured transparently and in accordance with approved procedures.
  •  Timely delivery of project supplies and materials to designated field locations.
  •  Accurate stock, asset and procurement records maintained.
  • Complete procurement and logistics documentation available for review and audit.
  • Regular logistics updates and timely reporting of operational risks and delays.

Qualifications and Experience

Essential

  •  Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Management, Logistics, Supply Chain Management or a related field.
  • Minimum 2 years of relevant experience in logistics, procurement or supply-chain management, preferably with NGOs/INGOs.
  • Practical experience in procurement, supplier management, stock management and transportation arrangements.
  •  Good understanding of procurement procedures, documentation and internal controls.
  • Good skills in MS Office, particularly MS Excel and Word.
  •  Strong organizational, coordination and negotiation skills.
  • Fluent Nepali and working English.
  •  Ability and willingness to travel and work in remote, flood- and landslide-affected areas.

Desirable

  •  Experience in emergency response, disaster recovery or humanitarian programs.
  • Experience procuring WASH, construction or relief materials.
  •  Experience working with INGO partners and donor-funded projects.
  •  Knowledge of local suppliers and transportation networks in Nuwakot and Dhading.
  •  Valid driving license and ability to ride a motorbike is an advantage.

Core Competencies

  •  Procurement integrity and transparency
  • Planning and organization
  • Negotiation and supplier management
  •  Problem-solving under operational constraints
  • Teamwork and adaptability
  •  Attention to detail

Safeguarding and Conduct

The post-holder must sign and adhere to ICDC Nepal’s Code of Conduct and safeguarding, child protection and PSEA (Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse) policies. Appointment is subject to reference checks and a child-safeguarding screening. Any safeguarding concern must be reported immediately through the agreed reporting channel.

Position: Admin & Finance Officer
No. of Vacancy: Few
Project: Child Protection-focused Early Recovery Response, Nuwakot and Dhading
Duty station: Dhading with frequent travel to Nuwakot
Reports to: Project Coordinator, ICDC Nepal (with technical/financial coordination with ICDC Executive Director, Finance Manager and Donor as required)
Works closely with: Project Coordinator, MEAL Officer, Field Officers, Logistic Officer, Case Workers and ICDC Finance/Admin team
Duration: 6 months from contract signature (Extension subject to funding and performance)
Salary/benefits: As per ICDC Nepal rules

Position Purpose

The Admin and Finance Officer will be responsible for the effective financial and administration management of the Early Recovery Flood Response Project in Nuwakot and Dhading. The position will ensure sound financial planning, budget monitoring, timely payments, accurate financial reporting and compliance with ICDC Nepal’s, and Donors requirements. The officer will also coordinate day to day office administration, professional documentation, travel arrangements, asset records, and other operational support to ensure the smooth and efficient implementation of project activities.

Key Responsibilities

  • Administration & Financial management: Coordinate day to day office administration as well as documentation, maintain accurate project accounts, vouchers, ledgers and supporting documents in accordance with ICDC financial procedures and donor requirements.
  • Office Administration: Ensure the smooth day to day administrative functioning of the project office, including office supplies, utilities, communication, stationery, and other administrative requirements.
  •  Budget monitoring: Track expenditure against approved budget lines, prepare budget-versus-actual updates and alert the Project Coordinator to variances, underspending or potential overspending.
  •  Payments and advances: Process staff, supplier and activity payments; manage advances and ensure timely settlement with complete supporting documents.
  •  Cash assistance: Support the financial aspects of multipurpose cash assistance, including beneficiary payment lists, payment documentation, reconciliation and secure handling of financial records.
  • Bank and cash management: Maintain project cash and bank records, conduct regular reconciliations and ensure appropriate controls over project funds.
  • Procurement and payment coordination: Work closely with the Logistic Officer and Project Coordinator to ensure procurement payments are processed on time and supported by approved documentation.
  • Compliance: Ensure expenditures comply with ICDC Nepal, and donor financial policies, approval procedures and applicable rules; identify and report any financial irregularities.
  • Reporting: Prepare regular administrative financial information and inputs for monthly, interim and final project reports; provide related documents required for donor reporting.
  •  Documentation and filing: Maintain complete, organized and secure financial files, including invoices, receipts, payment requests, quotations, approvals, advances and reconciliations.
  • Audit support: Support internal and external audits and provide requested financial documents and explanations in a timely manner.
  •  Field support: Conduct or support field-level financial monitoring and verification of project expenditures and activities.

Key Deliverables

  • Accurate and up-to-date project administrative and financial records and supporting documents.
  • Regular budget-versus-actual expenditure monitoring and timely identification of variances.
  • Timely processing and settlement of payments and staff/activity advances.
  •  Properly documented and reconciled cash assistance transactions.
  •  Monthly and final reports/inputs submitted on schedule.
  • Complete project documents and financial files ready for audit and donor review.

Qualifications and Experience

Essential

  •  Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, Management or a related field.
  •  Minimum 2 years of relevant experience in financial management, preferably with NGOs/INGOs or humanitarian/development projects.
  •  Good knowledge of project administration, accounting principles, budgeting, financial controls and documentation.
  •  Experience in payment processing, bank/cash reconciliation, advance management and financial reporting.
  • Good knowledge of MS Excel and MS Office; experience with accounting software is an advantage.
  •  Understanding of NGO/donor financial compliance and supporting documentation requirements.
  •  Fluent Nepali and working English.
  •  Ability and willingness to travel to project locations in flood- and landslide-affected areas.

Desirable

  •  Experience in emergency response, cash and voucher assistance or post-disaster programs.
  •  Experience working with INGO partners and donor-funded projects.
  •  Familiarity with ICDC Nepal financial procedures or similar NGO financial systems.
  • Experience in financial monitoring of field activities.

Core Competencies

  •  Financial accuracy and attention to detail
  •  Integrity and accountability
  •  Planning and organization
  •  Confidentiality and sound judgement
  •  Problem-solving and teamwork

Safeguarding and Conduct

The post-holder must sign and adhere to ICDC Nepal’s Code of Conduct and safeguarding, child protection and PSEA (Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse) policies. Appointment is subject to reference checks and a child-safeguarding screening. Any safeguarding concern must be reported immediately through the agreed reporting channel.

Interested candidates meeting the criteria are requested to submit their updated CV, a cover letter, copy of Nepali citizenship certificate, copies of academic certificates and transcripts, copies of experience letters, training certificates, recent passport size photograph and two professional references with their contact details to icdc.vacancy@gmail.com with the subject line “Application: Admin & Finance Officer/Logistic Officer – [Your Name]”.

Application Deadline: 5 PM, 26 October 2026.

National Federation of the Deaf Nepal (NDFN) is an umbrella organization of, by and for the Deaf People in Nepal. NDFN was established in 1995 by the joint effort and collaboration of the 8 local deaf associations and formally registered as non- governmental organization in District Administration Office, Kathmandu and Social Welfare Council. Currently NDFN is having 55 district deaf associations affiliated in Nepal.

The purpose of formation of NDFN is to strengthen the movement of rights of persons with deafness in Nepal by advocating deaf friendly law and policies and collaborating with possible stakeholders, raising awareness, developing and disseminating Nepali Sign Language, formation, capacity building of local deaf associations, strengthening interpreter’s service, communication, employment and many more. Access to information, quality education for deaf children in their preferred language, removing barrier in communication, job and employment opportunities and others are core issues and activities of NDFN.
NDFN is working in close collaboration with the organization of person with deafblindness, parent organization and organization of person of visually impaired to promote the rights of persons with deafblindness in Nepal. NDFN is recognized as the ‘National Resource Centre on Deafblindness’ and is currently working to enhance access to education and digital resources for persons with deafblindness in Kathmandu, Biratnagar, and Pokhara. In this context, NDFN is seeking qualified candidates for the following position:

PHASE Nepal is implementing the project “Strengthening Community Health Systems for Respectful, Equitable and Accountable Maternal, Newborn, Child Health and Nutrition Services” in partnership with UNICEF Nepal. PHASE Nepal will directly implement the project in Karnali Province and provide technical and financial oversight to the Dalit Ethnic Upliftment Center (DEUC), Bara for implementation in Madhesh Province. Field staff in both provinces will be engaged by PHASE Nepal and will work in close coordination with DEUC in Madhesh.

The project aims to strengthen the quality, equity and accountability of maternal, newborn, child health and nutrition (MNCHN) services by promoting respectful care, strengthening health worker and FCHV capacity, integrating the Maternal and Child Health (MCH) Handbook into routine antenatal care and counselling, strengthening community engagement and dialogue, and using health facility and community scorecards to identify gaps and support service improvements.

The project will be implemented in six municipalities: Bheri Municipality, Sani Bheri Rural Municipality and Birendranagar Municipality in Karnali Province, and Hanumannagar Kankalini Municipality, Kolhabi Municipality and Birgunj Metropolitan City in Madhesh Province. The project will particularly focus on pregnant and postnatal women, mothers and children, adolescents, and underserved and marginalized communities, with emphasis on improving access to respectful, equitable and accountable MNCHN services.

We are inviting applications from qualified, committed, and eligible individuals for the following positions based at the Trust’s Headquarters in Pokhara.

1. Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEAL) Coordinator.

2. Senior MEAL Coordinator.

1. MEAL COORDINATOR

Key Responsibilities:

The MEAL Coordinator is accountable to the Information Support Manager for internal HR and administrative management, ensuring compliance with organisational policies and procedures. The role is directly accountable to the MEAL Team for the development and implementation of MEAL strategy, prioritisation of workloads, and the effective delivery of MEAL objectives across the organisation.

Working closely with the Senior MEAL Coordinator, programme teams, and the UK MEAL Team, the postholder will support the implementation of agreed targeted monitoring visits, plans, frameworks, and reporting requirements, ensuring that MEAL activities are delivered in line with organisational priorities and standards.

Please read through the Job Description for further information on job responsibilities.

Essential and Desirable Criteria:

  •  Bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering, Public Health, Social Science, Public Administration or related field with 5 years of work experience in MEAL.
  • Excellent communication, presentation, and critical analytical skills.
  •  Experience in Infrastructure Technical Monitoring, Research studies, and good knowledge in Management Information System (MIS) and computer applications.
  • Professional technical knowledge/expertise in research study, data collection, survey, statistics and data analysis.
  •  Experience in documenting success stories, case stories for learning and writing high-quality reports and well-spoken English.
  • Self-motivated, adaptable, flexible and effective in delivery of service and good time management and Strong organisational skills.
  •  Must be able to demonstrate the knowledge in Cross Cutting Components topics like Gender Equality and Social Inclusion (GESI) and DRR within the programme.
  •  Must have excellent computing skills in Ms-Word, Excel and Power Point.
  • Professional technical knowledge/expertise in demography, statistics, and data management; Methodology of MEAL, theories, standards and models, quantitative/qualitative/mixed methods, validity/reliability testing of data, data analysis and interpretation, and statistical inference methods.
  • Professional technical knowledge/expertise in Activity Monitoring & Evaluation, Evaluation Design, data analysis, and reporting.
  •  Knowledge of Nepal Government Development Planning Procedures, Local Self-Governance Act, WASH, Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR), school and medical will be an advantage.

2. SENIOR MEAL COORDINATOR

Key Responsibilities:

The Senior MEAL Coordinator is accountable to the Information Support Manager for internal HR and administrative management, ensuring compliance with organisational policies and procedures.

The role is directly accountable to the UK MEAL Team for the development and implementation of MEAL strategy, the prioritisation of workloads, and the effective delivery of MEAL objectives across the organisation.

Working closely with the UK MEAL Team, the postholder will provide technical leadership and oversight to MEAL Coordinators in the implementation of agreed monitoring plans, targeted monitoring visits, MEAL frameworks, and reporting requirements. The role will ensure that MEAL activities are delivered consistently, efficiently, and in line with organisational priorities, standards, and best practices.

Please read through the Job Description for further information on job responsibilities.

Essential and Desirable Criteria:

  •  Ability to design, document, and produce high-quality survey reports, monitoring reports, assessment reports, and impact evaluation reports, ensuring findings are evidence-based, well analysed, and effectively communicated to support decision-making, learning, and programme improvement.
  •  Ability to collect, analyse and interpret data using tools such as Excel, Kobo/ODK, databases, and produce reports.
  •  Analytical, detail-oriented, organised, ethical, collaborative, adaptable and solution-focused, with the ability to use evidence to improve programme quality and decision-making.
  •  Excellent communication, presentation, and critical analytical skills.
  •  Professional technical knowledge/expertise in research study, data collection, survey, statistics and data analysis.
  • Must be able to share and contribute to the ethos and vision of the Trust.
  •  Knowledge of Nepal Government Development Planning Procedures, Local Self-Governance Act, WASH, Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR), school and medical will be an advantage.

Position: Communication and Outreach Coordinator
Location Kathmandu

About the organization

Ipas works globally with a vision that every woman and girl has the right and ability to determine her own sexuality and reproductive health. Our programs use a multifaceted approach that addresses reproductive health services, access to services and fulfillment of reproductive rights.

As part of the broader reproductive justice movement, Ipas is working to ensure that abortion and contraceptive care are essential health services and that all people can access them. Our programs use a multifaceted approach that addresses reproductive health services, access to services and fulfillment of reproductive rights. We seek to expand the availability, quality and sustainability of abortion and related reproductive health services, as well as improve the enabling environment for the services.

Ipas Nepal’s program intervention prioritize intersectional partnerships that integrates into the broader gender equality and social justice, including gender-based violence prevention and response, and women-led climate justice.

Job Summary

The Communication and Outreach Coordinator will serve as the focal point and architect of the Ipas Nepal’s internal and external communications. The position will lead the design and implementation of integrated communication, outreach, and stakeholder engagement strategies for Ipas Nepal. S/he will translate program evidence, organizational priorities, and advocacy objectives into clear and compelling communication products, strengthen organizational visibility and public engagement, promote consistent branding and messaging, and build meaningful relationships with media, government, partners, communities, donors, and other stakeholders. S/he will ensure that communication and outreach activities are timely, inclusive, rights-based, gender-transformative, and aligned with organizational policies and strategic goals.

Primary Responsibilities

1. Communication Strategy, Policy, and Brand Management

  • Lead the development, review, and implementation of integrated internal and external communication, outreach, and stakeholder engagement strategies aligned with Ipas Nepal priorities.
  •  Develop and update communication plans, protocols, key messages, editorial calendars, and branding guidelines.
  •  Ensure consistent application of Ipas brand standards, approved messages, visual identity, and rights-based language across digital and printed materials.
  • Advise leadership, program teams, and partners on communication for organizational positioning, advocacy, resource mobilization, and program visibility.
  •  Identify communication opportunities, emerging issues, and reputational risks and recommend appropriate responses.

2. Content Development, Documentation, and Knowledge Translation

  • Ensure quality of annual reports, fact sheets, briefs, brochures, newsletters, presentations, publications, campaign materials, and other information, education, and communication products.
  • Collect and package case studies, human-interest stories, photo stories, video stories, lessons learned, good practices, and program results using informed consent and safeguarding standards.
  • Maintain an organized communication asset library, including approved photographs, videos, publications, templates, consent records, media coverage, and key messages.
  •  Coordinate translation, editing, design, printing, and quality assurance of communication products.

3. Digital Communication and Public Engagement

  •  Manage and regularly update Ipas Nepal communication channels, including the website, social media platforms, digital campaigns, and relevant online portals.
  • Develop platform-appropriate content and publishing schedules to increase the reach, accessibility, and engagement of priority messages.
  • Monitor digital performance and audience engagement and use findings to improve communication approaches.
  •  Ensure digital content follows requirements for consent, accessibility, privacy, data protection, safeguarding, and brand compliance.
  • Support timely communication during humanitarian emergencies, public health concerns, and other situations requiring coordinated messaging.

4. Outreach and Stakeholder Engagement

  • Design and implement outreach and stakeholder engagement plans for government agencies, civil society organizations, professional associations, networks, communities, donors, media, and other priority audiences.
  •  Map and maintain stakeholder and media contact databases and support structured, timely, and respectful engagement.
  •  Coordinate communication and outreach for campaigns, advocacy initiatives, consultations, launches, workshops, conferences, and knowledge-sharing events.
  • Work with program teams and partners to tailor messages and materials for different audiences, including underserved and marginalized communities.
  • Represent or support Ipas Nepal in communication forums, networks, and public engagement platforms as assigned.

5. Media Relations and Organizational Visibility

  •  Build and maintain professional relationships with media houses, journalists, editors, and communication networks.
  •  Prepare approved media materials and coordinate inquiries and interview opportunities with authorized organizational representatives.
  • Monitor and document media mentions and relevant public discourse and prepare periodic summaries.
  • Promote accurate, ethical, stigma-free, and rights-based reporting on sexual and reproductive health and rights.

6. Internal Communication, Coordination, and Capacity Strengthening

  • Serve as the internal focal point for communication and outreach, supporting information flow across teams and projects.
  • Support teams to integrate communication and outreach objectives into project design, implementation, monitoring, and reporting.
  •  Orient and coach staff and partners on branding, communication policy, storytelling, media engagement, consent, and responsible digital communication.
  • Coordinate with relevant Ipas global and regional communication colleagues and brand champions to align messages and amplify Ipas Nepal content.
  • Support internal updates, staff communication, project milestones, and organizational announcements through appropriate channels.

7. Monitoring, Learning, and Reporting

  •  Use evidence and feedback to refine communication approaches, products, channels, and engagement methods.
  • Document lessons learned and contribute communication evidence to donor reports, organizational reports, and learning products.

8. Gender Equality, Social Inclusion, and Feminist Communication

  • Integrate Ipas Nepal Gender Equality and Social Inclusion commitments and a gender-transformative, feminist, and rights-based approach throughout communication processes and products.

PSEA compliance

As an Ipas Nepal employee read, understand, and sign the acknowledgement to comply with all aspects of the PSEA as defined by the PSEA policy.
Contribute to safe working environment where every team member is treated equally and respectfully.
Ensure Ipas representatives (including consultants, interns, volunteers, independent contractors, suppliers/vendors, board members, sub-awardees) and government officials directly working with Ipas and its partners understand and practice the prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse policy while in partnership and implement program with Ipas.

Other responsibilities

  • Engage in a learning culture and participate and enrol learning courses of Ipas University.
  • Willing to be back up for staff and vacant positions and perform other related duties as required.

Program Staff responsibilities

  • Take the responsibility and ownership to inform and display information on Ipas Nepal commitment about PSEA in every Ipas supported program/event/workshop/training as defined by Ipas Nepal PSEA policy.
  • All Ipas implementing partners will develop PSEA policy/or a brief guideline endorsed by the board.

Qualifications, Experience, Knowledge and Skills

  • Master’s degree in Media Studies, Mass Communication, Journalism, Gender Studies, Social Work, or a related field with at least 3 years of relevant professional experience; or a Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field with a minimum of 5 years of relevant professional experience.
  • Intermediate skills in photo and video design, editing, and content production.
  • Knowledge and conceptual understanding about sexual, reproductive and health rights, (focusing on safe abortion and contraception), gender-based violence, climate justice and Social and Behavior Communication Change (SBCC) and Humanitarian emergencies.
  • Experience in program development and knowledge management is an asset.
  • Very good analytical, speaking and writing skills (Nepali and English at least).
  • Familiarity and commitment to rights based and gender transformative approach.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills including familiarity with visibility, branding, and communication.
  • Passion, enthusiasm, and interests on Ipas vision, mission, and strategies
  • High quality of professional integrity and commitment
  • Willing to travel project districts on regular basis.undefinedundefined

Position: Project Associate-Managing the Human Tiger Interface in Nepal (HTI) Project
Location: Chitwan, Bagmati, Nepal

Company Description

WWF Nepal, the global conservation organization leading international efforts for a living planet, seeks applications from qualified Nepali candidates for the following full-time position. If you think you are an achiever and willing to work within a diverse team in a multicultural environment with commitment and passion for what you believe in, you are highly encouraged to apply.

Our Mission

At WWF Nepal, we firmly believe people and nature are inextricably linked. Our mission is to stop the degradation of our planet’s natural environment and build a future Nepal in which people live in harmony with nature.

Our Vision

From its origins as a small group of committed wildlife enthusiasts, WWF has grown into one of the world’s largest and most respected independent conservation organizations, active in over 100 countries.

Over this time, WWF’s focus has evolved from localized efforts in favor of a single species and individual habitats to an ambitious strategy to preserve biodiversity and achieve sustainable development across the globe.

WWF-Nepal envisions a prosperous Nepal, with an active and socially responsible citizenry that a greater sense of stewardship towards the environment.

Our Core Values

We celebrate and respect diversity in nature and among the people, partners, and communities with whom we work. Across the many cultures and individuals that represent WWF, we are unified by one mission, one brand, and one common set of values:

Courage: We demonstrate courage through our actions, we work for change where it’s needed, and we inspire people and institutions to tackle the greatest threats to nature and the future of the planet, which is our home.

Integrity: We live the principles we call on others to meet. We act with integrity, accountability, and transparency, and we rely on facts and science to guide us and to ensure we learn and evolve.

Respect: We honor the voices and knowledge of the people and communities that we serve, and we work to secure their rights to a sustainable future.

Collaboration: We deliver impact at the scale of the challenges we face through the power of collective action and innovation.

Job Description

Nepal’s Terai Arc Landscape has achieved remarkable success in tiger recovery, with numbers nearly tripling from 121 in 2009 to 355 in 2023. However, as a density-dependent species, dispersing sub-adult tigers are in frequent interactions with people and livestock. Consequently, human–tiger conflict is rising across Chitwan–Parsa, Bardia–Banke, and Shuklaphanta, particularly along park boundaries. Although the primary driver of conflict is a spatially expanding tiger population, habitat fragmentation, degraded grasslands, shrinking wetlands, and intense human activities compound the issue.

The project “Managing the Human–Tiger Interface in Nepal”, funded by the Global Environment Facility (GEF) and led by the Ministry of Agriculture, Forests and Environment (MoAFE), Department of National Parks and Wildlife Conservation, aims to advance human-wildlife coexistence efforts by building consensus and capacity for coexistence, reducing impacts of human-tiger conflict, and improving habitats for tigers. It does so through four components: (1) strengthening enabling conditions — improving national policy and municipal planning for conflict management and building frontline response capacity; (2) livelihoods support — engaging communities in social-behavior change, piloting faster and fairer relief and insurance, and supporting tiger-safe livelihood options; (3) habitat management — restoring grasslands and wetlands within park core zones to keep prey and tigers inside protected areas; and (4) knowledge exchange — documenting lessons and sharing them nationally and through the GEF-funded Global Wildlife Program. Together, these interventions aim to reduce conflict, benefit more than 121,000 people, and secure healthy tiger landscapes in Nepal.

Under the direct supervision of the Project Officer, the Project Associate will support the implementation of project activities. This position is expected to have expertise in community engagement and mobilization so that s/he can work with local communities from the buffer zone area and other stakeholders to identify and take up Social Behaviour Change (SBC) measures for HTC-affected communities to reduce exposure to HTC risks and increase empathy for wildlife conservation. This position requires frequent travel to the project site.

Major Duties and Responsibilities:

1. Technical Backstopping

  • Provide technical guidance and expertise for effective community and stakeholder engagement in the project area.
  • Directly responsible for the roll-out of social behavior change (SBC) measures for HTC-affected communities to reduce exposure to HTC risks and increase empathy for wildlife conservation

2. Capacity Building

  • Support in training local communities/farmers/user group members in management of the forest in the buffer zone.
  • Support in strengthening local communities/farmers/user group members’ capacity in livelihood activities.

3. Planning

  • Support the planning process by bringing the voices of the vulnerable community and their adaptation needs during annual workplan finalization.
  • Engage in local communities, government, and stakeholders’ planning process to integrate habitat management, livelihood, and minimizing pressure in PAs and human-wildlife mitigation actions and share project best practices and learning.
  • Support local municipalities in integrating human-wildlife mitigation activities in their annual plans.

4. Project Implementation

  • Facilitate local communities and other key stakeholders from buffer zone areas to ensure that activities are planned and executed in line with the project’s established processes and guidelines.
  • Support the overall implementation of project activities across all components.
  • Support in organizing workshops, training, and periodic planning meetings/sessions.
  • Support for preparing grants and contracts.

5. Coordination

  • Coordinate and communicate with local stakeholders and project partners.
  • Support in logistical arrangements and coordination for PCC meetings and PSC meetings.
  • Coordinate with contractors/consultants for timely completion of activities and submission of reports.

6. Reporting and Documentation

  • Support the Project Officer in the preparation of semi-annual and annual project progress reports (PPR), mainly in data collection and lessons learned from field activity implementation.
  • Support Inclusive Conservation staff to ensure documentation of all safeguards-related activities, including Grievance Redress Mechanisms (GRM).
  • Support the Monitoring, Evaluation, Learning (MEL) and Communications Officer to ensure that communication and learning materials are developed, and success stories are documented and published.

7. Inclusive Conservation

  • Support in identifying and integrating GESI and environmental and social safeguards provisions and activities in finalizing the annual work plan.
  • Support in identifying and integrating the voice, knowledge, skills, and values of indigenous peoples and local communities, and ensuring they benefit from project efforts and activities.

8. Other Duties

This job description covers the main tasks and conveys the spirit of the tasks that are anticipated proactively. Other tasks may be assigned as necessary according to the project needs.

Supervisory Responsibility: None

Working Relationship:

  • Works closely with PMU staff
  • Works closely with existing government, non-government, and civil society partners, consultants, and grantees.

Qualifications

Knowledge: A Bachelor’s degree in Forestry or a related field.

Experience: At least 2 years of experience in project implementation and local stakeholders’ engagement is required. Demonstrated expertise in local community engagement and stakeholder mobilization. Knowledge of integrated HWC interventions, including prevention, mitigation, response, and community engagement approaches, is highly desirable. Knowledge of WWF Projects and GEF projects is preferred. Experience of working in national GEF projects will be an added advantage.

Skills and Abilities:

  • Strong coordination and facilitation skill.
  • Ability to work with diverse local communities.
  • Attention to details and problem-solving skills.
  • Time management and adaptability.
  • Good skills in Microsoft office programs.
  • Strong communication skill with ability to prepare letters and documents in Nepali.
  • Ability to prioritize and work under time constraints.

Additional Information

Interested applicants are requested to apply for the position by 17:00 hours on October 26, 2026. Only shortlisted candidates will be informed.

All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.
