WFP celebrates and embraces diversity. It is committed to the principle of equal employment opportunity for all its employees and encourages qualified candidates to apply irrespective of race, colour, national origin, ethnic or social background, genetic information, gender, gender identity and/or expression, sexual orientation, religion or belief, HIV status or disability.

ABOUT WFP

The World Food Programme is the world’s largest humanitarian organization saving lives in emergencies and using food assistance to build a pathway to peace, stability and prosperity, for people recovering from conflict, disasters and the impact of extreme weather shocks.

At WFP, people are at the heart of everything we do and the vision of the future WFP workforce is one of diverse, committed, skilled, and high performing teams, selected on merit, operating in a healthy and inclusive work environment, living WFP’s values (Integrity, Collaboration, Commitment, Humanity, and Inclusion) and working with partners to save and change the lives of those WFP serves.

To learn more about WFP, visit our website: https://www.wfp.org and follow us on social media to keep up with our latest news: YouTube, LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, Twitter, TikTok.

WHY JOIN WFP?

  • WFP is a 2020 Nobel Peace Prize Laureate.
  •  WFP offers a highly inclusive, diverse, and multicultural working environment.
  • WFP invests in the personal & professional development of its employees through a range of training, accreditation, coaching, mentorship, and other programs as well as through internal mobility opportunities.
  • A career path in WFP provides an exciting opportunity to work across the various country, regional and global offices around the world, and with passionate colleagues who work tirelessly to ensure that effective humanitarian assistance reaches millions of people across the globe.
  •  We offer an attractive compensation package (please refer to the Terms and Conditions section of this vacancy announcement).

WFP encourages female candidates and people with disabilities to apply.

BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE OF THE ASSIGNMENT:

ORGANISATIONAL CONTEXT: These jobs are part of Global Headquarters (GHQ) and/or Country Offices (COs). They report to the Director, Communications Officer or designate.
Job holders at this level have independent responsibility for technical, specialized work including planning, organization and coordination, and setting objectives. They deal with issues that are often undefined and involve areas of uncertainty and complex inter-relationships. The instructions received are broad and the job holders consistently demonstrate a high degree of responsibility and initiative and respond independently to queries. Job holders have the technical expertise and knowledge required to adapt and develop reporting processes in order to continually improve the level of support provided. The position referred will be under the Country Office Partnerships, Communications and Reports Unit.

JOB PURPOSE:
To deliver specialized reporting requirements, contribute to the preparation of high-quality analytical reports, and support proposal development, resource mobilization efforts, and partnership engagement to advance programme objectives.

KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES (not all-inclusive, within delegated authority)

Under the direct supervision of the Partnerships Officer, the incumbent will:

  •  Coordinate and oversee implementation of established corporate and country office reporting systems, applying defined quality standards to ensure consistent, standardized information and reporting products.
  • Collate, validate and synthesize information and data from internal and external sources to facilitate and maximize the exchange of information and data flow between functional areas in the CO.
  •  Support the collation and dissemination of political, humanitarian and operational analysis relevant to WFP’s current and potential responses, including partner policies, trends and preferences that inform country-specific operational reporting.
  •  Coordinate the collection, analysis and communication of essential operational information on the operating environment, programme implementation and available human, financial and physical resources to support timely decision-making at country, regional and corporate levels.
  •  Coordinate preparation of the Annual Country Report (ACR) and related annual reporting exercise in collaboration with all CO units to ensure coherence and quality of performance information.
  • Prepare, coordinate and support clearance of corporate and management reporting products, including country briefs, situation reports, operational updates, Executive Director briefs, daily operational briefs and other ad hoc information products. Maintain reporting calendars and track Country Office and donor reporting requirements, coordinating inputs, quality review, clearance and timely submission of narrative reports and related products.
  •  Manage a broad range of day-to-day questions and information requests from internal and external stakeholders, using specialized knowledge to respond to these in a timely, appropriate manner.
  •  Support capacity strengthening of WFP staff and relevant partners on operational information management and performance reporting procedures, templates and systems, including orientation, coaching and training as required.
  • Ensure that relevant information is collected, and maintained in appropriate files and databases, by self or others, so accurate records are available.
  • Support the preparation and coordination of proposals, briefs, reports, talking points and other partnership products, while maintaining partnership information systems and providing research, analysis and coordination support for partner engagement, reporting, visibility requirements, high-level visits and events to ensure effective positioning, diversification, compliance and timely delivery.
  • Collaborate with counterparts internally to ensure consistency in humanitarian and programme information is complementary to WFP analysis and information.
  • Apply defined quality standards to all information-management and reporting processes and products, identify gaps and recommend practical improvements. Support the assurance of defined quality standards in all processes and products.
  •  Any other related tasks as required or assigned by the supervisor.

Experience consolidating, validating and analyzing qualitative and quantitative information from multiple functions and translating it into clear, accurate and decision-oriented products.

Agriculture Program Officer – Nepal

Basic Job Information

Job Category: Agriculture Value Chain/ Operations

Job Level: Full-time

Job Location: aQysta Nepal Private Limited, Lalitpur (Kathmandu with frequent travel to Lumbini, Karnali and Sudurpaschim Province)

Contract Period: 1 year (with possibility of extension)

TEAM AND ROLE OVERVIEW

The Agriculture Program Officer is being recruited in a full-time to join the dynamic team of aQysta Nepal. This role will focus on coordinating ongoing projects in collaboration with project partners, ensuring effective implementation of agriculture value chain activities, and supporting the company’s mission of improving livelihoods of smallholder farmers through sustainable innovation.

JOB PROFILE

  • Are you passionate about working closely with farmers and driving impact in Nepal’s agriculture sector?
  • Do you have the ability to coordinate stakeholders, manage field operations, and ensure project success?

If your answer is yes, this role offers an excellent opportunity to contribute to meaningful agricultural development initiatives. As an Agriculture Program Officer at aQysta Nepal, you will play a key role in strengthening value chains, supporting farmer engagement, and ensuring efficient project execution across Karnali and Sudurpaschim regions.

RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Identify and assess potential crop value chains, production areas, and farmer groups for exportable crops across Lumbini, Karnali and Sudurpashchim Provinces.
  • Map and evaluate farmer groups, cooperatives, and individual producers across Lumbini, Karnali and Sudurpashchim Provinces to expand aQysta’s sourcing network.
  • Coordinate with project partners, government agencies, cooperatives, and other stakeholders to expand farmer networks and strengthen agricultural value chains.
  • Supervise field staff, conduct farm visits and farmer surveys, and monitor crop production, yield potential, and sourcing feasibility.
  • Lead the overall on-boarding process for new farmers in these new working areas, including orientation on aQysta’s requirements, quality standards, and sourcing procedures.
  • Implement and monitor the Internal Control System (ICS), maintain farmer records, and support organic certification, traceability, and audit preparation.
  • Coordinate with agriculture, procurement, and quality teams to ensure timely sourcing, consistent product quality, and compliance with organic standards.
  • Coordinate with field technicians, farmers, and collection centers of new working areas of Lumbini, Karnali and Sudurpaschim to ensure timely and quality production.
  • Prepare field reports, document progress, and facilitate stakeholder meetings to support effective project implementation.

BACKGROUND AND SKILLS

Academic Background

Bachelor’s degree in Agriculture, Agribusiness, Supply Chain, or related field (Master’s preferred)

Work Experience

Minimum 4 years of relevant experience in agriculture value chain, agribusiness, stakeholder management, or farmer engagement.

Skills and Competencies

  • Strong understanding of Nepal’s agriculture value chains, cropping patterns, and export potential
  • Knowledge of Good Agricultural Practices (GAP), organic farming, and traceability systems
  • Excellent communication skills in English and Nepali
  • Strong stakeholder management and coordination skills
  • Good organizational and time management abilities
  • Experience working directly with farmers, cooperatives, and field teams

Traits

  • Result-oriented and proactive
  • Self-driven with strong ownership
  • Willingness to travel frequently to Lumbini, Karnali and Sudurpaschim Province

WHAT WE OFFER & EXPECT

aQysta offers a collaborative and purpose-driven work environment where you can contribute to impactful agricultural projects. You will gain hands-on experience in value chain development, work with diverse stakeholders, and play a direct role in improving farmer livelihoods through sustainable practices.

How to apply

To apply, please send your updated resume and cover letter to careers@aqysta.com

Position: Project Officer
Division: BBC Media Action
Reports to: Project Manager
Band: C
Location base: Kathmandu with possible travel to field locations
Contract: Till March 2027

Organisation structure

The Project Officer will report to the Project Manager.

Job responsibilities and accountability

Context

BBC Media Action is the BBC’s international development charity. Working with media and communication to help reduce poverty and support people, our aim is to inform, connect and empower people around the world. Our work in Nepal is focused on innovative media and communication initiatives that are strengthening democracy, supporting media ecosystems and tackling information disorder – while supporting communities to prepare for, and adapt to, extreme climate risks.
BBC Media Action Nepal Office is seeking potential applicants for the position of “Project Officer”. The ideal candidate will work full time for a project which aims to improve how weather and climate information is communicated and used by different audiences. The project focuses on ensuring that forecasts and climate related information are clear, practical and actionable. By strengthening communication between climate scientists, journalists, government authorities and local communities, the project supports last mile users to better understand and respond to weather and climate related risks.
“The role may involve working with groups of vulnerable children and adults. For the successful candidate, mandatory training will be provided on BBC Media Action’s safeguarding policy and staff code of conduct. BBC Media Action operates a zero-tolerance policy concerning all forms of abuse and exploitation of vulnerable people.”

Job Purpose

Reporting to the Project Manager, the Project Officer is responsible for helping to ensure that project activities are delivered on time, within budget, and to the desired standards. The responsibilities include systematically tracking and monitoring project activities, coordinating project activities, maintaining and organising project documentation, helping compile project progress reports and contributing to the design and planning of new projects and new business development initiatives.

Main Duties

  • Assist with project co-ordination, including work planning, financial management, and liaising with project donors and partners as required.
  •  Produce regular project reports and contribute to internal project review sessions.
  •  Track project activities against the timelines and regularly update project calendar and milestones.
  •  Provide administrative and logistical support to the project team and assist in the monitoring and evaluation of projects.
  •  Plan, organise and manage training and workshops for partner station as per the project timeline.
  • Organise internal and external meetings, document minutes, and follow up on action points.
  •  Provide support to the Project Manager in ensuring that the project activities adhere to BBC and BBC Media Action policies and editorial guidelines and are steered through the organisation’s central review procedures in a timely manner, ensuring all feedback is incorporated.
  • Provide input into the development of the long-term vision and strategic planning of BBC Media Action’ programme portfolio in Nepal.
  • Present the partnership work of BBC Media Action to external stakeholders and identify the range of opportunities for this.
  •  Contribute to the design of new projects and help identify new business opportunities for BBC Media Action in Nepal. Contribute to external fund-raising proposals, donor reporting, and activities as requested.
  •  Responsible for delivering value for money in the role through effective and efficient management of time and resources.

Essential Knowledge, Skills and Experience

  • A University degree preferably in media and communications, development studies, environmental science, agriculture, business or other relevant fields.
  •  A minimum of four years of experience in designing and managing development projects, preferably in areas related to communicating weather, climate, or agricultural science.
  •  Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English and Nepali.
  • Proven ability to develop and implement a range of project management tools and track activities; and prepare project reports and deliverables.
  •  A strong team player, able to manage relationships effectively and work collaboratively within a diverse team.

Desired Skills and Experience

  • Knowledge and experience in research, as well as monitoring and evaluation of complex projects.
  •  Ability to draw insights from research and apply them to inform project interventions.
  •  Adaptable in working across different time zones, with the ability to coordinate seamlessly with team members from diverse social and cultural backgrounds.
  •  Good understanding of the importance of BBC values, policies, procedures, and guidelines, including Health and Safety regulations.

If you are interested in applying for this position, please send a CV and Covering Letter outlining your interest in the role, and demonstrating how you fulfil the essential skills and experience, by 26 October 2026 to application@np.bbcmediaaction.org (with job title in the subject line).

Please note that only shortlisted candidates will be contacted for further recruitment processes.

Position: National Information Officer, NOC
Job Opening ID: 286168
Job Network : Public Information and Conference Management
Job Family : Public Information
Category and Level : National Professional Officers, NO-C
Recruitment Type : Position Specific Job Openings
Duty Station: KATHMANDU
Department/Office : Department of Global Communications
Deadline : Oct 23, 2026

Org. Setting and Reporting

This position is located in the United Nations Information Centre in Kathmandu (UNIC Kathmandu), within the Information Centres Service (ICS) of the Outreach Division (OD) of the Department of Global Communications (DGC). The UNIC is part of the global network of United Nations Information Centres (UNICs), and UNIC Kathmandu is the principal source of information about the United Nations system in Nepal. The UNIC is responsible for promoting public understanding and support for the aims and activities of the United Nations by communicating about its work and disseminating UN information materials to a local audience in English and local languages, including Nepali; engaging local and regional partners; and, overall, bringing the United Nations closer to the peoples it serves. The UNIC Kathmandu has been integrated with the Resident Coordinator Office (RCO) in Nepal since the operationalization of the United Nations development system reform on 1 January 2019. The incumbent reports directly to the Chief of Office of the RCO in Nepal and is under the general supervision of the Director, UNIC New Delhi.

Responsibilities

Within delegated authority, the incumbent is responsible for the following duties:

  •  In line with the Global Communications Strategy of the United Nations and the UN and UN country team (UNCT) branding strategy, support the UNCT Communication and Advocacy Group (UNCAG) with the development and implementation of country-wide strategic communications plans, campaigns and activities targeted to local audiences, in consultation with the RCO, and/or UN partners as well as with DGC UNHQ.
  • Takes a leading role on communications issues within the UNCT by serving as the Secretariat for the UNCAG at the country level in consultation with DGC UNHQ and the RCO.
  •  Provides substantive support to the Resident Coordinator and UN Country Team (UNCT) in designing, implementing and monitoring the UN joint communications strategy, aligned to the Global UN Communications Strategy and based on the UN Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF), a key instrument for planning and implementing UN development activities in the country, in support of the implementation of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development.
  •  Provides substantive support to the RC and UNCT, UN Programme Management Team (or equivalent) and Results Groups on potential issues, concerns and risks related to communications and advocacy, and suggests corrective actions.
  •  In collaboration with the UNCAG and the UN Programme Management Team (or equivalent), and in coordination with the RCO team responsible for data management and results reporting, drafts the annual communications plan to publicize and communicate results with a focus on the UN’s development impact.
  •  Drives and coordinates the development of country specific, including UNCT, multimedia communications products as well as digital and social media products and activities in multiple languages.
  •  Maintains the integrated UNCT website and social media accounts in English and Nepali, in line with UN Secretariat governance mechanisms, including those related to information security and using up-to-date social media platforms and web practices.
  •  Identifies, adapts, and institutes use of communications tools with innovative approaches and keeps pace with emerging technology to garner largest outreach and effectiveness of UN communications.
  • In support of the RC, drafts, at a high-quality level, in English and local languages, including Nepali various print and digital communications products, as well as engages in public speaking with media, partners and local interlocutors.
  • Monitors and analyzes current events, public opinion and press coverage, identifying issues and trends, advising DGC UNHQ, the RC and the UNCT on appropriate action/responses.
  •  In collaboration with the UNCAG, conducts media outreach, including development of media strategies and action plans, initiating proactive media outreach efforts; maintains contacts with national and regional media in Nepal, disseminates information materials to the media, drafts or places op-eds and arranges interviews, organizes press conferences and briefings, monitors press coverage of UN issues; consults with press on approach/story angle and other information requests, undertakes appropriate follow-up action and analyzes and reports on the impact of coverage.
  •  Initiates and sustains proactive professional relationships with key constituencies and partners at the national and regional level and undertakes joint strategic activities with them; plans and facilitates dialogues with partners to improve public engagement and participatory approaches to increase understanding about the UN’s work in Nepal.
  •  Conducts educational outreach activities, including the engagement with Model United Nations conferences and organizing public-speaking opportunities at local educational institutions with support from and/or the participation of the UN Resident Coordinator and/or the UN Country Team.
  •  Assumes responsibilities for the day-to-day running of UNIC Kathmandu; assumes overall responsibility for the administration of the UNIC by overseeing the planning and management of the UNIC’s overall activities and its operational requirements, including its budget and equipment; monitors the output of the UNIC and reports to DGC UNHQ and RC/O on a monthly, quarterly, annual and ad hoc basis.
  •  Performs other functions and special duties as required by the Director of CCOD, the Chief of ICS/CCOD, and/or the UN Resident Coordinator, including providing crisis communications support; representing the UN at conferences; participating in seminars; coordinating and drafting op-eds, speeches and interviews including for the Resident Coordinator.

Competencies

PROFESSIONALISM: Demonstrated knowledge of communications techniques, including audience-focused strategic communications and crisis communications; proven ability to implement effective media campaigns and to develop traditional and digital media products and activities targeting the media; ability to identify communications opportunities and problems and to articulate these to clients. Ability to advise on communications challenges, assess communications environments, develop communications strategies, and manage implementation of communications campaigns in Nepal with various promotional techniques. Ability to make decisions with an eye to the impact on others and on the Organization and to apply rules, regulations, policies and guidelines in work situations. Shows pride in work and in achievements; demonstrates professional competence and mastery of subject matter; is conscientious and efficient in meeting commitments, observing deadlines and achieving results; is motivated by professional rather than personal concerns; shows persistence when faced with difficult problems or challenges; remains calm in stressful situations. Takes responsibility for incorporating gender perspectives and ensuring the equal participation of women and men in all areas of work.

COMMUNICATION: Speaks and writes clearly and effectively; listens to others, correctly interprets messages from others and responds appropriately; asks questions to clarify and exhibits interest in having two-way communication; tailors language, tone, style and format to match audience; demonstrates openness in sharing information and keeping people informed.

PLANNING AND ORGANIZING: Develops clear goals that are consistent with agreed strategies; identifies priority activities and assignments; adjusts priorities as required; allocates appropriate amount of time and resources for completing work; foresees risks and allows for contingencies when planning; monitors and adjusts plans and actions as necessary; uses time efficiently
.
Education

An advanced university degree (Master’s or Doctorate degree, or equivalent) in communications, journalism, public information or a related field is required. A first-level university degree in combination with two (2) additional years of qualifying experience may be accepted in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Work Experience

A minimum of five years of progressively responsible experience, including experience in managing contacts and networking with the media, non-governmental organizations, government officials, international and national organizations, business groups, civil society, etc. in Nepal is required. Experience in developing and implementing communications strategies is required. Experience in crisis communications or reputational risk management is required. Experience in speaking to diverse audiences (e.g. general public, Government officials, special interest groups) is desirable. Experience working across multimedia platforms with traditional and digital media is desirable. Experience working with the United Nations or a comparable international organization is desirable.

ABOUT PROSPER GLOBAL

PROGRAM / DEPARTMENT SUMMARY

The Zurich Flood Climate Resilience Alliance (ZCFRA) is an alliance of nine organizations including international NGOs, private sector, and academic organizations, who have come together with the support of the Zurich Foundation to drive better policy and practice to reduce the negative impact of floods on peoples’ and communities’ ability to thrive.

The Alliance is implementing a 12-year vision through 2025. The current phase (phase 3, 2024-2027) represents the first cycle of this long-term vision. Previously, the Alliance completed its first phase in 2018, and its second phase in December 2023 and third phase will run till Dec 2027. During this time, The Alliance works together to achieve 12-year vision by implementing solutions, promoting good practice, influencing policy and facilitating systemic change. In Nepal, the Alliance is comprised of Prosper Global and Practical Action, working together on joint outcomes aiming at:

Building ex-ante resilience of communities at risk of flood and heat impacts across Nepal

Improving early warning and early action in advance of probable hazards

Enabling people who experience livelihoods losses due to floods and heat to recover quickly through compensation and/or insurance

The Communication and Knowledge Management Trainee position is a structured learning opportunity designed to build professional skills in strategic communication, content development, advocacy, influencing, knowledge management and organizational learning. This role offers dual benefit: the trainee gains hands-on experience in humanitarian and development programs, while the organization benefits from the trainee’s proactive support in documenting and disseminating impact. While mentorship is provided, the trainee is expected to take initiative, manage their learning journey effectively, and maintain full accountability for the tasks and products they oversee. The trainee will support Zurich Climate Resilience Alliance program “Climate Resilience for Communities” in Nepal. S/he will collaborate with Prosper Global field-teams in Sudurpaschim and Madhesh Provinces, CRC partners at the country level, as well as interact with government, UN, and private sector representatives.

LEARNING AREAS

Strategic Communication and Content Development:

  • Skill Building: Gain practical experience in drafting, editing, and formatting professional communication materials, including factsheets, success stories, briefs, tools and social media content.
  • Field Engagement :Learn to capture high-quality field narratives, photographs, and audio-visual materials by collaborating with program and MEL teams during field visits.
  • Brand Stewardship: Develop an eye for detail by ensuring all materials align with global branding and communication guidelines.
  • Event Documentation: Learn to document and disseminate key takeaways from project events and workshops to enhance organizational visibility.

Knowledge Management:

  • Learning Processes: Develop skills in identifying and documenting program lessons learned, best practices, impact briefs, case studies etc.
  • Information Architecture: Gain experience in organizing and managing digital knowledge repositories (shared drives/databases) to ensure information is accessible and user-friendly.
  • Product Translation: Learn to translate technical data into tailored knowledge products, such as learning notes and presentations, communication materials for diverse audiences.
  • Institutional Positioning: Support the team in understanding how strategic communication and documentation contribute to the organization’s influence and positioning in the sector.
  • Content Development: Contribute to develop reports, knowledge products, talking points, key messages, audio-visuals, web-based posts, synthesize studies/research etc.

Coordination, Influencing and Learning:

  • Cross-Functional Coordination: Build professional collaboration skills by working across the Program, MEL, and Operations teams to gather and share information.
  • Facilitation & Learning: Support the organization of internal learning events and workshops, gaining experience in facilitation and meeting documentation.
  • Evidence-Based Influencing: Learn how to use research and field evidence, develop influencing materials and support advocacy and influencing efforts.
  • Ownership & Delivery: While this is a learning role, the trainees are expected to proactively manage their assigned tasks, meeting deadlines and ensuring the high quality of their outputs.

ACCOUNTABILITY

Reports Directly to: Program Manager, Climate Resilience for Communities

Works Directly with: Program Team members and Country MEL focal person

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS AND SKILLS

  • Strong willingness to learn and professional growth.
  • Fresh graduates who have completed a bachelor’s degree in communication, development studies, or any other relevant fields within the last two years of experience.
  • Prior experience of academic research is desirable.
  • Good communication skills and interpersonal skills.
  • Good written and spoken English and Nepali
  • Basic computer skills (MS Word, MS Excel, MS PowerPoint, CANVA)
  • Use of AI and social media, knowledge of media interactions, photography, and webpage designing are advantageous.
  • Basic understanding of climate change, DRR, resilience and humanitarian actions is an advantage.
  • Attention to detail and organizational skills.
  • Willingness and availability to travel to the program’s working areas, actively support field-level implementation, and learn from field experiences.

SUCCESS FACTORS

Success in this role is defined by a proactive learning mindset and the initiative to turn on-the-job opportunities into professional growth in dynamic development and humanitarian context. A successful trainee will transition from assisted tasks to the independent management of assignments, bringing creative ideas to knowledge management and communication while remaining strictly accountable for the quality of their results. By demonstrating resilience, cultural sensitivity, and a commitment to planned professional development, you will help spark innovative ways to share information and contribute to the overall success of high-quality, collaborative programming.

The most successful Prosper Global team members have a strong commitment to teamwork and accountability, thrive in evolving and changing environments, and make effective written and verbal communication a priority in all situations. Prosper Global Team members represent the agency both during and outside of work hours when deployed in a field posting or on a visit/short-term assignment to a field posting. Team members are expected to conduct themselves in a professional manner and respect local laws, customs and MC’s policies, procedures, and values at all times and in all in-country venues.

ONGOING LEARNING

In support of our belief that learning organizations are more effective, efficient and relevant to the communities we serve, we empower all team members to dedicate 5% of their time to learning activities that further their personal and/or professional growth and development.

TEAM ENGAGEMENT AND EFFECTIVENESS

Achieving our mission starts with how we build our team and collaborate. By bringing together individuals with a variety of experiences, backgrounds, and perspectives, we strengthen our ability to solve complex challenges and drive innovation. We foster a culture of trust and respect, where every team member is valued for their contributions, empowered to reach their full potential, and motivated to do their best work.

We recognize that building a strong and effective team is an ongoing process, and we remain committed to learning, improving, and growing together.

EQUAL EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITY

Prosper Global is an equal opportunity employer committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all employees and qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, sex, sexual orientation, religion or belief, national origin, age, disability, marital status, veteran status, or any other characteristics protected under applicable law.

SAFEGUARDING AND ETHICS

Prosper Global is committed to ensuring that all individuals we come into contact with through our work, whether team members, community members, program participants or others, are treated with respect and dignity. We are committed to the core principles regarding prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse laid out by the UN Secretary General and IASC and have signed on to the The Misconduct Disclosure Scheme. We will not tolerate child abuse, sexual exploitation, abuse, or harassment by or of our team members. As part of our commitment to a safe and inclusive work environment, team members are expected to conduct themselves in a professional manner, respect local laws and customs, and to adhere to Ethics policies and reporting misconduct | Prosper Global and values at all times. Team members must complete mandatory Code of Conduct eLearning courses upon hire and annually.

Position: Senior Livelihood Coordinator
Location: Kusunti, KC Tower, Lalitpur
End Date: October 19, 2026

With 75 years of experience, our focus is on helping the most vulnerable children overcome poverty and experience fullness of life. We help children of all backgrounds, even in the most dangerous places, inspired by our Christian faith.

Come join our 31,000+ staff working in nearly 100 countries and share the joy of transforming vulnerable children’s life stories!

Employee Contract Type: Local – Fixed Term Employee (Fixed Term)

Job Description:

The Senior Livelihood Coordinator is responsible for overall livelihood recovery portfolio of RISE Rapid Activation project in coordination with other inter and cross-sectional departments. This position provides technical and managerial leadership for RISE projects economic and livelihood recovery portfolio, leading quality programme planning, market and livelihood assessments, implementation, monitoring and adaptive management to restore and diversify household livelihood including incomes, enterprises, employment, productive assets and market systems while strengthening resilience to future shocks, managing and provide technical oversight to the ER coordinator, Cash Coordinator and partners, ensure effective resource and budget management, and maintain strong coordination with government, private sector, financial institutions, communities and other recovery actors.

Furthermore, the incumbent will manage government and other stakeholder relationship to foster the strong collaboration, particularly related to early recovery, food security and livelihoods for the project activities, collaborating with identifying the gaps and needs that project intends to support and coordinating with like-minded agencies for coherent implementation. Additionally, the position will maintain the strong relationships with private sector actors, financial institutions, communities, and other stakeholders to promote sustainable, inclusive and market-oriented recovery outcomes.

MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES

Technical and project management and support

  • Lead planning, implementation, monitoring and completion of all Early Recovery project activities.
  • Oversee project objectives, outputs and outcomes are achieved within approved timelines and budgets.
  • Review annual, quarterly and monthly implementation plans.
  • Monitor and provide technical inputs for implementation of livelihood initiatives across Rasuwa and Nuwakot districts.
  • Provide overall technical and operational backstopping to project staff and partners.
  • Ensure quality programming aligned with Sphere Standards, CHS/humanitarian principles, and World Vision standards.
  • Identify implementation risks and develop mitigation measures.
  • Facilitate adaptive management based on emerging needs and lessons learned.
  • Regularly update the Early recovery cluster and represent World vision in district/province’s livelihood settings.

Necessary assessments are conducted and reports are prepared/drafted/endorsed which will lead to efficient, effective, and resilient recovery & rehabilitation outputs.

Leadership in the Assessment and Technical Support

  • Lead and oversee integrated recovery assessment and interventions with strong strategy in both districts including:

Initial livelihood loss & damage assessment

  • Work closely with Local Government (LG), agriculture and livestock units, enterprise development units and Federation of Nepalese Chambers of Commerce & Industry (FNCCI) to collect the initial loss and damage information.
  • Prepare and endorse the initial assessment from LG to prepare for early recovery actions

Prepare market assessment report post disaster

  • Work closely with FNCCI and LG to prepare market disruption, inflation and opportunity loss report to inform the WV’s livelihood team on necessary injection required to support immediate and long-term recovery/rehabilitation status.

Lead assessment on employment loss and new employment opportunities post disaster

  • Work closely with enterprise development unit, FNCCI and other relevant stakeholders to study the employment loss status and look for new employment/enterprise development opportunities created post disaster.
  • Assess the status of current job opportunities and provide necessary conducive environment for scale up or level up of such opportunities in the communities and in district.
  • Lead Business recovery and livelihood recovery program with fixed assets value under each category.

Prepare business case to support high-value schemes to support immediate livelihood upliftment of the community people including modes like CASH/Kind.

  • Formal documentation of the immediate livelihood need assessment is developed, shared and integrated into planning and budgeting.
  • Lead on the cash support modality with the information received from the market assessment and coordination group.

Oversee household and Community Recovery and Rehabilitation (Lead, monitor and provide necessary technical back stopping)

  • Recovery of household income sources.
  • Productive asset replacement and restoration.
  • Livelihood recovery initiatives.
  • Small enterprise recovery support.
  • Market-oriented recovery approaches.

Community Recovery and Rehabilitation

  • Community asset rehabilitation.
  • Community infrastructure restoration.
  • Small-scale recovery projects.
  • Community-based resilience strengthening initiatives.

Employment and Cash-Based Programming

  • Cash-for-Work activities.
  • Temporary employment opportunities.
  • Community rehabilitation schemes.
  • Environmentally responsible recovery approaches.

Resilience and Recovery Strengthening

  • Disaster-resilient recovery practices.
  • Community preparedness integration.
  • Recovery planning with affected communities.
  • Strengthening local recovery capacities.

Stakeholder’s contribution including Partner NGO is acquired during the project interventions

Partnership, Stakeholder Management & capacity building

  • Orient and provide technical guidance to Partner NGO staff on the programming tools and materials to ensure they are utilized correctly and applied during programme implementation;
  • Develop and deliver training and capacity building for Partner NGOs staffs to ensure adequate competencies at field/partner level to deliver all necessary components of the given projects/programme to ensure performance targets achieved;
  • Provide in-field support to Partner NGOs during key events to strengthen programming quality and results;
  • Lead in providing appropriate tools and techniques to Partner NGOs in order measure and update on the projects progress
  • Provide necessary training to WV and Partner NGO staff on various livelihood initiatives including CVP/CFW/ER/BR/alternative livelihood approaches (on-farm, off-farm), etc
  • Facilitate the vocational training required in the field on need and time-frame basis (categorize the type and number of days required for VT)
  • Ensure partner compliance with project agreements and donor requirements.
  • Build partner capacity in recovery programming, reporting and quality assurance.
  • Conduct regular review meetings with partners.
  • Facilitate collaborative planning and implementation processes.
  • Strengthen relationships with local stakeholders and community institutions.
  • Promote community participation throughout the project cycle.

WVI Nepal has strong relationship with the LG, various government units, stakeholders, private institutions and other relevant line agencies, take lead wherever necessary, particularly in the sector of livelihoods, food security and rehabilitation

Coordination and Representation

  • Represent WVI Nepal in district, cluster, livelihood and livestock service meetings/sectors and municipal recovery coordination mechanisms.
  • Support LG/livelihood cluster for phase and support categorization, business support plan, develop value voucher quantity and amount, description of criteria for conditional livelihood cash support, etc
  • Maintain close coordination with local governments, line agencies and humanitarian actors.
  • Participate in Early Recovery, Livelihoods and Recovery-related working groups and forums.
  • Strengthen collaboration with private sector and market actors where appropriate, validate data received from various sources and ensure effective representation of the affected communities.
  • Promote visibility of project achievements and learning.
  • The data and result appropriately depict the field level achievement, accountability mechanism is established and functional; the success and outcome of the program is demonstrated in stories and figures/data.

Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning

  • Work with WVI MEAL team and partner NGOs to ensure appropriate analysis and programme results, including sharing of results and continuous improvements of programme design, research and implementationEnsure data driven decision making approach is mainstreamed in the program planning, implementation, analysis and result sharing.
  • Provide effective handouts, reports and stories for publication both internally and externally.
  • Ensure effective monitoring systems are established and utilized.
  • Track project indicators, milestones and recovery outcomes.
  • Lead project review and reflection processes. Support assessments, surveys and evaluations.
  • Ensure community feedback and accountability mechanisms are functioning effectively.
  • Budget management and compliance is as per the standards of the donor and WVI Nepal’s requirement.

Budget, Compliance and Reporting

  • Monitor project expenditures against approved budgets.
  • Ensure that the project planned budget is on time with 95% of the burn rate.
  • Ensure efficient utilization of project resources.
  • Review financial forecasts and spending plans.
  • Ensure compliance with donor regulations, WVI Nepal policies and Government of Nepal requirements.
  • Prepare quality monthly, quarterly and donor reports.
  • Support audits, monitoring visits and project evaluations.
  • Maintain complete and accurate project documentation. undefinedundefinedundefined

Team Management and Leadership

  • Provide technical and management guidance to the project staff including the administrative business to the team and Partner NGOs
  • Lead the team by example to foster the organizational culture and best practices
  • Supervise, coach and manage the performance of the ER coordinator and other assigned recovery staff, provide technical direction, prioritization and quality assurance for economic recovery interventions.
  • Manage field visits of key stakeholders to showcase project successes and challenges
  • Perform other organizational and business processes that are required to contribute to WVI Nepal’s strategic objectives and to maintain a healthy organizational life.
  • Carry out duties as assigned by supervisor and WVI Nepal’s management.

KNOWLEDGE/QUALIFICATIONS FOR THE ROLE

Required Education, training, license, registration and certification

  • University degree or equivalent in an Agriculture/Livelihood/Food Security/Agriculture economics/Agri-business or related field Course on Livelihood programming/project models is preferred.

Required Professional Experience

  • Previous working experience as a lead in early recovery need assessment, design, implementation, and result dissemination.
  • Specialization in livelihood program approach particularly during response, early recovery and rehabilitation.
  • Working experience with private sectors; entrepreneurship development, job creations and resilient livestock shelter establishment
  • Minimum 5 years of progressive experience in development, humanitarian, recovery or resilience programming.
  • Minimum 3 years of experience managing donor-funded projects.
  • Demonstrated experience in disaster response, early recovery and community resilience programmes.
  • Experience managing local partners and consortium relationships.
  • Proven experience working with local governments and community institutions.
  • Experience in project planning, budget management and reporting.

Preferred Knowledge and Qualifications

Technical Competencies

  • Well versed with Sphere handbook, CHS and Livelihood in emergencies (LiE) program design and approach
  • Strong knowledge on enterprise/business case story development
  • Strong background on working with cooperatives, soft-loan structure and other banking and finance institution (BFI) to promote quick return business ideas
  • Understanding of Early recovery and technical skills: CVA/CFW for livelihood, assessment tools including EMMA, restoration of productive assets and quick/short cycle IG support (agriculture (on/off farm), alternative livelihood, micro-enterprise), etc with high Return on investment/high B/C ratio and lower pay-back period, etc.
  • Understanding of market system and value chains along with green enterprise and resilient agriculture/livestock systems
  • Knowledge of humanitarian-development nexus programming.
  • Experience in livelihood recovery and economic strengthening.
  • Understanding of cash-based programming and community rehabilitation approaches.
  • Knowledge of market systems and resilience programming.
  • Strong project cycle management skills.
  • Excellent monitoring, reporting and analytical skills.
  • Budget planning and financial management skills.

Other Competencies

  • Excellent coordination and stakeholder engagement skills.
  • Strong leadership and team management capability.
  • Effective negotiation and influencing skills.
  • Ability to work under emergency and post-disaster contexts.
  • Strong problem-solving and decision-making skills.
  • High level of integrity and accountability. “

World Vision is committed to achieving diversity, as the diversity of our teams is critical to our overall success. WV welcomes applications from qualified professionals all over Nepal. Women, people with disability, and members from other marginalized groups are strongly encouraged to apply.”“Children and vulnerable adults who come into contact with WV as a result of our activities must be safeguarded to the maximum possible extent from deliberate or inadvertent actions and failings that place them at risk of abuse, sexual exploitation, injury, and any other harm. One of the ways that WVI Nepal shows this on-going commitment to safeguarding is to include rigorous background and reference checks in the selection process for all candidates, in accordance to its Child and Adult Safeguarding Policy. WVI Nepal has zero tolerance to child rights’ violations, by employees and/or affiliates.”

WVI Nepal reserves all rights to qualify/disqualify applications in any case.

1. Organization Overview

Women’s Rehabilitation Centre (WOREC) Founded in 1991, Women’s Rehabilitation Centre (WOREC) is a national level leading NGO working in Nepal from local to global level with feminist values to support and bridge collective actions for women rights and feminist movement. Together with collaborators from a diverse range of feminist human rights movements and networks, WOREC works to advance the rights of women in diversity. WOREC advocates for affirmative structural and social changes influencing national and international actors. WOREC works for the protection and promotion of women’s human rights and social justice with the campaigns against violence against women, and women’s economic, social and cultural rights.

WOREC is active nation-wide by its presence with central office in Lalitpur, provincial and district offices in 6 provinces. WOREC is currently looking for a dynamic and competent candidate to fulfill the position of Program Director at Central Office based in Balkumari, Lalitpur. The position reports to the Executive Director and is responsible for overall execution ensuring organizational vision, mission, goals and objectives.

2. Position Summary

The Program Director will provide overall leadership, strategic direction, coordination and management of assigned programs and projects, ensuring effective implementation in line with WOREC’s organizational vision, mission, values, approved project documents and donor requirements.

The position will lead engagement with federal, provincial and local governments, relevant ministries, development partners, civil society organizations, women-led organizations, networks and other stakeholders to strengthen integrated Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights (SRHR) and Gender-Based Violence (GBV) services, policies, systems, financing and accountability mechanisms.

The position will be based in Kathmandu and may require frequent travel to project sites, field offices and other locations based on program requirements and emerging needs.

Position: Disaster Response Coordinator
Department: Program
Reporting Line: Program Manager/Executive Director
Location: Rasuwa/Nuwakot/Dhading and other disaster-affected areas with frequent travel
Level: Coordinator
Required Number: 01

1. Organization Overview:

Women’s Rehabilitation Centre (WOREC) Founded in 1991, Women’s Rehabilitation Centre (WOREC) is a national level leading NGO working in Nepal from local to global level with feminist values to support and bridge collective actions for women rights and feminist movement. Together with collaborators from a diverse range of feminist human rights movements and networks, WOREC works to advance the rights of women in diversity. WOREC advocates for affirmative structural and social changes influencing national and international actors. WOREC works for the protection and promotion of women’s human rights and social justice with the campaigns against violence against women, and women’s economic, social and cultural rights.

WOREC is active nation-wide by its presence with central office in Lalitpur, provincial and district offices in 6 provinces. WOREC is currently looking for a dynamic and competent candidate to fulfill the position of Disaster Response Coordinator. The position reports to the Program Manager/Executive Director and is responsible for overall execution ensuring organizational vision, mission, goals and objectives.

2. Position Summary:

The Disaster Response Coordinator will coordinate WOREC’s protection-focused disaster response in flood- and disaster-affected areas, ensuring the safety, dignity, rights, and protection of women, girls, children, adolescents, persons with disabilities, and other vulnerable groups. The position will coordinate field-level response with local government, communities, service providers, partners, and humanitarian actors, and support protection assessments, GBV prevention and response, referrals, community-based protection, and safe/women-friendly spaces. The position will also oversee field coordination, monitoring, documentation, reporting, and learning, applying WOREC’s feminist, gender-responsive, rights-based, survivor-centered, and inclusive approaches.

3. Preferred Discipline / Areas/Specialization:

To coordinate effective, timely, and protection-focused disaster response for women, girls, children, adolescents, and vulnerable and marginalized communities affected by floods and other disasters through protection assessment, prevention and response to violence, referral and support services, community engagement, local-level coordination, and evidence-based response planning.

4. Main Roles & Responsibilities:

R.1. Disaster Response Planning and Coordination:

  • Coordinate the overall implementation of WOREC’s protection-focused disaster response activities in assigned disaster-affected areas.
  • Develop field-level response plans and priorities based on identified protection needs, risks, and available resources.
  • Coordinate timely implementation of response activities in accordance with approved plans, project requirements, and WOREC’s policies and procedures.
  • Regularly assess changing needs and protection concerns and recommend appropriate response actions to the Program Manager.
  • Ensure that disaster response activities are inclusive, participatory, gender-responsive, and accessible to affected communities.
  • Coordinate with relevant WOREC teams to ensure timely administrative, financial, logistical, MEAL, and technical support for response activities.

R.2. Protection Assessment and Risk Identification:

  • Conduct and coordinate rapid protection assessments in flood- and disaster-affected communities to identify the protection needs, risks, and priority concerns of women, girls, children, adolescents, persons with disabilities, older persons, and other vulnerable groups.
  • Monitor, collect, and analyze information on protection risks, including GBV, sexual exploitation and abuse, trafficking, child protection concerns, discrimination, exclusion, unsafe shelters, and barriers to essential services.
  • Document and communicate key protection findings and emerging needs to relevant WOREC teams and stakeholders, and support timely adjustment of response activities based on changing protection risks and priorities.

R.3. Protection from Gender-Based Violence and Violence against Women:

  • Coordinate prevention and response activities related to gender-based violence and violence against women and girls in disaster-affected communities.
  • Ensure that GBV-related concerns identified during the response are handled in a safe, confidential, survivor-centered, and non-discriminatory manner.
  • Strengthen community awareness on GBV prevention, available services, protection mechanisms, and referral pathways.
  • Coordinate with relevant service providers for psychosocial, health, legal, protection, and other required support.
  • Support community-based mechanisms to identify and address protection risks faced by women and girls.
  • Ensure that response activities do not increase the risk of violence, exploitation, abuse, or discrimination.

R.4. Referral, Case Support and Service Linkages:

  • Coordinate and strengthen referral pathways and maintain updated mapping of government and non-government service providers, including health, psychosocial, legal, police, shelter, and other relevant services.
  • Support community mobilizers and staff to identify protection concerns, make appropriate referrals, and ensure timely follow-up while respecting confidentiality, dignity, and survivors’ choices.
  • Ensure referral and case-related information is handled securely and in line with WOREC’s safeguarding, confidentiality, and data protection requirements.

R.5. Women-Friendly and Safe Spaces:

  • Coordinate the establishment, operation, strengthening, and monitoring of safe and women-friendly spaces, ensuring safe, accessible, inclusive, and confidential services.
  • Ensure women, girls, children, and vulnerable groups have meaningful access to information, support, services, and participation, and recommend improvements based on feedback and identified needs.
  • Coordinate and represent WOREC with local government, humanitarian organizations, UN agencies, NGOs, civil society organizations, and other relevant stakeholders in response meetings and forums.
  • Share relevant protection priorities and gaps while maintaining confidentiality, and identify opportunities for collaboration to strengthen service coverage and avoid duplication.

R.8. Field Team Coordination and Capacity Building:

  • Coordinate and provide regular guidance to community mobilizers, field staff, volunteers, and response team members on their roles, responsibilities, and response protocols.
  • Orient and support field teams on protection principles, GBV prevention and response, safeguarding, confidentiality, referral mechanisms, and survivor-centered approaches.
  • Identify capacity-building needs, support relevant training and coaching, and regularly review field performance to ensure quality implementation.

R.9. Monitoring, Documentation and Reporting:

  • Monitor the implementation, quality, coverage, and progress of disaster response and protection activities through regular field visits, follow-up, and verification against plans and targets.
  • Maintain accurate and confidential records and document response activities, protection concerns, referrals, achievements, challenges, good practices, and lessons learned.
  • Prepare timely situation updates and reports, and provide relevant information and evidence to the Program Manager and WOREC teams for decision-making and program improvement.

R.10. Accountability, Safeguarding and Community Feedback:

  • Promote accountability to affected populations through safe and accessible feedback mechanisms, ensuring community concerns and recommendations are documented, communicated, and appropriately followed up.
  • Maintain strict confidentiality and protection of sensitive information, ensuring compliance with WOREC’s safeguarding standards and zero-tolerance approach to violence, exploitation, abuse, harassment, and discrimination, while upholding the dignity, rights, safety, choices, and informed participation of affected people.

R.11. Coordination with MEAL, Finance, Administration and Other Teams:

  • Coordinate with MEAL, Finance, Administration, and relevant WOREC teams for monitoring, data verification, documentation, financial and narrative reporting, procurement, logistics, transportation, and other operational requirements.
  • Provide accurate program information and supporting documents, address operational challenges, and contribute to regular program review and planning based on field evidence and protection needs.

R.12. Advocacy, Learning and Organizational Engagement:

  • Identify and communicate protection gaps and emerging issues, and support WOREC’s advocacy and campaigns on women’s rights, protection, GBV prevention, disaster response, and social justice.
  • Contribute field-based evidence, lessons learned, case studies, good practices, and knowledge products to strengthen WOREC’s disaster response, preparedness, and organizational learning.

4. Required Qualifications and Experience:

  • Master’s degree or equivalent in Disaster Management, Development Studies, Social Sciences, Gender Studies, Human Rights,
  • Social Work, Public Health, or related field, with at least 5 years of relevant experience.
  • Additionally Practical experience in humanitarian/disaster response, protection, GBV, community-based protection, referrals, and stakeholder coordination.
  • Strong knowledge of protection, safeguarding, gender-responsive and survivor-centered approaches, with experience in field coordination, team supervision, assessment, and reporting.
  • Willingness to undertake frequent travel and field deployment in disaster-affected areas.

5. Core Competencies:

Strong experience in disaster response, protection, and humanitarian coordination; knowledge of GBV prevention and response, safeguarding, protection, and survivor-centered approaches; strong assessment, planning, monitoring, reporting, communication, stakeholder engagement, team coordination, and problem-solving skills; ability to work effectively under pressure and coordinate with government, humanitarian actors, service providers, communities, and partners; understanding of feminist, gender-responsive, human rights, and social justice approaches; bilingual proficiency and willingness to undertake frequent travel and field deployment.

  • Comply with WOREC’s policies, procedures, safeguarding standards and organizational values.
  • Demonstrate professional conduct, accountability and respect in all interactions.
  • Contribute to a safe, inclusive, respectful and learning-oriented organizational environment.

Key Responsibilities:

The ED’s specific tasks will include, but not be limited to: Play strong roles to upgrade organizational goal, objectives, vision, mission long and short-term development plans and policies as per the changing context.

A. Organizational Strategy, Vision and Policy Development

Rural Women Upliftment Association (RWUA), established on 22 Kartik 2050 B.S. in Sarlahi District, Madhesh Province, Nepal, is a non-governmental, non-profit social organization working for women’s empowerment, child rights and protection, education, health, livelihoods, and community development. With more than 34 years of experience in community development and social transformation, RWUA has been implementing various development programmes in partnership with national and international development organizations. RWUA, in partnership with Save the Children under the SAMUNNATI Sponsorship Programme, invites applications from qualified, competent, committed, and motivated Nepali citizens for the following position:

Position: Field Officer Education – 1

Project: SAMUNNATI (Sponsorship) Programme

Level: Officer

Duty Station: Haripur and Ishworpur Municipalities, Sarlahi

Working Area: Haripur and Ishworpur Municipalities, Sarlahi

Reports To: Field Coordinator

Employment Type: Project-based

Field Engagement: Approximately 90% field implementation and 10% coordination, reporting, and documentation

Position Summary

The Field Officer Education will be responsible for the overall implementation, monitoring, supervision, documentation, and reporting of education-related activities under the SAMUNNATI Sponsorship Programme. The position holder will provide technical support, coaching, mentoring, and capacity building to teachers, ECCD and Basic school teacher, School Management Committees (SMCs), Parent-Teacher Associations (PTAs), community volunteers, parents, and children. The Field Officer will particularly support ECCD, basic education, literacy, numeracy, child-friendly learning, school enrollment, retention, and quality education initiatives and will work closely with schools, communities, local governments, and other stakeholders. 90% field based

Major Responsibilities

  • Plan and implement education activities according to the Sponsorship Annual Plan (SAP), Detailed Implementation Plan (DIP), and approved project standards.
  • Provide technical support, coaching, mentoring, and supervision to teachers, ECCD facilitators, SMC/PTA members, volunteers, parents, and children.
  • Facilitate ECCD, basic education, literacy, numeracy, reading clubs, and safe-school activities.
  • Conduct regular monitoring and supervision visits to schools, ECCD centres, and communities.
  • Support teachers in developing age-appropriate lesson plans and improving classroom practices.
  • Organize and facilitate training, orientation, workshops, meetings, and community-level education activities.
  • Support school enrollment, retention, regular attendance, and learning improvement initiatives.
  • Prepare and support implementation of Individual Education Plans (IEPs) for school-at-home children.
  • Coordinate with headteachers, teachers, SMC/PTA members, local government education authorities, parents, and community stakeholders.
  • Collect, verify, manage, and report programme data accurately through OPMIS and other relevant systems.
  • Support assessments, surveys, research, MEAL activities, and programme reviews.
  • Prepare monthly, quarterly, semi-annual, and annual reports.
  • Document best practices, lessons learned, case studies, and success stories.
  • Prepare at least one case story and one success story every month.
  • Support the timely procurement and distribution of educational and learning materials.
  • Ensure programme activities are implemented according to quality standards and donor requirements.
  • Address MEAL feedback and recommendations in a timely manner.
  • Support advocacy, networking, coordination, and policy-related activities related to education.
  • Represent in meetings, workshops, coordination forums, and other events as assigned.
  • Support humanitarian and emergency response activities when required.
  • Promote gender equality, inclusion, diversity, child protection, climate resilience, and the Do No Harm approach.
  • Perform other duties assigned by the line manager.

Child Safeguarding and Protection

  • The position holder will have frequent direct contact with children and young people and must strictly comply with RWUA and Save the Children safeguarding standards. The selected candidate will be required to:
  • Follow child safeguarding and protection policies.
  • Comply with PSEAH (Protection from Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Harassment) requirements.
  • Follow the RWUA Code of Conduct and Do No Harm Policy.
  • Follow the dual-adult rule when interacting with children.
  • Report safeguarding and child protection concerns through established mechanisms.
  • Ensure appropriate visibility and implementation of child protection policies at programme sites.

Minimum Qualification and Experience

Minimum qualification: Bachelor’s Degree in Education (B.Ed.) with at least five years of relevant officer-level experience in education programmes, particularly ECCD, basic education, integrated development, and stakeholder engagement. Experience working with NGOs/INGOs, schools, local governments, teachers, SMCs/PTAs, and communities, as well as knowledge of the local language, will be an advantage

Required Skills and Competencies

  • Strong facilitation, training, coaching, and mentoring skills.
  • Excellent communication, coordination, and interpersonal skills.
  • Strong report writing and documentation skills in Nepali and English.
  • Ability to prepare reports in Nepali (Preeti font) and English (Times New Roman).
  • Good knowledge of MEAL, monitoring, data collection, validation, and reporting systems.
  • Proficiency in MS Office, particularly MS Word, Excel, and PowerPoint, and internet applications.
  • Ability to develop activity plans and support programme budgeting.
  • Ability to work effectively with government authorities, schools, communities, and development partners.
  • Ability to work independently and effectively as part of a team.
  • Willingness to work extensively in rural, remote, and field-based locations.
  • Strong commitment to child rights, safeguarding, gender equality, inclusion, and organizational values.

Other Conditions

  • The selected candidate must be willing to spend approximately 90% of working time in the field.
  • Staff assigned to Haripur and Ishworpur Municipalities are expected to reside within their respective assigned working areas, except during approved leave, holidays, or official assignments.
  • Applicants must be reliable, accountable, committed, and willing to work in diverse cultural and rural contexts.
  • RWUA follows a merit-based and equal-opportunity recruitment process.
  • RWUA maintains a strict zero-tolerance policy toward fraud, bribery, safeguarding violations, and other unethical practices.

Application Procedure

Qualified Nepali candidates aged 20 to under 45 years are encouraged to apply by submitting an updated CV, a cover letter, and their expected salary to vacancy@rwua.org or by delivering a hard copy to the HR Department, RWUA, Haripur-02, Sarlahi. Priority will be given to qualified local women, persons with disabilities (PWDs), individuals from disadvantaged and marginalized communities, and LGBTQI+ applicants. Candidates who have already applied for this position are requested not to submit again. The application deadline is 25 October 2026, at 5:00 PM. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. Telephone inquiries regarding this vacancy will not be entertained.
