Position: Project Manager (Climate Change Adaptation)
Location: Kusunti, KC Tower, Lalitpur, Nepal
End Date: October 18, 2026

With 75 years of experience, our focus is on helping the most vulnerable children overcome poverty and experience fullness of life. We help children of all backgrounds, even in the most dangerous places, inspired by our Christian faith.

Come join our 31,000+ staff working in nearly 100 countries and share the joy of transforming vulnerable children’s life stories!

Employee Contract Type: Local – Fixed Term Employee (Fixed Term)

Job Description:

The Project Manager will be responsible for leading the implementation of an Australian funded Climate Change Adaptation project in Sudurpaschim and Karnali provinces, which aims to strengthen the climate resilience and economic empowerment of the poorest and most vulnerable HHs, communities, and local enterprises. The project will test, adapt and innovate locally led climate adaptation approaches that can be scaled and sustained by the Government of Nepal and Nepali stakeholders. The project focuses on four areas:

Area 1: Adaptation and resilience models for effective local climate actions

Area 2: Economic and social empowerment to increase adaptation and resilience of the most vulnerable

Area 3: Improved collective action and institution building

Area 4: Improved capacity of subnational governments to effectively plan, resource, and implement inclusive, evidence-based climate actions to increase climate and disaster resilience among vulnerable communities

A central focus of the role is to lead the consortium of three national NGOs, World Vision and a knowledge partner to successfully implement this four-years project. This includes participating in the project steering committees representing all partners and liaising with World Vision Australia and DFAT.

The Project Manager is also expected to technically lead in one of the four above-mentioned focus areas, possibly the capacity strengthening and engagement of the subnational government.

In leading project operations, the Project manager will ensure strong planning, coordination, and compliance with donor requirements, including those of partners. This includes standard, timely high-quality reporting, financial and supply chain management, policy adherence, managing teams and partners, strengthening monitoring and data systems. The role also emphasizes adaptive management—using data insights to guide informed decisions, improve performance, and inform strategic direction. Ability to make critical decisions in a timely manner and to ensure alignment of the project with WVI Nepal country strategy and ongoing long term programing are essential, in addition to maintain strong donor relations.

Additionally, the Project Manager will foster a supportive team environment, prioritizing staff wellbeing, capacity development, and partner strengthening to ensure effective, accountable, and impactful project delivery. Emotional intelligence is duly taken into consideration while managing and engaging with people and stakeholders.

MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES

Project Management

  • Project commences on time, delivers results per plans and budgets, and is implemented per quality benchmarks, donor guidelines and requirements, government regulations, and organizational policies and procedures.
  • Provide overall managerial leadership to, and ensure technical leadership and competency in the Climate Change Adaptation project offering the necessary support to project team and partner organizations.
  • Lead the projects strategic, financial, and operational planning and implementation, including the annual work planning process, budgeting, partnership management and development of an appropriate project exit strategy.
  • Orientate and equip project staff and partners on project requirements and compliances, ensuring project team has access to appropriate information, tools and resources to enable compliance with organizational standards and legal requirements in all areas, including financial management, supply chain management, people and project management
  • Oversee timely submission of all deliverables to management and donor, including written and financial reports (monthly, quarterly and annually), and other key documents
  • Conduct quarterly review of project, identify and manage project risks, issues and challenges, prepare mitigation measures, recommend vital changes if any, and communicate timely to supervisor and concerned authorities
  • Integrate social and environmental safeguarding, GEDSI, and ‘Do No Harm’ as cross-cutting themes for broader impact. Ensure all
  • Safeguarding requirements are maintained as per WVI and donor standards
  • Monitor risk and implement mitigation measures

Partnership Management, Capacity Building and Coordination

  • Facilitate and ensure adequate capacity of project team and partners to deliver their roles and responsibilities.
  • Together with partners development of strategic external relationships, partnerships and engagement with key stakeholders at National, Provincial and Local Level.
  • Close cooperation with the Deputy Team Leader / Deputy Project Manager who sits in a partner NGO. The Deputy Team Leader /
  • Deputy Project Manager is Technical Lead and responsible for leading technical quality and MEAL.
  • Provide technical support to partners in a technical area relevant to the four focal areas of this project.
  • Manage partner NGOs’ performance to ensure project results are delivered as per the agreed MOAs, plans, budgets, quality benchmarks, donor guidelines and requirements, government regulations, and organizational policies and procedures.
  • Conduct regular meetings with partner NGO to ensure expected requirements, corrective actions from project monitoring and tracking are taken up, and action plans followed
  • Ensure adequate strengthening of partner NGOs’ management, technical and functional capacity to achieve Rise in Nepal’s deliverables, including reaching the target population and the most vulnerable children as per project design
  • Review monthly progress and plans of implementing partners and provide necessary support for planning, monitoring and implementations of project activities

MEAL and Information Management

  • Ensure quality monitoring and report submission. Develop and apply appropriate tools and strategies to monitor progress, quality and impact of project targets and ensure accountability.
  • Ensure partner NGO roll out effective MEAL mechanisms with learnings incorporated into program implementation.
  • Ensure partner NGO’s effective project database set up and management, including timely data entry, verification and effective data utilization for project learning, adaptation and preparation of project reports/infographic on progress and entry in IMPAQ.
  • Manage knowledge and learning to capture lessons, best practices, and case studies to support program improvement and institutional learning.
  • Develop Communications Plan that captures evidence (such as project brief, media coverage, visibility materials, and success/change stories) of good practices on a regular basis.
  • Ensure the Information Management (IM) system is established for data collection, storage, analysis and reporting

Financial Management

  • Ensure effective and efficient utilization of program resources through monitoring and tracking expenditures against project plan. Lead budget revision if needed.
  • Provide project financial oversight and ensure accurate financial reporting. Monitor monthly expenditures and compare with implementation plan, budget requirements and provide variance explanation.
  • Ensure that milestone payments are completed on time as per the WVI Nepal’s standard on the pre-financing and advance settlement process.
  • Ensure 100% compliance of donor finance and procurement policies.
  • Ensure internal control mechanisms are in place, and Limited Risk is obtained in internal, project and Global Center audits.
  • Oversee timely procurement and risk based monitoring of all partners
  • Review and document donor requirements and checklists and orientate WVI Nepal departments as required.

Donor Relationship & Compliance

  • Represent the project in donor forums and technical coordination platforms
  • Maintain regular communication with donor focal points, organize review meetings, field visits, and donor briefings, managing donor expectations and incorporate feedback.
  • Ensure adherence to donor rules, regulations, and reporting formats, including compliance in procurement, finance, and contracting processes and submission of timely narrative and financial reporting
  • Review and edit key project reports (semi-annual, annual), design documents and other programme output documents as per the donor prescribed format and checklists.
  • Maintain proper documentation and audit trails and support internal/external audits and compliance reviews

Team management and leadership

  • Provide technical and administrative guidance to project staff at WVI Nepal and partner NGOs
  • Facilitate learning, coaching and mentoring to team members with clear performance expectations and individual learning plans outlined in performance appraisals,
  • Lead by example to foster accountability, agility, team spirit and strategic leadership.
  • Create working atmosphere that inspires and motivates staff to pursue excellent performance and integrity. Promote diversity, openness, safe environment to enhance open culture and maintain team dynamics.
  • Manage in ensuring safety and security of WVI Nepal’s staff and assets as per Core Security Requirements and policies.
  • Familiarize self and project team with WVI Nepal’s country strategy, technical programs, projects, policies and guidelines, including adherence to adult and child safeguarding.
  • Manage field visits of key stakeholders to showcase project successes and challenges
  • Perform other organizational and business processes that are required to contribute to WVI Nepal’s strategic objectives and to maintain a healthy organizational life. Carry out duties as assigned by supervisor and WVI Nepal’s management.

KNOWLEDGE/QUALIFICATIONS FOR THE ROLE

Required Education, training, license, registration and certification

  • Master’s degree in environmental studies, social science studies, agriculture or other relevant disciplines

Required Professional Experience

  • At least 10 years management experience in national and/or international NGOs, including grants management.
  • Demonstrated depth of experience and expertise preferably in an NGO context in working with climate change adaptation programming.
  • Demonstrated experience of leading/ managing multiple partners-based projects at different levels.
  • Demonstrated understanding of donor compliance
  • Extensive experience and recognized expertise in models and methods of training, facilitation and capacity building, project management and organizational development for staff, communities and government stakeholders.
  • Technical knowledge of one of the four focus areas of this project – mentioned above.
  • Thorough understanding and experience about Nepal Government’s strategies, policies, guidelines on climate change action, climate financing and climate related programming.
  • Strategic, creative, and innovative thinking, solves problems with prudent decision making. Effective people management with emotional intelligence.
  • Demonstrated experience in capacity building and different approaches to building capacity of partners, staff and organizational competencies.
  • High level of fluency in Nepali and English language (reading, writing, speaking)
  • Experience in using logical frameworks and project monitoring
  • Implementation of child protection policy and social and environmental safeguarding practices

Preferred Knowledge and Qualifications

  • Expert knowledge of climate change adaptation
  • Very good experiences in using digital platforms
  • Work experience in INGO in the relevant area is preferred.
  • Team building, collaboration, facilitation and leadership skills
  • Demonstrated networking, partnership and coordination ability
  • Excellent problem-solving skills and detail orientation
  • Able to work under pressure
  • Demonstrate understanding of and commitment to World Vision’s Core Values in the approach to work and relationships
  • Willingness to work outside office hours especially when traveling and working with partners and communities.
  • Skilled in MS office applications

Duration: One year (with possibility of extension)

Travel and/or Work Environment

Travel to field for around 50% of work time.

ABOUT HEALING TOGETHER

Healing Together Nepal builds the power of everyday people to disrupt generational cycles of trauma and violence. Our mental health and trauma-informed care workshops and support groups democratize access to community-centered, peer-led healing resources—so communities disproportionately impacted by trauma can reclaim their inherent strength, wisdom, resilience, and power to heal themselves and others.

To date, we’ve facilitated trainings with 3000+ community leaders from various districts of Nepal, who support over 300,000 trauma survivors in their communities.

We are seeking a passionate, highly self-motivated, multi-talented professional who can assist in administration and trainings, so we can grow and scale our impact and co-create the movement for mental health and healing justice in a way that is thoughtful, equitable, adaptable, and sustainable in the midst of a rapidly changing environment.

Our ideal candidate has a proven track record of executing and completing projects from start to finish, with a real knack for working around obstacles to get things done, while maintaining a sense of humor, grace, and humility, and prioritizing relational care and alignment with our Guiding Principles.

We encourage and seek applications from individuals who identify as women, marginalized, and/or are members of the LGBTQ community. Applicants shall not be discriminated against because of race, religion, sex, national origin, ethnicity, age, disability, political affiliation, sexual orientation, gender identity, color, marital status, or medical condition.

Employee Contract Type: Local – Fixed Term Employee (Fixed Term)

Job Description:

The Early Recovery Coordinator will provide overall leadership, management, technical oversight, coordination and quality assurance for the implementation of the RISE Rapid Activation Project supporting flood-affected households and communities in Rasuwa and Nuwakot districts.

The position is responsible for ensuring timely, effective and accountable delivery of early recovery interventions that help affected households restore their livelihoods, recover productive assets, rehabilitate community infrastructure, improve access to income-generating opportunities, strengthen resilience, and accelerate the transition from humanitarian response to sustainable recovery.

The incumbent will provide strategic, technical and operational leadership for the RISE Rapid Activation Project, supporting flood-affected households and communities in Rasuwa and Nuwakot to transition from humanitarian assistance toward sustainable recovery. The role will lead integrated, market-informed and climate/disaster-resilient recovery programming focused on restoring livelihoods and productive assets, rehabilitating critical community infrastructure, generating employment and strengthening household and community resilience. The position will ensure recovery interventions are locally led, inclusive, accountable and aligned with Government of Nepal priorities, donor requirements, humanitarian standards and WVI Nepal policies.

The role will coordinate closely with local government authorities, implementing partners, community groups, and technical stakeholders to ensure integrated, community-driven and market-oriented recovery programming while maintaining compliance with donor, government and World Vision policies and standards.

MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES

Project is implemented with quality, time and budget.

Project Leadership and Management

  • Lead planning, implementation, monitoring and completion of all Early Recovery Project activities.
  • Ensure project objectives, outputs and outcomes are achieved within approved timelines and budgets.
  • Develop annual, quarterly and monthly implementation plans.
  • Coordinate implementation across Rasuwa and Nuwakot districts.
  • Provide overall technical and operational support to project staff and partners.
  • Ensure quality programming aligned with Sphere Standards, humanitarian principles and World Vision standards.
  • Identify implementation risks and develop mitigation measures.
  • Facilitate adaptive management based on emerging needs and lessons learned.

Technical input is provided for the project intervention where the community and household will get benefit from the project interventions

Early Recovery Programme Implementation

Lead and oversee integrated recovery interventions including:

Early Recovery Strategy

  • Ensure the rapid assessment and recovery needs are conducted for the appropriate plan and interventions
  • Ensure rehabilitation and livelihood recovery interventions and apply Building Better Back principles, climate and disaster-risk considerations, environmental safeguarding, and risk-informed site selection to reduce future exposure and vulnerability
  • Ensure and support basic hazard and risk screening of community rehabilitation activities, integrate flood, landslide and climate risks into recovery planning, promote action on nature-positive recovery
  • Supporting and working with local government/authorities to lead recovery prioritization, planning, implementation oversight and monitoring

Household Economic Recovery

  • Plan, implement and ensure Recovery of household income sources.
  • Productive asset replacement and restoration.
  • Livelihood recovery initiatives.
  • Small enterprise recovery support.
  • Market-oriented recovery approaches.

Community Recovery and Rehabilitation

  • Community asset rehabilitation.
  • Community infrastructure restoration.
  • Small-scale recovery projects.
  • Community-based resilience strengthening initiatives.

Employment and Cash-Based Programming

  • Cash-for-Work activities.
  • Temporary employment opportunities.
  • Community rehabilitation schemes.
  • Environmentally responsible recovery approaches.

Resilience and Recovery Strengthening

  • Disaster-resilient recovery practices.
  • Community preparedness integration.
  • Recovery planning with affected communities.
  • Strengthening local recovery capacities.

Stakeholder’s contribution including partner NGO is acquired during the project interventions

Partnership and Stakeholder Management

  • Provide management and technical oversight to implementing partners.
  • Ensure partner compliance with project agreements and donor requirements.
  • Build partner capacity in recovery programming, reporting and quality assurance.
  • Conduct regular review meetings with partners.
  • Facilitate collaborative planning and implementation processes.
  • Strengthen relationships with local stakeholders and community institutions.
  • Promote community participation throughout the project cycle.

Information sharing and coordination in the districts is smooths and WVI Nepal is positioned for the strong relationships

Coordination and Representation

  • Represent World Vision in district and municipal recovery coordination mechanisms.
  • Maintain close coordination with local governments, line agencies and humanitarian actors.
  • Participate in Early Recovery, Livelihoods and Recovery-related working groups and forums.
  • Support alignment of project interventions with district and municipal recovery plans.
  • Strengthen collaboration with private sector and market actors where appropriate.
  • Promote visibility of project achievements and learning.

Project accountability and compliance is adhered throughout the project

Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning

  • Ensure effective monitoring systems are established and utilized.
  • Track project indicators, milestones and recovery outcomes.
  • Lead project review and reflection processes.
  • Support assessments, surveys and evaluations.
  • Ensure community feedback and accountability mechanisms are functioning effectively.
  • Document project learning, success stories and best practices.
  • Promote evidence-based decision-making.

Project budget and finance is managed according to the requirements.

Budget, Compliance and Reporting

  • Monitor project expenditures against approved budgets.
  • Ensure efficient utilization of project resources.
  • Review financial forecasts and spending plans.
  • Ensure compliance with donor regulations, World Vision policies and Government of Nepal requirements.
  • Prepare quality monthly, quarterly and donor reports.
  • Support audits, monitoring visits and project evaluations.
  • Maintain complete and accurate project documentation.

KNOWLEDGE/QUALIFICATIONS FOR THE ROLE

Required Education, training, license, registration and certification

  • Master’s Degree in Rural Development, Development Studies, Disaster Management, Agriculture, Economics, Social Sciences, Community Development, International Development or related field.

Required Professional Experience

  • Minimum 5 years of progressive experience in development, humanitarian, recovery or resilience programming.
  • Minimum 3 years of experience managing donor-funded projects.
  • Demonstrated experience in disaster response, early recovery and community resilience programmes.
  • Experience managing local partners and consortium relationships.
  • Proven experience working with local governments and community institutions.
  • Experience in project planning, budget management and reporting.

Preferred Knowledge and Qualifications

Technical Competencies

  • Strong understanding of Early Recovery programming approaches.
  • Knowledge of humanitarian-development nexus programming.
  • Experience in livelihood recovery and economic strengthening.
  • Understanding of cash-based programming and community rehabilitation approaches.
  • Knowledge of market systems and resilience programming.
  • Strong project cycle management skills.
  • Excellent monitoring, reporting and analytical skills.
  • Budget planning and financial management skills.

Other Competencies

  • Excellent coordination and stakeholder engagement skills.
  • Strong leadership and team management capability.
  • Effective negotiation and influencing skills.
  • Ability to work under emergency and post-disaster contexts.
  • Strong problem-solving and decision-making skills.
  • High level of integrity and accountability.

Local Initiatives for Biodiversity, Research, and Development (LI-BIRD) is a non-profit, non-governmental organization established in October 1995 with its Head Office in Pokhara and Programme Coordination Office in Lalitpur. LI-BIRD is committed to capitalizing on local initiatives for sustainable management of renewable natural resources and improving the livelihoods of rural people in Nepal.

LI-BIRD offers a collegial and supportive working environment where young professionals with a learning attitude thrive and succeed. LI-BIRD provides unparalleled mentoring support while challenging its staff to learn, innovate and acquire skills and experiences that will become foundational for the rest of their careers.

Transitioning to Agroecological Production (TAP) is a regional project funded by the International Fund for Agriculture Development (IFAD) for implementation in Nepal, Bhutan and Pakistan for the period of 3 years. In Nepal, the project will be implemented in Karnali, Sudurpaschim and Lumbini Provinces to support the IFAD funded Resilient High Value Agriculture Program (RHVAP), the Nepal Government’s flagship programme under the Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Environment (MoAFE). The TAP project aims to support transition to commercially viable agroecological systems and strengthen the economic resilience of smallholder farmers through promotion and scaling of agroecological farming systems in the region. The project will seek to accelerate on farm agroecological transformation while strengthening the market, knowledge and institutional systems required to sustain and scale agroecological practices within ongoing investment projects in Nepal, Bhutan and Pakistan. While project implementation in each country will be led by the respective implementing partners, LI-BIRD will be responsible for overall coordination and project management. The project will promote collaboration, learning and knowledge exchange among the three countries while ensuring effective planning, implementation, monitoring, financial oversight, reporting and accountability at both national and regional levels.

LI-BIRD invites applications from eligible and qualified Nepali citizens who are committed and have the ability to deliver results with the highest integrity for the position.

Team Leader (Level 11) – (1): To be based at Programme Coordination Office, Sanepa, Lalitpur

Job Summary: Reporting to the Head of Programmes (HoP), the Team Leader will provide overall strategic, technical, and managerial leadership for the project, ensuring effective partnership, coordination, planning, implementation, monitoring, financial oversight, quality assurance, reporting, and compliance. The Team Leader will lead the Nepal project team and coordinate closely with the funding agency, implementing partners, Nepal Government’s flagship RHVAP programme, and provincial government, and other relevant stakeholders. At the regional level, the position will provide strategic coordination, technical support, and oversight to partners in Bhutan and Pakistan, including joint planning, progress and results tracking, reporting and compliance, and cross-country learning and knowledge exchange. The position will also support the Capacity Development and Knowledge Management Expert in generation, documentation, and dissemination of evidence and knowledge to support agroecological transformation and strengthen regional collaboration and learning.

Education and Experience: Master’s degree in agriculture, agroecology, agribusiness management or related field with at least 7 years of relevant experience in management, implementation and monitoring projects related to agriculture, agroecology, agri-value chains. Candidates with a demonstrated track record of developing technical guidelines, manuals, Palika agriculture strategy and delivering trainings and having experience working closely with government systems and managing consortium projects is an advantage and are encouraged to apply.

Mission and objectives

The United Nations World Food Programme (WFP) is the world’s largest humanitarian agency fighting hunger worldwide. The mission of WFP is to help the world achieve Zero Hunger in our lifetimes. Position: Project Officer

The Organisation

Plan International is an independent development and humanitarian organisation that advances children’s rights and equality for girls. We believe in the power and potential of every child but know this is often suppressed by poverty, violence, exclusion and discrimination. And it is girls who are most affected.

Working together with children, young people, supporters and partners, we strive for a just world, tackling the root causes of the challenges girls and vulnerable children face. We support children’s rights from birth until they reach adulthood and we enable children to prepare for and respond to crises and adversity. We drive changes in practice and policy at local, national and global levels using our reach, experience and knowledge.

For over 85 years, we have rallied other determined optimists to transform the lives of all children in more than 80 countries.

We won’t stop until we are all equal.

ROLE PURPOSE

The Project Officer (PO) (herein referred as PO) will implement the “Bhotekoshi Flash Flood Response Project” The project will be implemented by local NGO partner in Nuwakot, Rasuwa and Dhading district. The position is responsible to lead the project in implementing, monitoring and control and closure of the project including reporting within donor compliance. The position shall maintain close coordination with internal team, local implementing partner, provincial donor focal person, EDP’s, other key stakeholders including local government.

In adherence to Plan International Nepal’s Country Strategy 2023-28, the Project Officer will play a significant role in achieving its objective through this project, as demonstrated by its high sense of accountability, mutual respect and teamwork. As the Project Officer, he/she must have an in-depth understanding of project management for smooth facilitation, effective organisational and programme communication, partnership management and adherence to high quality programming and reporting while maintaining full compliance with the standards and requirements set by both the Government of Nepal and donor agencies.

Dimensions of the Role

The Project Officer’s (PO) main responsibility is to execute the project, monitoring and reporting meeting the donor compliance. PO should ensure timely and quality implementation of the project through local NGO. The position will require frequent travel to working districts and local government and need to coordinate with local government and prepare quality report i.e. event report and support partner to produce quality monthly and quarterly report as required. The position will also work closely with the partners and maintain cordial relationship with the provincial donor focal person.

The PO is a member of Programme, Partnership, and Impact (PPI) Department and works closely with Programme Quality and Innovation Unit (PQI) including Monitoring, Evaluation Research and Learning (MERL) unit, Business Development Department (for grants compliance/donor reporting) Influencing, Campaigns and Communications (ICC) team with regards to program effectiveness, quality program and efficiency.

Key relationships

Accountabilities

The Project Officer is responsible for the overall management including project implementation, partner oversight, monitoring, reporting, coordination, and donor compliance of the flood response project, ensuring timely, quality, and accountable delivery of services for adolescents and young people affected by floods.

Project Management and Implementation

  • Provide regular support to ensure smooth implementation with partner organizations. Conduct monitoring, documentation and close-out of the flood response project in Nuwakot, Rasuwa, and Dhading.
  • Develop and track project work plans, timelines, and targets to ensure timely delivery of project activities and results.
  • Monitor project progress and take timely actions to address implementation challenges, risks, and delays.
  • Conduct regular field visits to ensure quality, accountability, and achievement of project objectives.
  • Act as a communication link between partners and Plan International Nepal.

Partner Management and Compliance

  • Serve as the primary focal point for the implementing partner and provide day-to-day oversight and support.
  • Ensure partner activities are implemented on time, within budget, and in accordance with approved project plans and quality standards.
  • Ensure compliance with donor requirements, donor agreements, and Plan International Nepal policies and procedures.
  • Maintain regular communication and relation with donor on a day to day basis.
  • Review partner reports, financial documents, and supporting evidence to ensure accuracy, quality, and accountability.

Budget Management, Monitoring and Reporting

  • Assis Emergency Response Specialist in reviewing project budget. Support correct WBS and program codes are used, and support in tracking expenditures and burn rates through bi-weekly/monthly transaction reports.
  • Track project indicators and results, ensuring timely collection, verification, and reporting of data.
  • Support in preparing and submitting quality narrative reports, donor reports, success stories, case studies, and project updates within agreed timelines.
  • Maintain complete project documentation and records for compliance, audits, monitoring, and donor verification.

Coordination, Networking and Representation

  • Coordinate with local governments, district level stakeholders and other relevant coordination mechanisms to support effective project implementation.
  • Represent Plan International Nepal in project-related meetings, workshops, monitoring visits, and coordination forums as required.
  • Facilitate donor visits and provide timely updates on project progress, achievements, and challenges.

Safeguarding, Gender Equality and Accountability

  • Ensure safeguarding, PSHEA, gender equality, inclusion, and accountability principles are integrated across all project activities.
  • Ensure all interventions involving adolescents and young people comply with Plan International and donor safeguarding standards.
  • Promptly report and address safeguarding, compliance, and protection concerns in line with organizational procedures.

Other Responsibilities

  • Carry out any other duties assigned by the line manager in support of project objectives and organizational priorities.
  • Ensure compliance with Plan International’s Code of Conduct, Safeguarding, PSHEA, and Gender Equality and Inclusion policies.

Technical expertise, skills and knowledge

Essential Knowledge and Experience

  • A Bachelor’s Degree in development studies, development management, gender studies, social science or other relevant subjects with at least three (3) years of experience in project management, preferably in SRHR, GBV, Protection.
  • Proven experience in managing and working with partner NGO, implementing the activities including quality reporting.
  • Proven experience of working in emergency setting/humanitarian response will be added value.
  • Ability to communicate effectively and authoritatively on area of expertise, and influence others to reach common goals.
  • Proven experience and ability to coordinate and collaborate with different organizations including the government and demonstrable working experience in emergency response.
  • Knowledge of basic MS Office including MS Outlook, MS Word and MS Excel.
  • Good written and verbal communication skills in English and Nepali.

Skills (leadership/managerial if applicable)

  • Ability to establish and maintain effective relationships with colleagues, a variety of team members and external contacts, through good written and spoken communication skills
  • Good interpersonal skills for team working in multi-lingual and multi-cultural environment.
  • Demonstrably strong verbal and written communication, presentation and persuasion skills.
  • Ability to plan work and meet deadlines when working under pressure.
  • Able to create linkages, networking, lobbying and advocating with relevant stakeholders.
  • Good awareness and analysis of sensitivities attached with the government functionaries.
  • Ability to articulate the vision of Plan’s programme to different audiences.

Behaviours

  • Demonstrable professional maturity and able to work independently.
  • Ability to apply good judgment and professionalism in the resolution of work-related problems
  • Honest, encourages openness and transparency
  • Efficient in meeting commitments and deadlines in achieving results.
  • Ability to plan and organize work by identifying priority activities and adjusting priorities as required.
  • Demonstrated approach to work that is characterized by commitment, motivation, energy and flexibility.
  • Ability to relate to government authorities, UN agencies, and other development/humanitarian actors and to build a rapport effectively.
  • Commitment to Plan’s values including the rights and needs of children.

Plan International’s Values in Practice

We are open and accountable

We create a climate of trust inside and outside the organization by being open, honest and transparent. We hold ourselves and others to account for the decisions we make and for our impact on others, while doing what we say we will do.

We strive for lasting impact

We strive to achieve significant and lasting impact on the lives of children and young people, and to secure equality for girls. We challenge ourselves to be bold, courageous, responsive, focused and innovative.

We work well together

We succeed by working effectively with others, inside and outside the organisation, including our sponsors and donors. We actively support our colleagues, helping them to achieve their goals. We come together to create and implement solutions in our teams, across Plan International, with children, girls, young people, communities and our partners.

We are inclusive and empowering

We respect all people, appreciate differences and challenge inequality in our programmes and our workplace. We support children, girls and young people to increase their confidence and to change their own lives. We empower our staff to give their best and develop their potential.

Physical Environment

This position is based at Nuwakot District with frequent travel to Rasuwa and Dhading District.

Level of contact with children

High level: Frequent interaction with children and adolescents

Location: Nuwakot

Type of Role: Short-term employment until February 2027

Reports to: Emergency Response Specialist

Grade: C1

Closing Date: 22 October 2026

Equality, diversity and inclusion is at the very heart of everything that Plan International stands for.

We want Plan International to reflect the diversity of the communities we work with, offering equal opportunities to everyone regardless of age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, religion or belief, sex or sexual orientation.

Plan International is based on a culture of inclusivity and we strive to create a workplace environment that ensures every team, in every office, in every country, is rich in diverse people, thoughts, and ideas.

We foster an organisational culture that embraces our commitment to racial justice, gender equality, girls’ rights and inclusion.

Plan International believes that in a world where children face so many threats of harm, it is our duty to ensure that we, as an organisation, do everything we can to keep children safe. This means that we have particular responsibilities to children that we come into contact with and we must not contribute in any way to harming or placing children at risk.

A range of pre-employment checks will be undertaken in conformity with Plan International’s Safeguarding Children and Young People policy. Plan International also participates in the Inter Agency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme. In line with this scheme we will request information from applicants previous employers about any findings of sexual exploitation, sexual abuse and/or sexual harassment during employment, or incidents under investigation when the applicant left employment. By submitting an application, the job applicant confirms their understanding of these recruitment procedures.

Please note that Plan International will never send unsolicited emails requesting payment from candidates.

Job Title: Education Officer
Required No: 6 (4 for Koshi and 2 for Tanahun)
Location: Program Districts of Koshi and Tanahun District of Gandaki province
Reports to: District Lead

Role Summary

UWS Nepal is committed to improving learning outcomes and promoting inclusive, equitable, and quality education in remote and underserved communities. The Education Officer (EO) plays a strategic role in translating this vision into actionable support at the local level. Working closely with District Lead, local government bodies, school leadership, and communities, the EO is responsible for leading teacher
development, strengthening school systems, and driving data-informed education interventions.

Key Responsibilities:

1. Strategic Teachers’ Training, Development and Mentorship

  •  Identify training needs and develop training programs accordingly
  •  Deliver a minimum of 60 hours of school-based Professional Development training to all teachers annually, based on UWS Training Guidelines.
  •  Lead high-quality and engaging training workshops for teachers in program schools, focusing on effective and innovative teaching methodologies and student assessment.
  •  Guide teachers in implementing child-friendly, inclusive, and engaging pedagogical practices.
  •  Mentor and coach teachers to implement program strategies and improve classroom practices.
  •  Conduct quarterly lesson observations of each teacher and provide actionable feedback.
  • Facilitate collaborative learning among teachers through workshops, peer coaching and lesson sharing.
  • Track training schedules, manage quarterly deadlines for trainings, and ensure smooth program execution.
  •  Adapt and translate training materials to suit the local context as needed

2. School Improvement & Program Implementation

  • Conduct regular school monitoring visits to assess school operations, classroom practices, and learning environments.
  •  Collaborate with Head Teachers and SMCs to implement the long-term School Development Plan (SDP) at the school level.
  • Implement interventions aligned with the SDP and track progress using the School Development Report (SDR).
  •  Oversee and advise on the procurement and effective use of textbooks, teaching aids, and other educational resources.
  • Support the recruitment, onboarding, and capacity-building of community teachers.

3. Monitoring, Evaluation & Data-Driven Planning

  • Collect, verify, and analyse data on student learning, teacher effectiveness, and school performance.
  •  Use assessment and attendance data to identify trends, gaps, and improvement opportunities.
  •  Report findings and insights to the Education Coordinator to inform regional strategies.
  • Contribute to the development of school-based action plans based on data and observations.

4. Local Government Coordination & Policy Alignment

  • Serve as the primary liaison with Municipality Education Offices, ensuring alignment with local education policies and priorities.
  • Advocate for the integration and sustainability of UWS Nepal’s programs through local education plans.
  • Represent UWS Nepal in relevant municipal and district-level education forums.

5. School Mobilizer Supervision and Support

  • Provide strong leadership and guidance to School Mobilizers to ensure smooth implementation of education initiatives.
  •  Support SMs in building effective relationships with SMCs, teachers, and communities.
  •  Monitor SM performance, provide feedback, and ensure their alignment with UWS goals and values.

6. Community Engagement & Safeguarding

  • Build and maintain trust within the community through regular consultations and collaboration with parents and local leaders.
  • Encourage parental involvement in children’s learning and foster community ownership of schools.
  •  Promote UWS Nepal’s Child Protection and Safeguarding policies at all levels.
  • Ensure that all educational activities are inclusive and responsive to the needs of marginalized and vulnerable children.

7. Coordination and Logistical Support

  •  Support planning and coordination of donor, partner, and official visits to UWS Nepal schools.
  •  Collaborate with external education stakeholders and organizations to promote shared learning and local partnerships.
  •  Participate in inter-agency meetings and joint education initiatives where relevant.

Qualification and Experience:

  • Bachelor’s degree in any discipline preferably in Education
  •  At least 3 years of working experience in the field of education.
  •  Experience in holding ToT trainings in CCA and curriculum development
  •  Proven track record of coordinating projects involving different stakeholders

Skills & Competencies

  •  Knowledge of the country’s education system, policies and strategies
  • Understanding of the education system of government schools in rural Nepal.
  •  Understanding of programme development with experience in Project Cycle Management and Result Based Management
  •  Results-oriented team player with very good analytical skills and problem-solving attitude
  •  Willing to work with children, teachers, parents, and the community.
  • Fluency in Nepali language(s) and English (spoken and written)
  • Knowledge in Child Rights, Child Protection Policies and Inclusive Education are an asset.
  •  Flexible to work long hours beyond working hours.
  •  Computer proficiency
  •  Report writing skill

Organizational Context

The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) is the world’s largest humanitarian network, with 191 member National Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies. IFRC uses the Triple R – response, resilience and respect – to deliver on Strategy 2030. IFRC responds to disasters and crises, ensuring timely, coordinated and locally led humanitarian action. IFRC supports its members in building community resilience in the areas of climate and environment, health and wellbeing, and migration and displacement. IFRC promotes respect for our fundamental principles of humanity, impartiality, neutrality, independence, voluntary service, unity, and universality, including in our work on values, power and inclusion. The IFRC focuses throughout on our core mandate – our raison d’être – of strategic and operational coordination, humanitarian diplomacy, National Society development, and accountability. IFRC is led by its Secretary General and has its Headquarters in Geneva and five regional offices in Africa (Nairobi); the Americas (Panama); Asia Pacific (Kuala Lumpur); Europe (Budapest); and MENA (Beirut) as well as representation offices, service centres and delegations across the globe. The IFRC has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment and other forms of harassment, abuse of authority, discrimination, and lack of integrity (including but not limited to financial misconduct). IFRC also adheres to strict child safeguarding principles. The IFRC is currently present in Nepal through a Country Delegation (CD – first established in 1965 with a presence through regional representation at times), providing support to Nepal Red Cross Society (NRCS) programmes and National Society development (NSD) amongst as well as emergency response, other areas. The longer-term mission of the Nepal Delegation is to facilitate organisational growth, technical capacities, partnerships, and resource mobilisation that enable Nepal Red Cross Society to deliver on its humanitarian mandate in the country through the provision of technical support, advocacy, representation and coordination functions, in accordance with Strategy 2030, the IFRC Renewal and annual Operational Plans. The Country Delegation also provides integration services to six IFRC members with a presence in Nepal. On 26 August 2026, a major ice-rock avalanche occurred in the upper Bhote Koshi watershed near the China–Nepal border, resulting in an historically powerful flash flood that advanced from the border down the entire length of Nepal along the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli River basins. This position is being hired to respond to the operational requirements of the Flash Flood 2026 response operation, within a Federation-wide operation

  • Proven ability to gather, analyse and organise information and translate it into clear and compelling communications for different audiences.
  • Excellent written and spoken English and Nepali, with strong skills in writing and editing articles, stories and other communications materials.
  • Good skills in photography, videography, digital content and basic design, with the ability to produce or coordinate multimedia content.
  • Experience in media engagement, developing media contacts and supporting spokespersons with key messages, briefings and interviews.

What we offer

This role will provide you with an opportunity to make a difference in Oxfam by working closely with a group of passionate people that are specialists in their field of Gender, WASH and Water Governance, Humanitarian and DRM and so forth along with the national and international training and development opportunities. Our offer consists of fair pay and competitive benefits package. At Oxfam, we believe that every aspect of our work can lead to a positive outcome. If you have the same opinion, together with the ability to meet the challenges involved, this role offers scope for immense personal fulfilment – as well as outstanding opportunities to develop your career.

Oxfam is committed to providing a fair compensation package and to providing a flexible, supportive, working environment.

How to apply

As part of your online application, please upload your up-to-date CV and Cover Letter explaining your suitability against the essential criteria in the job profile. Please click in APPLY for the application.

Please note that this is a rolling recruitment process and the vacancy may close once a suitable candidate is identified.

Terre des hommes (Tdh), headquartered in Lausanne with an office in Zurich, is the largest Swiss children’s rights organization, with over 2,000 staff members worldwide. We are committed to working alongside children to guarantee their rights, protect their lives, and improve their well-being. We achieve this through our innovative programs in the areas of health, migration, and access to justice, designed to have a positive and lasting impact.

Founded in 1960 and active in Nepal since 1985, Tdh has implemented impactful interventions in Maternal and Child Health, Migration, and WASH in Institutions, with a strong focus on Child Protection. All initiatives are carried out in close collaboration with government bodies and civil society organizations to ensure sustainable and child-centered outcomes.

Position: Health & WASH Program Manager

Report to: Country Director

Location: Kathmandu

Duration: 1 year with possibility of extension

Application deadline: 28th October 2026

Background:

The Health & WASH Program Manager (H&WPM) is responsible for the overall management, development, and supervision of Tdh Nepal’s Health and WASH Programs, including project design and fundraising, in alignment with Tdh policies, strategies, plans, and thematic indicators. The H&WPM is also responsible for establishing and maintaining effective linkages with relevant stakeholders, managing partnerships, ensuring timely reporting, donor compliance, and appropriate representation of the organisation. The position ensures the availability and effective utilisation of financial, logistical, and material resources for Health and WASH Programs, as well as the effective implementation of the Monitoring and Evaluation framework across all Health and WASH programs. In addition, the H&WPM leads the development of funding proposals and concept notes to mobilise resources for Tdh Nepal’s Health and WASH portfolio, including Digital Health.

Main Responsibilities

Strategic Management

  •  Steer strategically the Health & WASH programs in coordination with the Multi-Country Director and Regional Advisors/Managers.
  • Lead the definition and proactive implementation of country strategic directions for Health & WASH, using operational strategies, action plans and relevant monitoring and follow-up tools.
  • Lead the development and periodic review of institutional strategies, fundraising proposals, strategic country guidelines and policies.
  • Contribute to Senior Management Team deliberations and organizational decision-making, providing strategic technical leadership on Health & WASH.

Project Management

  •  Lead the design and management of projects under his/her thematic responsibility, including budgeting, implementation planning, reporting, steering, quality assurance, partnership management, donor liaison, field visits, advocacy and representation in relevant networks and forums.
  • In collaboration with the MCD and relevant teams, assess the evolving needs of target populations to inform program adaptation, new project development and appropriate allocation of resources.
  • Develop quarterly strategic action plans with partners and Tdh staff to ensure Health & WASH projects remain aligned with objectives, priorities and expected results.
  •  Conduct regular partner meetings and field monitoring, providing critical analysis of activities, outcomes, challenges, solutions, adaptations and impact.
  • Contribute to institutionalizing CPMS and lead its mainstreaming across Tdh Health & WASH preparedness and response actions.
  • Conduct monthly budget-versus-actual analysis and ensure timely adjustments to program spending and resource allocations.
  • Ensure compliance with Social Welfare Council (SWC) requirements throughout project development, approval, implementation and reporting; facilitate engagement with relevant government authorities, partnership selection and required local government pre-consent.

Resource Mobilization

  • Identify and cultivate strategic funding opportunities and prospective donors for the Health & WASH portfolio, aligned with Tdh Nepal’s strategic priorities.
  •  Lead the development and timely submission of high-quality concept notes, proposals and budgets in line with donor requirements and Tdh standards.
  • Develop and maintain strategic donor relationships and contribute to positioning Tdh for longer-term, diversified and sustainable Health & WASH funding.

Partnership Management

  • Lead partner selection, assessment and capacity-strengthening processes, and support Tdh teams in delivering planned and responsive partner capacity development.
  •  Maintain effective, accountable and professional relationships with project partners and stakeholders, ensuring partners understand and comply with Tdh policies, standards and contractual obligations.
  • Address partner concerns and grievances constructively, resolving operational challenges while safeguarding Tdh’s mandate, standards and institutional interests.

Program Coordination

  • Establish and maintain strategic networks with UN agencies, bilateral and multilateral donors, foundations, I/NGOs and relevant Government of Nepal entities working in Health & WASH to strengthen Tdh’s positioning, visibility and influence.
  • Coordinate with HR, M&E, Capacity Development, Communications, External Relations and other thematic teams to deliver integrated program results.

Human Resource Management

  • Supervise and support staff under his/her responsibility through effective performance management, professional guidance, coaching and capacity strengthening.
  • Foster effective teamwork and provide leadership on cross-departmental collaboration, coordination and harmonization of approaches.
  • Contribute to a positive, inclusive and respectful working environment through proactive dialogue, constructive feedback and collaborative problem-solving.

Monitoring and Evalaution Framework

  • Support the M&E team in designing, maintaining and using quality data for program monitoring, reporting, learning and decision-making.
  •  Lead the development and periodic review of logical frameworks in coordination with the M&E team.
  • Ensure sound and relevant needs assessments, project concepts, approaches and proposals are developed in line with Tdh’s Project Cycle Management (PCM) standards and donor requirements, grounded in field realities and beneficiaries’ needs.

Advocacy, Representaiton and Networking

  • Support and facilitate advocacy initiatives and strategies on Health & WASH in coordination with thematic advisors, headquarters and relevant partners.
  • Represent Tdh with international organisations, inter-agency coordination mechanisms, UN agencies, thematic clusters, Health Working Groups and relevant government and institutional forums.
  • Coordinate national partnerships with government agencies, INGOs and national NGOs to advance joint advocacy and policy objectives.
  • In emergencies, coordinate with relevant agencies and inter-agency mechanisms for assessment, planning and response, including integration of CPMS into emergency preparedness and response.

Research and Learning

  • Ensure management of Tdh Nepal’s thematic needs assessments and relevant research in coordination with the MEAL team.
  • Organize regular strategic briefings for the MCD, SMT, Tdh staff and partners on findings, progress and implications of research and assessments.

Reporting and Knowledge Management

  •  Produce and ensure timely, accurate and reliable program information and reports, maintaining confidentiality of sensitive mission information and securing required validation.
  •  Ensure effective data collection, analysis and reporting systems to demonstrate achievement of project objectives and meet donor requirements within agreed timelines and formats, in coordination with the Line Manager.
  • Share relevant program learning, reports and information with Tdh coordinators to strengthen cross-program coherence and organizational learning.

Safeguarding and Risk Management

  • Adhere to and promote the application of Tdh’s Child Safeguarding Policy, Code of Conduct, Security, Whistleblowing, Anti-Fraud and Anti-Corruption Policies and other organizational risk-management standards.
  • Ensure safeguarding, PSEA, Do No Harm, accountability and risk mitigation are integrated across Health & WASH program design, implementation, partnerships and field operations

Profile:

Education/Qualifications:

  • Master’s degree in public health, development studies or related discipline(s)

Experience

  • At least ten years of working experience in managing health projects, especially mother and child health projects.
  • Minimum of 5 years of direct experience in Water, Sanitation and Hygiene, particularly WASH in Healthcare facilities (also, WASH school)
  •  Has been part of the Senior Management Team of the organization.
  • Experience of implementing an integrating health and WASH projects.
  • Experience and willingness to travel to and work with remote and underprivileged communities.
  • Solid Management experience including e.g. team, project partners, government coordination, networking with like-minded organization and advocacy.
  • Solid understanding and experience of PCM, project design and a solid understanding of Theory of Change
  • Prior experience of working with the diversified team and thematic groups
  • Very good report writing and communication skills

Languages: Excellent proficiency in both written and spoken English and Nepali, with the ability to communicate clearly, professionally, and effectively across diverse audiences.

IT Knowledges

Ability to operate Microsoft Office 365 suite: Word, Excel & Power Point, SharePoint.

Tdh General Code of Conduct and Ethical Policies :

Commits to promoting and complying with the Global Code of Conduct, systematically reporting any violations of the Code through Tdh’s formal reporting mechanisms and dealing with any violations of procedures and processes appropriately.

Raises awareness of the Foundation of the risks of policy non-compliance, violence and abuse, and related rights, towards children, community members and our own employees.

Undertakes to comply with key ethical policies and guidelines, including the Safeguarding Policy, the Anti-Fraud and Corruption Policy, the Conflict-of-Interest Policy and other policies related to the prevention of terrorist financing and criminal activities, as well as workplace behavior.

Commits to putting values and principles into practice through exemplary behavior, in full compliance with the Code of Conduct, and always respecting established procedures and processes.

Commits to developing a compliant and enlightened management culture within the organization and in our work with children and the communities in which we operate

Tdh is an equal opportunities employer. Employees are recruited regardless of their race, ethnicity, religion, or gender. Women, LGBTQI and People with disability are also encouraged to apply.

References :

Please note that all job offers will be subject to satisfactory references and checks (criminal record and anti-terrorism funding check). Position: Communication and Reporting Analyst-Roster Recruitment
Location: Birendranagar

Job Description

This is a roster recruitment. The selected candidate can be placed in Kathmandu or any provincial offices within Nepal as per the requirement

Tiered Approach

In Line With The Commitment To Safeguard Capacity And Support Personnel Already In The Organization, a Majority Of UNDP UNCDF/UNV Vacancies Are Advertised Using a Tiered Application Process Whereby

  • Tier 0: UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.
  • Tier 1: Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

  • Tier 3 or no tier indicated: All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) is the UN’s global development network, advocating for change and connecting countries to knowledge, experience, and resources to help people build a better life. We are on the ground in 170 countries and territories, working with governments and people on their own solutions to global and national development challenges to help empower lives and build resilient nations.

Duties And Responsibilities

The Communications and Reporting Analyst will be responsible for designing and implementing a comprehensive communications and visibility strategy that effectively showcases the results, innovations, and lessons of the Nepal project. The Communications and Reporting Analyst will develop and manage communication materials, coordinate outreach with national and international stakeholders, and ensure alignment with UNDP and donor branding requirements. Key duties include documenting project achievements, producing multimedia content, strengthening media and partner networks, and supporting advocacy and knowledge exchange at national, regional, and global levels.

Design, Develop, Implement And Manage The Project Communication Strategy

  • Finalize, implement, and update a communications and visibility strategy aligned with UNDP standards.
  • Ensure coverage of all project components and integration of GESI and safeguards dimensions.
  •  Produce high-quality materials, including press releases, newsletters, infographics, reports, case studies, photo essays, and short videos.
  • Oversee the design, layout, and production of communication outputs, ensuring adherence to UN editorial and branding guidelines.
  • Maintain a digital library of media, photographs, and knowledge products.
  • Track communication outputs, media coverage, and audience engagement.
  •  Provide quarterly updates and inputs to project progress reports, highlighting communication milestones and results.
  • Recommend adjustments to enhance visibility, outreach, and impact.
  • Integrate GESI principles in all planning, implementation, and monitoring processes to ensure equitable participation and benefits for women, men, persons with disabilities, and marginalized groups.

Strengthen Media Engagement And Partnerships

  • Establish and maintain relationships with national and international media outlets, journalists, and influencers to raise awareness of project outcomes.
  •  Facilitate media coverage of key milestones, site visits, and events related to UNDP projects.
  •  Provide technical guidance and capacity building to staff, partners, and stakeholders on applying gender and social inclusion approaches in project interventions.

Support Knowledge Management And Dissemination

  • Document project progress, achievements, and lessons learned through accessible communication formats.
  • Translate technical findings into clear and engaging knowledge products for diverse audiences, including policymakers, communities, and global partners.
  • Contribute to South-South exchanges by preparing content for UNDP, and donor platforms.
  •  Collect, analyze, and report disaggregated data (by sex, age, disability, and other relevant factors) to identify gaps and recommend strategies for inclusive programming.

Coordinate Outreach And Advocacy Activities

  •  Organize public events, workshops, and campaigns to showcase project achievements.
  • Provide communication support for donor engagement, joint monitoring missions, and stakeholder consultations.
  •  Ensure advocacy efforts highlight the inclusion of vulnerable groups, and sustainable development linkages.

Ensure internal and partner communication alignment

  • Maintain close collaboration with UNDP, government counterparts, and partner institutions’ communication focal points.
  • Ensure consistency of project messaging across all channels and partners.
  •  Support resource mobilization by producing compelling content for partners and donors.
  • EnsureGESI priorities to promote coherence, accountability, and consistency in messaging and implementation.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement

The Communication and Reporting Analyst will report directly to the Project Manager and work closely with the Communication Analyst of UNDP Country Office.

Think Innovatively: LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements

Learn Continuously: LEVEL 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback

Act with Determination: LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident

Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 1: Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confront discrimination

Ability to manage communications internally and externally, through media, social media and other appropriate channels

Required Skills And Experience

  •  Advanced University Degree (Master´s degree or equivalent) in Communication, Journalism, Media Relations, External Relations, Public Affairs, Iinternational Development, Social Sciences, or other relevant area is required. Or
  • A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the above-mentioned fields in combination with additional 2 years of relevant experience will be given due consideration in lieu of master’s degree.

Min. Years Of Relevant Work Experience

  • Applicants with master’s degree (or equivalent) in a relevant field of study are not required to have professional work experience.
  • Applicants with a bachelor’s degree (or equivalent) are required to have a minimum of two (2) years of working experience in communication and reporting.

Desired skills in addition to the competencies covered in the Competencies section

  •  Experience in MS Office and design/multimedia tools (e.g., Adobe Creative Suite, Canva, video editing software).

  •  Experience working with UNDP, or other donor-funded projects.

UNDP does not tolerate harassment, sexual harassment, exploitation, discrimination and abuse of authority. All selected candidates, therefore, undergo relevant checks and are expected to adhere to the respective standards and principles.

This is a roster recruitment. The selected candidate can be placed in Kathmandu or any provincial offices within Nepal as per the requirement

In Line With The Commitment To Safeguard Capacity And Support Personnel Already In The Organization, a Majority Of UNDP UNCDF/UNV Vacancies Are Advertised Using a Tiered Application Process Whereby

• Tier 0: UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

Background

The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) is the UN’s global development network, advocating for change and connecting countries to knowledge, experience, and resources to help people build a better life. We are on the ground in 170 countries and territories, working with governments and people on their own solutions to global and national development challenges to help empower lives and build resilient nations.

Under the overall guidance of the Project Manager, the Administration and Finance Analyst will be responsible for the day-to-day financial management, administration, and operational support of the project. The Analyst ensures the effective and transparent utilization of financial resources, compliance with UNDP rules and regulations, and integrates principles of Gender Equality, Social Inclusion (GESI), and Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) into all operational activities.

Duties And Responsibilities

Ensure implementation of Financial Management and Accounting

  • Manage the day-to-day financial operations, ensuring full compliance with UNDP rules, regulations, policies, and NIM/DIM procedures.
  •  Process payment requests, disbursements, and travel claim accurately within the UNDP ERP system (e.g., Quantum).
  •  Maintain a robust internal expenditure control system. Regularly monitor financial exception reports, investigate unusual transactions or anomalies, and propose corrective actions to management.
  •  Continuously monitor project budgets and expenditures in cooperation with the Project Manager.
  •  Conduct quality financial analysis of budget performance by cost inputs and partners and support the preparation of financial forecasts and disbursement requests.
  •  Prepare timely and accurate financial statements, bank reconciliations, and consolidated reports for the Project Board, donors, and the Country Office.
  • Support the development of funding requests, grant negotiations, and amendments.
  • Facilitate programme audits and investigations in coordination with relevant oversight bodies.
  •  Ensure the effective implementation of audit recommendations, management actions, and recovery actions.
  •  Conduct regular field visits in close coordination with the programme team to ensure financial compliance and provide monitoring support for implementing partners and sub-recipients.

Ensure management of programme budgets and the operation of the optimal cost recovery system

  • Prepare, continuously monitor, and revise programme budgets in UNDP ERP systems (Quantum and Hyperion), ensuring strict alignment with approved detailed budgets and Annual Work Plans (AWPs).
  •  Implement optimal cost recovery mechanisms, ensuring Direct Project Costs (DPC) and General Management Support (GMS) fees are accurately calculated and billed.
  •  Maintain robust internal controls to ensure transactions are correctly coded against budget lines and donor agreements prior to approval.
  •  Conduct regular analysis of budget delivery and expenditure variances.
  • Prepare budget reviews, financial forecasts, and provide justifications for necessary budget reallocations or reprogramming requests for submission to donors.
  •  Prepare accurate monthly, quarterly, and annual cash flow forecasts.
  •  Monitor incoming donor contributions, ensuring the timely transfer, identification, and registration of receipts in the system.
  • Finalize the financial sections of progress reports, disbursement requests, and statements of sources and use of funds, strictly adhering to specific donor reporting timelines and requirements.
  •  Transaction Processing & Records Management: Manage the initiation, approval, and settlement of bank transfers.
  •  Ensure the proper management of cash receipts and petty cash, and maintain a rigorous, audit-ready filing system for all finance records and documents.

Ensure facilitation of knowledge building and knowledge sharing in monitoring and evaluation

  • In coordination with the Project Manager supports the development of partnerships and maintains strong working relationships with the national, provincial partners and entities, donors, technical partners, and UN agencies to ensure transparent and effective management, quality services and oversight of the programmes.
  •  Supports the Project Manager in the development of capacity development through different trainings/coaching/mentoring and transition strategies to support national entities to implement and assume the PR role, ensuring access to appropriate tools and resources.
  • Actively participates in UNDP and other relevant external networks/forums to promote the programme.
  •  Conduct training for the project and other relevant stakeholders on financial management and oversight.

Ensure Effective Administration and Operations Management

  • Ensure the effective administration and operational management of the project in compliance with UNDP rules, regulations, policies, and procedures.
  • ] Coordinate project procurement activities, including preparation of procurement plans, specifications, requests for quotations, purchase orders, and contract management in accordance with UNDP procurement policies.
  •  Monitor the implementation of procurement activities and maintain an updated procurement tracking system to ensure timely delivery of goods and services.
  •  Support recruitment processes for project personnel and consultants, including preparation of Terms of Reference (TORs), evaluation processes, contract administration, and onboarding arrangements.
  • Coordinate travel arrangements for project personnel, consultants, and stakeholders, including travel authorizations, ticketing, logistics, security clearances, and travel claim settlements.
  • Organize project meetings, workshops, trainings, and field missions, ensuring appropriate logistical, administrative, and financial arrangements.
  • Maintain project asset and inventory records and ensure proper utilization, maintenance, verification, transfer, and disposal of project assets in accordance with UNDP policies.
  • Ensure effective records management and maintain an organized filing system for project administrative, procurement, human resources, and operational documentation.
  •  Monitor the validity and timely renewal of project contracts, agreements, leases, and service arrangements.
  •  Support the preparation and monitoring of project work plans, procurement plans, HR plans, and operational plans.
  • Coordinate with UNDP operations units and service providers to ensure timely provision of administrative and operational support services.
  • Identify operational risks and recommend appropriate mitigation measures to ensure efficient project implementation.
  • Support project closure activities, including asset disposal, records archiving, contract closure, and administrative reporting.
  • Ensure environmental sustainability, accessibility, safeguarding, and GESI considerations are integrated into project operations and administrative processes.

Contribution towards Gender Equality and Social Inclusion (GESI)

  •  Ensure GESI is mainstreamed in the budget, Annual Work Plan (AWP), procurement and HR plans, and all other administrative work to be undertaken by the project in coordination with Community, Rights and Gender Analyst and GESI Analyst of UNDP CO.
  •  Promote gender equality and social inclusion (GESI) throughout programme implementation.
  •  Collaborates with team members, programme partners, and sub-grantees to ensure safe implementation of programmes at the community level applying Do No Harm approach.
  •  Promote a respectful, inclusive, and safe workplace culture, supporting “Do No Harm” principles in all administrative and field-level operations.
  •  Assist in collecting and reporting gender-disaggregated data related to project administration, procurements, and event participation.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

The incumbent will be reporting to Project Manager.

Core
