Details

Mission and objectives

The UN Resident Coordinator’s Office (UN RCO) in Nepal works under the strategic guidance of the UN Resident Coordinator (RC) and supports the UN Country Team (UNCT) in the advancement of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. The UN RCO fulfills the following five key functions in support of the responsibilities of the RC and the UNCT including: Strategic planning; Development economics; Partnerships and development finance; Data and results management and reporting; and Research, communications and advocacy. The UN RCO and UNCT work closely with the Government of Nepal and other Development Partners to support Nepal in achieving Agenda 2030 and the Sustainable Development Goals. The UN RCO team supports the RC and UNCT in ensuring a more coordinated and coherent approach across the work of the UN and is composed of experts in development and humanitarian coordination, information management, human rights, gender equality, communications and communications.

Context

The UN Resident Coordinator is the highest-ranking representative of the UN development system in Nepal and leads the UN Country Team (UNCT) of resident and non-resident agencies, funds and programmes. The Resident Coordinator’s Office supports the Resident Coordinator in steering the delivery of the UN Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF) 2023 to 2027, agreed with the Government of Nepal, and in coordinating the UN’s collective response to national priorities, including disaster response, Nepal’s transition out of the least developed country category, climate action and the 2030 Agenda. The RCO’s communications function positions the UN as one coherent partner to the Government and the people of Nepal. It supports the Resident Coordinator’s public voice, produces joint UNCT content and chairs the UN Communications Group (UNCG), which brings together communications focal points from across the UN system in Nepal. Nepal’s audiences are young and mobile-first. Reaching them requires content that is made for vertical screens, published in Nepali as well as English, and produced at the speed of the platforms. This assignment brings a young Nepali creator into the RCO to strengthen that capacity and to keep the UN’s digital presence current, credible and genuinely watchable.

Task description

Under the supervision of the National Information Officer, the UN Volunteer will produce original digital content for UN Nepal’s social media channels, maintain the joint content calendar, and support campaigns and live coverage of UNCT events. The UN Volunteer will contribute a young audience perspective to communications planning and will build practical creative skills in a multilateral working environment

. A. Content production

  • Produce short-form vertical video(reels) for UNCT Nepal channels, covering concept, script, filming, editing, subtitling, sound and export in platform-native formats.
  • Design static and animated assets, including carousels, quote cards, infographics and event graphics, in line with the UNCT visual identity and UN Nepal brand guidance.
  • Write platform-tailored copy in Nepali and English, adjusting register and length for each channel rather than reposting a single text across all of them.
  • Cover Resident Coordinator and UNCT events, launches and joint events as photographer and videographer, and deliver same-day clips and images where required.
  •  Source and produce human-interest content with agency communications colleagues, showing how UN support reaches people, with informed consent obtained and recorded for every person featured.
  •  Maintain the RCO digital asset library, including captions, credits, consent records and version control.

B. Channel management and engagement

  •  Maintain and update the UN Nepal content calendar across Facebook, X, Instagram, LinkedIn, YouTube and TikTok, aligned to the UNSDCF, international days and joint UNCT moments.
  •  Schedule and publish approved content, and monitor comments and direct messages during agreed hours.
  •  Draft responses to routine audience queries, and escalate sensitive, political or reputational matters to the supervisor without responding directly.
  •  Monitor conversation and sentiment on UN-related topics in Nepali digital spaces, and flag misinformation for verification and coordinated response.
  •  Support live coverage of high-visibility events, including real-time posting and rapid-turnaround edits.

C. Campaigns and joint UN work

  •  Contribute creative concepts for content to joint UN campaigns and international day observances, and produce the assets agreed for each.
  • Support the UNCG with shared content packages, including toolkits that agencies can adapt for their own channels.
  • Support youth-facing initiatives such as reel competitions, creator collaborations, vox pop series and campus activations.
  • Support the digital rollout of RCO publications, including the UNCT Results Report and the UN Nepal newsletter.

D. Analytics and learning

  • Compile monthly performance analytics across platforms, with plain-language interpretation of what worked and what did not.
  •  Test formats, posting times and narrative approaches, and document findings so they inform the following month’s calendar.
  • Contribute inputs on communications results to RCO reporting.

E. Youth perspective and skills transfer

  •  Bring the perspective of young Nepali audiences into content planning discussions and editorial decisions.
  • Share editing, design and platform skills with UNCG colleagues through short peer learning sessions.
  •  Maintain awareness of platform and format shifts relevant to UN Nepal’s audiences and advise accordingly.

By the end of the assignment, the following are expected:

  •  A live UN Nepal content calendar maintained continuously and shared with the UNCG each month.
  • A minimum of four original short-form videos and eight designed assets produced each month.
  •  Photo and video coverage delivered for all Resident Coordinator public engagements assigned to the UN Volunteer.
  •  Monthly analytics reports produced for twelve months, with documented recommendations acted on in subsequent planning.
  • An organized, searchable and consent-compliant RCO digital asset library.
  • At least two peer learning sessions delivered to UNCG colleagues.
  • Demonstrable growth in engagement and reach on UN Nepal channels against the baseline set in the first month.

Position: MERL Coordinator- Shikshya Project Preparation Fund (55066)

The Organisation

Plan International is an independent development and humanitarian organisation that advances children’s rights and equality for girls. We believe in the power and potential of every child but know this is often suppressed by poverty, violence, exclusion and discrimination. And it is girls who are most affected.

Working together with children, young people, supporters and partners, we strive for a just world, tackling the root causes of the challenges girls and vulnerable children face. We support children’s rights from birth until they reach adulthood and we enable children to prepare for and respond to crises and adversity. We drive changes in practice and policy at local, national and global levels using our reach, experience and knowledge.

For over 85 years, we have rallied other determined optimists to transform the lives of all children in more than 80 countries.

We won’t stop until we are all equal.

ROLE PURPOSE

The MERL Coordinator provides the MERL expertise required to establish and use valid evidence for the formulation of the upcoming MOFA Japan-funded project through the Shikshya – Project Preparation Fund. The role validates targeting, needs, interventions, and results through the Needs Assessment and Pilot Program and applies the evidence to future project design and formulation. The role also provides MERL expertise throughout the project cycle for projects implemented with top-up funding.

Dimensions of the Role

The MERL Coordinator is responsible for the MERL functions of Shikshya – Project Preparation Fund and projects implemented with top-up funding. Under the project, the main areas of responsibility are the Needs Assessment, Pilot Program, Evidence-Based Project Formulation, and Evidence-Based Reporting & Strategic Visibility. All project responsibilities are carried out under the direction and approval of the Project Manager, with technical guidance from the MERL Specialist for ROE on MERL matters.

Direct Line Manager: Project Manager

Dotted Line Manager: MERL Specialist for ROE (Providing technical guidance on MERL matters)

Budget Accountability: Management of NPR 1,750,000 allocated to the Needs Assessment under the Shikshya – Project Preparation Fund, subject to approval by the Project Manager.

Number of direct reports: 0

External relationships and representation: Coordinates with Implementing Partners on program implementation, monitoring, and data management and provides technical guidance and capacity strengthening as needed. Coordinates with external consultants and other stakeholders involved in the Needs Assessment and Pilot implementation and evaluation as required.
Project team: Works as part of a four-member project team comprising the Project Manager, Finance Coordinator, MERL Coordinator, and Construction Coordinator, with responsibility for the project’s MERL functions.

Level of Effort (LOE): 100% allocated to the Shikshya – Project Preparation Fund and projects implemented with top-up funding. Support to other projects or functions is limited to exceptional cases and requires prior coordination with the Project Manager.

Authority / technical guidance: All project responsibilities are carried out under the direction and approval of the Project Manager, with technical guidance from the MERL Specialist for ROE on MERL matters.

Key relationships

The MERL Coordinator engages with key internal and external stakeholders on MERL matters related to the Needs Assessment, Pilot Program, project formulation, reporting, and strategic visibility under the Shikshya – Project Preparation Fund and projects implemented with top-up funding.

Accountabilities

The MERL Coordinator is accountable for the following results to establish and use the evidence required for the formulation of the upcoming MOFA Japan-funded project,

1. Needs Assessment

Establish valid evidence on target areas and populations, priority issues, and intersectional needs to inform targeting and design of the upcoming project.

  •  Design the methodology, data requirements, and quantitative and qualitative methods.
  • Manage data collection, verify data quality, and analyze the evidence collected.
  • Identify target areas and populations, priority issues, and intersectional needs, and consolidate the findings as evidence for the Pilot Program and future project formulation.

2. Pilot Program

Validate the effectiveness of interventions and the conditions for their implementation through the design, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of the Pilot Program.

  •  Provide MERL technical input to the design of interventions, expected results, Results Framework / Logframe, indicators, and measurement methods based on the Needs Assessment findings.
  • With the requirements of MOFA Japan, including No Change and Details, in view, verify alignment between approved activity details, actual implementation, and reported data; identify discrepancies across records and data sources; and ensure corrective follow-up as required. This includes participant numbers and breakdowns, number of sessions, attendance, outputs, and other activity-level information.
    Assess change and effectiveness using quantitative and qualitative methods and determine what works, for whom, under what conditions, and to what extent.

3. Evidence-Based Project Formulation

Integrate evidence from the Needs Assessment and Pilot Program into the design and formulation of the upcoming project.

  • Analyze evidence from the Needs Assessment and Pilot Program and provide technical input to targeting, priority issues, approaches, and interventions.
  •  Provide evidence-based technical input to the design of the results logic, Results Framework / Logframe, indicators, and measurement approach.
  •  Organize data, analysis, and evidence required for proposal development and support the Project Manager in evidence-based project formulation.

4. Evidence-Based Reporting and Strategic Visibility

Use quantitative and qualitative evidence to clearly demonstrate project results and changes through reporting and strategic visibility.

  • Manage and analyze evidence on activities, outputs, and outcomes and provide verified information for internal and donor reporting.
  •  Collect and document qualitative evidence, including photographs, participant stories, and quotes, with appropriate consent.
  •  Integrate quantitative and qualitative evidence and coordinate with ICC and other relevant teams to use verified project results and changes for reporting and strategic visibility.

5. Cross-Cutting Responsibility

  • Coordinate with Implementing Partners and the project team on field-level implementation of program activities and required follow-up.
  •  Provide Implementing Partners with technical guidance and capacity strengthening on monitoring, data management, and MERL systems.
  •  Manage and update MERL information and data in project management systems such as SAP and PMERL.
  •  Provide accurate Nepali-English translation and consecutive interpretation as required during field visits, meetings, and stakeholder coordination.

Any other tasks as assigned by line manager in accordance to organizational mandate and priority.

  • Ensures the full integration of Plan International’s global policies on Safeguarding Children, Program Participants, and Gender Equality and Inclusion (DEI) within their area of responsibility. This includes adherence to the policy principles, relevant Implementation Standards, and Guidelines. Key responsibilities involve ensuring that staff and associates are informed of and understand their obligations under these policies and Plan International’s Code of Conduct (CoC), their relevance to their specific roles, and that any concerns are promptly reported and managed in line with established procedures.

Technical expertise, skills and knowledge

The role requires the following technical expertise, knowledge and skills to deliver the above accountabilities,

Education qualification and experience

  • Master’s degree in Social Sciences with at least three years of professional experience in MERL, research and/or evaluation in the development sector or a Bachelor’s Degree with minimum five years of experience
  •  Practical experience in development projects in Madhesh Province.
  •  Practical experience in field-level project implementation with Implementing Partners.
  •  Practical experience in collecting and documenting photographs, participant stories, quotes, and other evidence of project results for reporting and communications.

Knowledge

  •  Practical knowledge of MOFA Japan donor compliance, including No Change, No Extension, Details, Visibility, Sustainability, and accountability for both results and implementation processes.
  •  Professional knowledge of results-based MERL and quantitative and qualitative research and evaluation methodologies is added advantage
  •  Knowledge of evidence-based project design and formulation, including the relationships between evidence, targeting, intervention design, results logic, indicators, and measurement approaches.

Skills

  • Ability to design and conduct Needs Assessments and Pilot measurement and evaluation and analyze quantitative and qualitative evidence.
  • Ability to translate evidence from Needs Assessments and Pilot Programs into project formulation, including targeting, intervention design, results logic, and indicators.
  • Ability to verify alignment between approved project details, actual implementation, and reported data, identify discrepancies, and ensure corrective follow-up.
  • Ability to combine quantitative data and qualitative evidence to clearly demonstrate project results and changes through reporting and strategic visibility.
  •  Ability to use MS Office and project management systems, including SAP and PMERL, for MERL data management and reporting.
  •  Written and verbal communication skills in English and Nepali, including the ability to provide accurate Nepali-English translation and consecutive interpretation as required..
  •  Ability to analyze expenditures, implementation, and results, assess cost-effectiveness and cost-efficiency, and translate findings into financial input for project design and budget formulation.
  •  Ability to use MS Office, including Excel, and project management systems for financial management, analysis, and reporting.
  •  Written and verbal communication skills in English and Nepali, including the ability to provide accurate Nepali-English translation and consecutive interpretation as required.

Plan International’s Values in Practice

We are open and accountable

We create a climate of trust inside and outside the organisation by being open, honest and transparent. We hold ourselves and others to account for the decisions we make and for our impact on others, while doing what we say we will do.

We strive for lasting impact

We strive to achieve significant and lasting impact on the lives of children and young people, and to secure equality for girls. We challenge ourselves to be bold, courageous, responsive, focused and innovative.

We work well together

We succeed by working effectively with others, inside and outside the organisation, including our sponsors and donors. We actively support our colleagues, helping them to achieve their goals. We come together to create and implement solutions in our teams, across Plan International, with children, girls, young people, communities and our partners.

We are inclusive and empowering

We respect all people, appreciate differences and challenge inequality in our programmes and our workplace. We support children, girls and young people to increase their confidence and to change their own lives. We empower our staff to give their best and develop their potential.

Physical Environment

This position is based in Regional Office- East, Dhanusha, with frequent travel to field as necessary

Level of contact with children

Equality, diversity and inclusion is at the very heart of everything that Plan International stands for.

We want Plan International to reflect the diversity of the communities we work with, offering equal opportunities to everyone regardless of age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, religion or belief, sex or sexual orientation.

Plan International is based on a culture of inclusivity and we strive to create a workplace environment that ensures every team, in every office, in every country, is rich in diverse people, thoughts, and ideas.

We foster an organisational culture that embraces our commitment to racial justice, gender equality, girls’ rights and inclusion.

Plan International believes that in a world where children face so many threats of harm, it is our duty to ensure that we, as an organisation, do everything we can to keep children safe. This means that we have particular responsibilities to children that we come into contact with and we must not contribute in any way to harming or placing children at risk.

As a global leader, CARE is shaping the future of the humanitarian and development sector. Each year, we deliver support and services to millions of people in over a hundred countries. We do this by focusing on our mission and living the values that drive our organization. A career at CARE is an opportunity to be part of a movement that brings communities together to solve complex problems and foster lasting change throughout the world. We seek individuals who are passionate about humanitarian and development work, collaborate well with others, embrace learning and innovation, and deliver results.

CARE has been operational in Nepal since 1978 and works in partnerships with government and non-government stakeholders across the spectrum of humanitarian action and long-term development programs. We create local solutions to poverty and inequality and seek dignity for everyone every day and during times of crisis. CARE puts women and girls at the center of everything we do because they have proven to be the best hope for creating lasting change in the world.

What it’s like to work at CARE?

CARE is a mission-driven international humanitarian aid and development organization that offers an opportunity to work with people across the world. Not a day will go by that you won’t learn something profound, meet an expert, or write a sentence that can change a life. We are committed to an environment where everyone can succeed.

The Bhotekoshi flash floods caused widespread damage and displacement across the affected districts of Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading, Gorkha, Tanahun, and Chitwan. The disaster severely disrupted shelter, livelihoods, WASH services, and access to essential services, while also increasing protection, gender, and social inclusion risks for affected communities.

CARE Nepal hereby invites qualified and motivated Nepalese candidates to join its Emergency Response and Recovery Programme to support disaster-affected communities across these districts. (Click on the links below for the more Job details):

Mission: Our mission is to improve the lives of individuals and families in the poorest, vulnerable, socially excluded and marginalised communities of Nepal.

PARTNERSHIP: Partner with local, Province and Central governments, Development Partner and civil society organisations for programme design, implementation and evaluation

LEARNING: Generate learning through applied research on relevant socio-economic, climate, disaster and environmental issues and utilise learning for advocacy and also utilize for organisational development

GOVERNANCE – Advocate and campaign at the local, province and national levels to address the root causes of development challenges

PHASE Nepal is a non-governmental, organization established in 2006 with a vision to build a self-empowered and self-sustained society where all kinds of discrimination are absent (please visit www.phasenepal.org for more information). PHASE Nepal’s health, education, livelihoods, research and strengthening the concept of independent living projects are currently running across various rural communities in Nepal.

We also implement various research projects in partnership with different universities from the UK and organizations from other Asian and African countries. Around 57 colleagues work with PHASE Nepal as full time staff and hundreds of volunteers help to accomplish our research and implementation activities. PHASE Nepal is currently looking for suitable candidates for the following positions for our future research projects.

Position: Qualitative and Quantitative Research Associates

Number of Positions: Few (we will keep the prospective candidates in a roaster and will contact as required)

Duty Station: Either PHASE Nepal central office Bhaktapur or field depending upon the requirement.

Duration: As per project requirements

Remuneration: Gross monthly salary of NRs 55000 (pro rata if for shorter durations) while working in Kathmandu and additional transportation, lodging and food allowances will be provided during the field work.

Key Responsibilities

  • Conduct quantitative and qualitative data collection as per approved research tools and guidelines.
  • Administer structured questionnaires, surveys, interviews, and other data collection tools.
  • Conduct Key Informant Interviews (KIIs), Focus Group Discussions (FGDs), and in-depth interviews (IDIs) where required.

Supply Chain Officer, Nepal Emergency Response (Consultant), Global Health

Location: Nepal

Project HOPE is an international NGO with more than 1,000 engaged employees and volunteers who work around the globe, responding to the world’s most pressing global health challenges. Throughout our 60-year legacy, Project HOPE has treated millions of patients, provided more than $3 billion worth of medicines to local health care organizations around the world helped build hundreds of health programs from the ground up, and responded to humanitarian crises worldwide.

Code of Conduct

It is our shared responsibility and obligation to treat each other with respect, take affirmative steps to prevent matters involving Sexual Exploitation & Abuse and Trafficking in Persons, and to disclose all potential and actual violations of our Code of Conduct, which may include Conflicts of Interest, Fraud, Corruption, Discrimination or Harassment. Together we can reinforce a culture of respect, integrity, accountability, and transparency.

Summary:

Project HOPE is seeking a WASH Technical Advisor to support its emergency response to landslides and flooding in Nepal. The consultant will provide technical guidance and support for the design, implementation, monitoring, and coordination of emergency WASH activities serving affected communities and supporting health delivery points.

The consultant will work closely with Project HOPE’s emergency response and program teams, local partners, government authorities, WASH Cluster actors, and other humanitarian organizations. The consultant will provide technical recommendations, monitor progress and water quality, support coordination, and identify and address challenges affecting WASH activities.

Scope of Consultancy

The consultant will provide services in the following areas:

  • Provide technical guidance on emergency WASH activities, including water supply, sanitation, hygiene promotion, water trucking, and water quality monitoring.
  • Support the design, implementation, and rehabilitation of water systems, as appropriate to the emergency context.
  • Monitor WASH activities and provide recommendations and mitigation measures to address implementation challenges.
  • Conduct and document water quality testing associated with water trucking, water distribution, and other relevant WASH activities.
  • Support the integration of WASH activities with health, gender, protection, nutrition, and other relevant humanitarian sectors.
  • Coordinate with government authorities, WASH Cluster actors, UN agencies, NGOs, local implementing partners, and other relevant stakeholders.
  • Provide technical input to WASH-related planning, procurement, budgeting, partner activities, monitoring, and reporting.
  • Participate in relevant coordination meetings and provide regular technical updates to the Emergency Response Team.
  • Support monitoring of WASH-related partner deliverables and identify and flag implementation, performance, or compliance concerns.
  • Provide technical input to internal and donor reporting related to WASH activities.

Expected Outputs

During the consultancy period, the consultant is expected to contribute and deliver the following:

  • Effective technical oversight and support for implementation of emergency WASH activities in Nepal.
  • Regular monitoring of WASH activities, including water trucking, water distribution, water quality testing, and hygiene-related interventions.
  • Timely identification of WASH-related challenges, with practical recommendations and mitigation measures provided to the Emergency Response Team.
  • Regular technical updates and reporting on WASH activities, progress, challenges, and priorities.
  • Effective coordination with government authorities, WASH Cluster actors, humanitarian organizations, local partners, and other relevant stakeholders.
  • Support technical input to WASH-related planning, procurement, budgeting, partner activities, and reporting.
  • Documentation of water quality testing and other relevant WASH monitoring data.
  • Technical recommendations to support quality, accountability, and alignment of WASH activities with applicable humanitarian standards, including Sphere standards.
  • Detailed deliverables, timelines, and performance expectations will be agreed upon with the consultant and documented as part of the consultancy engagement.

Duration of Assignment: Approximately 1 month

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Bachelor’s degree in water and sanitation engineering, civil engineering, or a related WASH technical field.
  • At least 5 years of experience designing and implementing emergency WASH programs, preferably in humanitarian, IDP, refugee, or migrant settings.
  • Experience with water supply systems, sanitation, hygiene promotion, water quality testing, and WASH activities in or around health facilities.
  • Experience working in emergency and early recovery contexts.
  • Knowledge of Sphere standards and humanitarian WASH practices.
  • Experience coordinating with government authorities, humanitarian organizations, partners, and WASH Cluster actors.
  • Experience with WASH monitoring, reporting, proposal development, and/or donor reporting.
  • Strong communication and coordination skills.
  • Experience working in Nepal or a similar humanitarian emergency context.
  • Experience integrating WASH with health, gender, protection, and other humanitarian sectors.
  • Experience working with local implementing partners and supporting WASH-related procurement and activity planning.
  • Fluency in Nepali and working proficiency in English are required.

The consultancy fee will be determined based on the scope of services, qualifications, and experience of the selected consultant.

Notice to applicants: Project HOPE does not conduct direct solicitation/recruitment via email. Project HOPE never asks consultant applicants for payment or financial information at any stage of the recruitment process. Project HOPE will never send you a third-party check and ask you to cash it. If you have been recruited via email, please contact Compliance@projecthope.org

Due to the substantial number of inquiries we receive, only applicants who meet the required qualifications and experience for this consultancy will be contacted. No phone calls please. However, since we are active around the world in the field of public health, we may wish to retain your CV in our database for other/future opportunities, unless you direct us otherwise.

Thank you very much for your interest in Project HOPE.

title.rendered: Culture and Arts Editor, Culture and Arts Reporter

content.rendered:
CULTURE AND ARTS EDITOR – 1

Kantipur Publications is looking for an ambitious and experienced editor to spearhead our coverage of arts & culture. This role will oversee our journalism spanning film, theatre, books, music, visual arts, literature, heritage, content creation, and creative industries—developing stories that examine how culture shapes Nepali society.

The Culture and Arts Editor will commission, edit and produce distinctive coverage across print and

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Lead and shape culture and arts coverage of The Kathmandu Post and Kantipur Daily across print and digital platforms
  • Commission, edit and develop features, profiles, interviews, criticism, reviews and reported stories from in-house and freelance journalists
  • Identify emerging cultural trends, important voices and underreported stories across Nepal
  • Build a strong network of writers, critics, artists, filmmakers, musicians, scholars and cultural practitioners
  •  Collaborate with photo, design, video and digital teams to develop visually compelling storytelling
  •  Maintain high editorial standards for accuracy, fairness, originality and critical independence
  •  Work with the wider editorial team to identify stories that connect culture and the arts to broader social, political and economic questions.

digital platforms, working closely with reporters, critics, freelance contributors, photographers and visual journalists. We are looking for an editor with strong editorial judgment, a deep understanding of Nepal’s cultural scene, and the ability to take the section beyond reviews and event coverage towards ambitious, original journalism. This is a player-coach role – you’ll manage a small team of reporters and are expected to do your own reporting and writing on a regular basis.

CULTURE & ARTS REPORTER – 1

Kantipur Publications is looking for a curious, energetic Culture and Arts Reporter to cover Nepal’s vibrant and evolving cultural scene for Kantipur and The Kathmandu Post. The reporter will cover film, music, books, theatre, visual arts, literature, heritage and creative industries, while developing original stories that go beyond routine event coverage.

WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR:

  • 1–2 years of journalism experience, preferably in culture and arts
  •  Strong writing and reporting skills in English or Nepali
  •  Genuine interest in Nepal’s cultural and creative landscape
  • Ability to find original stories, interview sources, and report independently

WHO YOU ARE

  • An experienced journalist or editor with at least 7 years of relevant experience, including meaningful experience editing or commissioning culture and arts journalism
  •  A strong writer and editor with excellent command of either English or Nepali language
  •  Deeply familiar with Nepal’s cultural and creative landscape and its major institutions, practitioners, debates and emerging trends
  •  Experienced in commissioning and developing original features, criticism and in-depth cultural journalism
  •  Possesses strong editorial judgment and the ability to distinguish meaningful cultural stories from routine event coverage
  •  Curiosity, initiative, and strong news judgment
  • Experience with multimedia or digital storytelling is an advantage

TO APPLY : By October 15, send:

  • Cover letter
  •  CV/resume
  • Two story ideas you would pursue in your first month
  • Three published work samples

Email: careers@kantipurmediagroup.com

Subject: Culture and Arts Reporter

HOW TO APPLY : To apply, please submit the following by October 15:

  • A cover letter explaining why you want this role and how you would strengthen the culture and arts coverage of Kantipur and The Kathmandu Post
  •  A full CV or resume
  •  Two story ideas you would pursue in your first three months and Three examples of your published work

Send your application to careers@kantipurmediagroup.com with the subject line: Culture and Arts Editor.

Source: Kantipur Dainik, 4 October, 2026

LACC Project is hiring an Office Secretary based at the LACC Project Support Unit (PSU) in Surkhet.

(Open for female candidates only)

NOTE:

Before submitting your job application, please read carefully all instructions and requirements that are provided in the job advertisement.

The application form and CV template to be used to apply for this position are provided at the end of this job advertisement. Applications and CVs that are done in any other formats or that are submitted through other channels, will not be considered in the recruitment.

The application period is open until 23.59 NPT on Saturday the 29th of October 2026. Late applications will not be considered.

Duty Station: Project Support Unit (PSU), Birendranagar, Surkhet

Recruitment: National. Preference to candidates who are from or based in Surkhet, no relocation or living allowances provided. (Open for local female candidates only)

Accountable to: Chief Technical Advisor / Deputy Team Leader / Chief Administrative & Financial Officer (CAFO)

Reporting to: Chief Administrative & Financial Officer (CAFO)

Job description:

The Local Adaptation to Climate Change (LACC) Project supports land use planning and management, integrated water and forest resources management, environmental conservation, climate change adaptation, and disaster risk reduction in Sudurpaschim and Karnali provinces. The Office Secretary plays a crucial role in ensuring efficient office operations by managing administrative tasks, documentation, and logistical support.

The Office Secretary is a long-term support position responsible for providing administrative, secretarial, and logistical assistance to the Project Support Unit (PSU). Key responsibilities include document management, preparation and administration of correspondence, translation between English and Nepali, management of incoming and outgoing letters, organisation of meetings, trainings, seminars, and workshops, and verification of related administrative and hotel documentation.

The position also supports procurement and logistical arrangements and ensures systematic filing, records management, and confidentiality of project information. The role contributes to the efficient day-to-day functioning of the PSU by maintaining organised administrative systems and supporting communication and coordination across project activities. As the majority of project documentation is managed electronically through Microsoft 365 and other digital platforms, fluent IT skills and proficiency in modern office applications are essential requirements for the position. Secretary will need to be able to type Nepali Unicode and have fluent English language skills.

This position offers an opportunity for young professionals to gain experience in office administration within an international development project while contributing to climate resilience efforts in Nepal.

Academic Qualifications: The candidate must have at least an Intermediate (10+2) qualification in Management, Administration, IT, or a related field. Preference will be given to those with a Bachelor’s degree.

Languages: Fluency in written and spoken Nepali and English. Must be able to type Nepali Unicode.

Experience and Skills:

  • Experience in office secretarial work, office management, and/or IT-related tasks, especially in donor-funded or international projects.
  • Candidate should have strong IT skills and proficiency in MS Office (Word, Excel, OneDrive, PowerPoint, Teams, Outlook) and internet use, along with excellent organizational, time management, and multitasking skills.
  • Strong communication and interpersonal abilities, the capacity to work both independently and in a team.
  • A high level of discretion and confidentiality are essential.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Administrative and Secretarial Support
  • Manage official correspondence, reports, and project documentation in both digital and hard-copy formats.
  • Draft letters, templates, routine correspondence, and administrative documents.
  • Translate documents, correspondence, and reports between Nepali and English.
  • Prepare meeting minutes, event reports, and incident reports as required.
  • Maintain filing, registration, archiving, and records management systems for incoming and outgoing correspondence and project documents.
  • Maintain and update the project library, including reports, guidelines, manuals, and reference materials.
  • Monitor staff timesheets and leave records, and follow up on timely submission and filing of supporting documentation.
  • Maintain records of staff leave, holidays, field visits, and field reports in coordination with CAFO.
  • Prepare and maintain framework contract documentation and related administrative records.
  • Provide day-to-day administrative and secretarial support to the CAFO and PSU team.

Logistics and Office Management

  • Arrange travel, accommodation, and logistical support for project staff, consultants, and visitors in coordination with the Operational Manager.
  • Serve as the primary reception and contact point for visitors, guests, and external stakeholders.
  • Provide administrative and logistical support for meetings, trainings, workshops, seminars, and other project events.
  • Coordinate office supplies, consumables, refreshments, drinking water, and other routine office requirements.
  • Maintain and update staff contact lists and internal administrative records.
  • Coordinate the production, issuance, and collection of staff identity cards, visiting cards, and project visibility materials.
  • Support the supervision and coordination of office support personnel, including office assistants, cleaners, and security staff, in coordination with the CAFO.
  • Follow up on operational invoices, vendor documentation, and administrative records related to office operations.
  • Maintain vendor databases, standing lists, and related procurement documentation in accordance with project procedures.

HR and Finance Support

  • Verify supporting documentation related to training events, workshops, seminars, hotel services, participant allowances, and other administrative expenditures before submission for processing.
  • Collect and organise invoices, receipts, attendance records, and supporting documents required for payment processing.
  • Check hotel quotations, venue rates, and service packages, and prepare price comparison documentation for approval.
  • Support the administration of staff medical, accident, vehicle, and asset insurance, including renewals and claims follow-up.
  • Assist in processing insurance claims, reimbursements, and other administrative payments.
  • Maintain records, summaries, and supporting documentation related to office operational expenditures.
  • Recommend properly supported expenditures to the Accountant for processing in accordance with established procedures.

Logistics Related Support

  • Obtain quotations and assess venue suitability, costs, and facilities for trainings, seminars, workshops, and meetings in close coordination with the Operational Manager.
  • Coordinate venue bookings and logistical arrangements, including accommodation, catering, and training packages.
  • Arrange and distribute training materials, stationery, participant certificates, and other event supplies.
  • Coordinate the collection of supplies and materials from the store and ensure timely availability for events.
  • Maintain attendance records and supporting documentation for training and workshop activities.
  • Provide on-site logistical support to ensure the smooth implementation of trainings, seminars, workshops, and meetings.

Other Responsibilities

  • Undertake additional tasks assigned by the management and project administration team to support project goals.
  • Maintain confidentiality in all aspects of work.

Any other tasks assigned by the Supervisor
